# OP-SL-005 — Communication & Documentation Systems
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-SL-005 |
| Title | Communication & Documentation Systems |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | SL — Service Logistics |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy defines requirements for communication and documentation systems that support the clinical and operational functions of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective communication systems are essential for care coordination, patient safety, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency.
## 2. Scope
All agency staff, the Operations Director, the IT Director/CISO, and the Administrator.
## 3. Policy Statements
3.1 The agency shall maintain reliable communication systems that enable: (a) real-time communication between office staff and field clinicians; (b) secure transmission of PHI in compliance with HIPAA; (c) after-hours contact per OP-SL-002; (d) emergency communication per OP-FM-005 and RM-EP-003.
3.2 The agency shall maintain an Electronic Health Record (EHR) system that meets all CMS, HIPAA, and state requirements per IT-SA-001.
3.3 All communication systems used for PHI must be encrypted and HIPAA-compliant per CO-HP-002 and IT-SC-003.
3.4 Staff shall not use personal, non-approved communication channels (personal email, personal text messaging, social media) to communicate PHI.
3.5 The agency shall maintain a backup communication plan in the event of primary system failure.
## 4. Procedures
### 4.1 Communication Systems Requirements

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.1.1 | Operations Director / IT Director | Maintain the following communication systems: (a) agency landline telephone system; (b) secure mobile communication (HIPAA-compliant messaging/calling); (c) secure email (encrypted); (d) after-hours answering service or automated routing system; (e) fax (encrypted/HIPAA-compliant); (f) electronic referral portal (if applicable). | Continuous. |
| 4.1.2 | IT Director | Ensure all communication systems meet HIPAA encryption and security requirements per CO-HP-002 and IT-SC-003. Conduct annual security assessment. | Annual assessment; continuous monitoring. |
| 4.1.3 | Operations Director | Establish and maintain a Communication System Directory (Appendix A) listing all agency communication systems, contact numbers, access procedures, and backup contacts. Distribute to all staff. | Maintained continuously; redistributed at any change. |

### 4.2 EHR System Requirements

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.2.1 | IT Director / Operations Director | Maintain the EHR system per IT-SA-001 including: (a) OASIS data entry and transmission capability; (b) plan of care documentation; (c) visit note documentation; (d) physician order management; (e) scheduling integration; (f) audit trail per CO-DC-001. | Continuous. |
| 4.2.2 | IT Director | Ensure all clinicians have mobile EHR access for point-of-care documentation, with secure login and device management per IT-UP-001. | Continuous. |
| 4.2.3 | Operations Director | Monitor EHR system uptime. If system downtime exceeds 2 hours during business hours, activate the downtime procedure (paper documentation backup per Appendix B). | Activated when downtime > 2 hours. |

### 4.3 Backup Communication Plan

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.3.1 | Operations Director / IT Director | Maintain a communication backup plan including: (a) backup phone numbers for all key staff; (b) alternative messaging platform; (c) paper documentation forms for EHR downtime; (d) manual scheduling board procedure. | Documented and tested annually. |
| 4.3.2 | IT Director | Test backup communication systems annually. Document test results and any gaps requiring remediation. | Annually. |

## 5. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Communication systems HIPAA-compliant | Annual security assessment | 100% |
| EHR system uptime | Monthly uptime tracking | ≥ 99.5% |
| Communication directory current | Semi-annual review | Current within 30 days |
| Backup plan tested annually | Test documentation | Annual test completed |

## Appendix B — EHR Downtime Procedures
CARE INDEED HOME HEALTH CARE, INC. EHR Downtime Procedures Policy Reference: OP-SL-005 | Version: 6.0
When EHR system is unavailable for more than 2 hours during business hours:
Notification: IT Director notifies Operations Director and all clinical staff of downtime and estimated recovery time.
Paper Documentation: Clinicians shall use the agency's standardized paper visit documentation forms (maintained in each clinician's supply bag and in the office).
Scheduling: Scheduling Coordinator maintains a manual scheduling board or spreadsheet for the duration of downtime.
Physician Orders: All verbal and new orders received during downtime shall be documented on paper order forms and entered into the EHR within 4 hours of system restoration.
OASIS: OASIS documentation delayed during downtime must be completed and transmitted within CMS-required timeframes from the assessment date (not the system restoration date).
Data Entry: All paper documentation must be entered into the EHR within 24 hours of system restoration.
Verification: Operations Director verifies all paper documentation has been entered within 48 hours of restoration.

# OP-SL-006 — Service Delivery During Public Health Emergencies
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-SL-006 |
| Title | Service Delivery During Public Health Emergencies |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | SL — Service Logistics |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy defines the clinical and operational protocols for maintaining home health services during declared public health emergencies including pandemics, infectious disease outbreaks, and other public health crises. This policy ensures continuity of patient care while protecting staff and patients per 42 CFR § 484.102 (Emergency Preparedness).
## 2. Scope
All agency staff, the Operations Director, the Director of Nursing/Clinical Manager, the Administrator, and the Governing Body.
## 3. Policy Statements
3.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain the ability to deliver essential home health services during public health emergencies, adapting service delivery methods as necessary while maintaining patient safety and regulatory compliance.
3.2 The agency shall prioritize patient care based on acuity, safety, and medical necessity during periods of reduced capacity.
3.3 Telehealth and remote monitoring may be utilized as adjuncts to in-person visits during public health emergencies when authorized by CMS and consistent with CL-SD-009.
3.4 Staff safety protocols, including PPE requirements, shall be enhanced during public health emergencies per RM-EP-001 and CL-SD-016.
3.5 The agency shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local public health orders during declared emergencies.
## 4. Procedures
### 4.1 Activation of Public Health Emergency Protocols

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.1.1 | Administrator | Monitor public health advisories from CDC, CMS, California DPH, and local health departments. Activate the agency's Public Health Emergency Protocol when: (a) a federal, state, or local public health emergency is declared; (b) a local infectious disease outbreak threatens staff or patient safety; (c) CMS issues emergency waivers or flexibilities. | Continuous monitoring; activation within 24 hours of triggering event. |
| 4.1.2 | Administrator | Convene the Emergency Management Team (Administrator, Director of Nursing, Operations Director, Compliance Officer) to assess the situation and develop the response plan. | Within 24 hours of activation. |
| 4.1.3 | Operations Director | Notify all staff of activation and distribute initial guidance including: (a) infection control precautions; (b) PPE requirements; (c) service delivery modifications; (d) reporting requirements. | Within 24 hours of activation. |

### 4.2 Patient Triage and Prioritization

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.2.1 | Director of Nursing | Categorize all active patients using the Patient Acuity Triage Tool (Appendix A): PRIORITY 1 — Critical (must receive in-person visits; life-threatening if service interrupted); PRIORITY 2 — High (requires in-person visits; significant risk if delayed > 48 hours); PRIORITY 3 — Moderate (may be served via telehealth with periodic in-person visits); PRIORITY 4 — Low (may be temporarily managed via telehealth only with monitoring). | Within 48 hours of activation. |
| 4.2.2 | Director of Nursing | Reassess patient prioritization weekly during the emergency. Adjust categories as patient conditions change. | Weekly. |
| 4.2.3 | Operations Director | Adjust scheduling to ensure Priority 1 and 2 patients receive all required in-person visits. Coordinate telehealth alternatives for Priority 3 and 4 patients. | Within 72 hours of triage completion. |

### 4.3 Service Delivery Modifications

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.3.1 | Director of Nursing | Implement enhanced infection control protocols per RM-EP-001 and CL-SD-016 including: (a) PPE requirements for all visits; (b) pre-visit screening of patients for symptoms; (c) post-visit decontamination procedures; (d) staff health monitoring. | At activation. |
| 4.3.2 | Director of Nursing | Authorize telehealth visits per CL-SD-009 for eligible patients when CMS waivers permit. Document the clinical rationale for telehealth substitution. | When CMS authorization available. |
| 4.3.3 | Operations Director | Implement geographic zone assignments to minimize travel and cross-contamination risk. | At activation. |
| 4.3.4 | Operations Director | Increase supply inventory for PPE, hand sanitizer, and infection control supplies. Coordinate with vendors per OP-SL-004. | At activation; weekly supply assessment. |

### 4.4 Staff Safety and Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.4.1 | Operations Director / HR Director | Implement staff health screening including: (a) daily symptom screening before shifts; (b) exposure tracking; (c) quarantine/isolation protocols if staff are symptomatic or exposed. | At activation; daily during emergency. |
| 4.4.2 | Operations Director | Ensure adequate PPE supply for all field staff. No clinician shall be required to make a patient visit without appropriate PPE. | Continuous during emergency. |

### 4.5 Communication During Emergency

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.5.1 | Administrator | Provide daily (or as-needed) communications to all staff with status updates, policy changes, and safety reminders. | At least daily during active phase. |
| 4.5.2 | Operations Director | Notify all active patients and caregivers of service modifications per RM-EP-003. | Within 48 hours of activation. |
| 4.5.3 | Administrator | Report emergency response status to the Governing Body. If the emergency duration exceeds 30 days, convene a special Governing Body meeting to review the agency's response and resource adequacy. | Per GV-GB-001 §6.3.2. |

### 4.6 Deactivation and After-Action Review

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.6.1 | Administrator | Deactivate public health emergency protocols when the triggering conditions no longer exist and public health authorities confirm the emergency has ended. | When conditions warrant. |
| 4.6.2 | Emergency Management Team | Conduct an after-action review within 30 days of deactivation. Document: (a) what went well; (b) gaps identified; (c) corrective actions; (d) policy/procedure updates needed. Submit to QAPI and Governing Body. | Within 30 days of deactivation. |

## 5. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Emergency protocols activated within 24 hours of triggering event | Documentation review | 100% |
| Patient triage completed within 48 hours | Triage documentation | 100% |
| Priority 1 patients received all in-person visits | Visit compliance audit during emergency | 100% |
| After-action review completed within 30 days | AAR documentation | 100% |

# OP-SL-007 — Inclement Weather & Hazardous Conditions
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-SL-007 |
| Title | Inclement Weather & Hazardous Conditions |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | SL — Service Logistics |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy defines protocols for managing service delivery during inclement weather, natural disasters, hazardous road conditions, and other environmental hazards that may affect the safety of staff traveling to patient homes or the ability to deliver scheduled services.
## 2. Scope
All field staff, the Operations Director, the Director of Nursing/Clinical Manager, scheduling staff, and the Administrator.
## 3. Policy Statements
3.1 Patient safety and staff safety are equally important. No staff member shall be required to travel to a patient visit when road conditions, weather conditions, or environmental hazards present an unacceptable risk to personal safety.
3.2 The Operations Director shall make timely decisions regarding service modifications during hazardous conditions and communicate those decisions to all affected staff and patients.
3.3 Priority patients (defined as patients with acute, unstable, or life-sustaining care needs) shall receive continued service through modified arrangements whenever possible.
3.4 All service modifications due to weather or hazardous conditions shall be documented with the specific reason, the patients affected, and the rescheduling plan.
## 4. Procedures
### 4.1 Weather Monitoring and Decision Authority

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.1.1 | Operations Director | Monitor weather forecasts and road condition reports daily. When hazardous conditions are expected, make a proactive decision regarding service modifications before the start of the business day. | By 5:00 AM on affected day or as conditions develop. |
| 4.1.2 | Operations Director | Issue one of three operational status levels: LEVEL GREEN — Normal operations; LEVEL YELLOW — Modified operations (priority patients only; non-priority visits rescheduled); LEVEL RED — Suspended field operations (all visits suspended; emergency triage by phone only). | At the earliest time a determination can be made. |
| 4.1.3 | Operations Director | Notify all staff and patients of the operational status level via the agency's communication system. Document the notification. | Within 1 hour of status decision. |

### 4.2 Service Modification During Hazardous Conditions

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.2.1 | Director of Nursing / Scheduling | Under Level Yellow, identify priority patients who must receive in-person visits: (a) IV therapy patients; (b) wound vac patients; (c) patients on high-risk medications requiring monitoring; (d) patients with recent hospital discharge (< 48 hours); (e) patients identified as Priority 1 or 2 per OP-SL-006 triage. | Immediately upon Level Yellow activation. |
| 4.2.2 | Scheduling Coordinator | Reschedule all non-priority visits to the next available day. Notify patients and assigned clinicians. | Within 2 hours of status decision. |
| 4.2.3 | On-Call Clinician | Under Level Red, provide telephonic triage for all patient calls. If an in-person visit is deemed life-sustaining, coordinate with the Operations Director for safe dispatch. | During Level Red activation. |
| 4.2.4 | All Field Staff | Any staff member who encounters unsafe conditions en route to a visit may exercise professional judgment to turn back. Notify the scheduling coordinator immediately. The visit shall be rescheduled without penalty to the clinician. | At time of occurrence. |

### 4.3 Documentation and Rescheduling

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.3.1 | Scheduling Coordinator | Document all cancelled, delayed, or modified visits using the Inclement Weather Visit Log (Appendix A). | At time of modification. |
| 4.3.2 | Scheduling Coordinator | Reschedule all affected visits within 48 hours of return to normal operations. | Within 48 hours. |
| 4.3.3 | Operations Director | Review the impact of the event and report to the Administrator. If the event resulted in > 10 visits cancelled, include in the monthly report to QAPI. | Within 7 days. |

## 5. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Proactive weather decision made before business day start | Documentation review | 100% |
| Priority patients served during Level Yellow | Visit records | 100% |
| All cancelled visits rescheduled within 48 hours | Scheduling audit | ≥ 95% |
| Staff and patient notification documented | Communication records | 100% |

# OP-PA-001 — Patient Complaint & Grievance Resolution
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-PA-001 |
| Title | Patient Complaint & Grievance Resolution |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | PA — Patient Access & Experience |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 1 — Public |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy defines the process for receiving, documenting, investigating, and resolving patient complaints and grievances at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. per 42 CFR § 484.50(a)(3) which requires that patients be informed of and have access to a complaint process and that the agency investigate and resolve complaints.
## 2. Scope
All agency staff, the Operations Director, the Director of Nursing/Clinical Manager, the Administrator, the Compliance Officer, and the QAPI Coordinator.
## 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Complaint | Any expression of dissatisfaction by a patient, family member, caregiver, or patient representative regarding any aspect of care or services provided by the agency. |
| Grievance | A formal complaint that has been documented and requires investigation and formal resolution. All written complaints and any verbal complaint not resolved at the time of the initial contact are classified as grievances. |
| Complainant | The individual filing the complaint or grievance (patient, family member, caregiver, or authorized representative). |

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a formal complaint and grievance resolution process that is accessible to all patients and their representatives.
4.2 All patients shall be informed of their right to file complaints at the time of admission and provided with: (a) the agency's internal complaint process; (b) the State Home Health Hotline number; (c) the CMS 1-800-MEDICARE number; (d) contact information for the California Department of Public Health.
4.3 No patient shall experience retaliation, reduction in services, or negative consequences for filing a complaint or grievance.
4.4 All complaints shall be acknowledged within 24 hours. All grievances shall be investigated and resolved within 30 calendar days. If resolution requires more than 30 days, the complainant shall receive written notification of the status and expected completion date.
4.5 Complaint and grievance data shall be trended, analyzed, and reported to QAPI quarterly per QA-SM-003.
## 5. Procedures
### 5.1 Complaint Receipt and Logging

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Any Staff Member | Upon receiving a complaint from any source, immediately document: (a) complainant name and contact; (b) patient name; (c) date and time; (d) nature of complaint; (e) desired resolution. Forward to the Operations Director. | At time of receipt. |
| 5.1.2 | Operations Director | Log the complaint in the Complaint & Grievance Tracking Log (Appendix A). Assign a unique tracking number. Classify as: (a) INFORMAL COMPLAINT — resolved at the point of initial contact; (b) FORMAL GRIEVANCE — requires investigation. | Within 4 hours of receipt. |
| 5.1.3 | Operations Director | Acknowledge receipt to the complainant: INFORMAL — verbal acknowledgment at the time of resolution; FORMAL — written acknowledgment within 24 hours (via mail, email, or hand-delivery). | Within 24 hours. |

### 5.2 Investigation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Operations Director (or designee) | Investigate all formal grievances. Investigation shall include: (a) review of the patient's clinical record; (b) interviews with involved staff; (c) review of relevant policies and procedures; (d) consultation with the Clinical Manager for clinical concerns; (e) consultation with the Compliance Officer for compliance concerns. | Investigation initiated within 72 hours; completed within 21 calendar days. |
| 5.2.2 | Operations Director | Document investigation findings on the Complaint Investigation & Resolution Form (Appendix B). | Upon completion of investigation. |
| 5.2.3 | Operations Director | If the investigation reveals a substantiated clinical concern, notify the Clinical Manager and initiate corrective action per applicable policies. If the investigation reveals potential compliance violation, notify the Compliance Officer per CO-CP-007. If the investigation reveals potential abuse, neglect, or exploitation, report per CL-PR-006. | Immediately upon identification. |

### 5.3 Resolution and Notification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | Operations Director | Determine the resolution. Options include: (a) corrective action with involved staff; (b) process improvement implementation; (c) additional staff training; (d) service modification; (e) formal apology; (f) finding unsubstantiated (with explanation). | Within 30 calendar days of initial complaint. |
| 5.3.2 | Operations Director | Notify the complainant of the resolution in writing. The notification shall include: (a) summary of the investigation; (b) findings; (c) actions taken; (d) right to escalate to the State Home Health Hotline or CMS if dissatisfied. | Within 30 calendar days; or written status update if investigation ongoing. |
| 5.3.3 | Operations Director | Close the complaint in the tracking log. Retain documentation for minimum 7 years per CO-HP-007. | Upon resolution notification. |

### 5.4 Trending and Reporting

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | Operations Director | Analyze complaint data monthly for: (a) volume trends; (b) common categories; (c) repeat complaints; (d) correlation with specific staff, services, or locations. | Monthly. |
| 5.4.2 | Operations Director | Report complaint/grievance trends to QAPI quarterly including: (a) total complaints received; (b) complaints by category; (c) average resolution time; (d) corrective actions implemented; (e) patient satisfaction impact. | Quarterly. |
| 5.4.3 | QAPI Coordinator | Integrate complaint data into the QAPI program for identification of systemic issues and performance improvement opportunities. | Quarterly. |

## 6. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All complaints logged within 4 hours | Tracking log audit | 100% |
| Written acknowledgment within 24 hours (formal) | Acknowledgment documentation | 100% |
| Investigation completed within 21 days | Tracking log audit | ≥ 95% |
| Resolution within 30 calendar days | Tracking log audit | ≥ 95% |
| Complainant notified of resolution in writing | Notification documentation | 100% |
| Quarterly QAPI report submitted | QAPI records | 100% |

# OP-PA-002 — Patient Identification & Verification
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-PA-002 |
| Title | Patient Identification & Verification |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | PA — Patient Access & Experience |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 1 — Public |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for verifying patient identity at each home health visit to prevent service delivery errors, medication errors, and misidentification. Patient identification is a National Patient Safety Goal (NPSG) and a fundamental requirement of safe healthcare delivery.
## 2. Policy Statements
2.1 All clinical staff shall verify the identity of the patient using at least two patient identifiers before providing any care, treatment, or services at each visit.
2.2 Acceptable identifiers include: (a) patient's full legal name; (b) date of birth; (c) medical record number; (d) home address. Room number, bed number, or physical location are NOT acceptable identifiers.
2.3 If identity cannot be verified, the clinician shall not proceed with care delivery until verification is achieved.
## 3. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1 | All Clinical Staff | At the start of each visit, ask the patient (or caregiver if patient cannot respond) to state their full name and date of birth. Compare responses to the patient record. | At each visit, before care delivery. |
| 3.2 | All Clinical Staff | Document patient identity verification in the visit note. | At each visit. |
| 3.3 | All Clinical Staff | If the patient or caregiver cannot verify identity, use alternative methods: (a) check identification documents; (b) verify against photograph (if available in record); (c) contact the agency office for verification. | At point of concern. |
| 3.4 | All Clinical Staff | If identity cannot be confirmed, do not deliver services. Notify the Clinical Manager immediately. Document the incident per RM-ER-002. | Immediately. |

## 4. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patient identification documented in visit notes | Quarterly chart audit (10% sample) | ≥ 98% |
| No service delivery errors due to misidentification | Incident report tracking | 0 events |

## 5. Cross-Referenced Policies

| Policy ID | Title | Relationship |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CL-SD-012 | Medication Management & Administration | Identification required before medication administration |
| RM-ER-002 | Incident Reporting & Investigation | Misidentification is a reportable incident |
| QA-AE-004 | Patient Safety Program | Patient identification as a safety goal |

## Appendix A — Patient Identification Quick Reference Card

If identity CANNOT be verified: 🚫 DO NOT deliver care 📞 CALL the agency office for verification 📝 DOCUMENT the incident and notify the Clinical Manager

# OP-PA-003 — Interpreter & Language Access Services
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-PA-003 |
| Title | Interpreter & Language Access Services |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | PA — Patient Access & Experience |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 1 — Public |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy defines standards for providing language access services to patients with limited English proficiency (LEP) at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. per Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, 42 CFR § 484.50 (Patient Rights), and CMS Guidance on Providing Language Access Services.
## 2. Policy Statements
2.1 The agency shall provide meaningful access to services for all patients regardless of their primary language.
2.2 At the time of intake and admission, the patient's preferred language shall be assessed and documented.
2.3 Qualified interpreter services (in-person, telephonic, or video) shall be provided at no cost to the patient during all clinical encounters, care coordination activities, and patient rights notification.
2.4 Family members, friends, and minor children shall NOT be used as interpreters for clinical communication unless the patient specifically requests it after being informed of the availability of free professional interpreter services, and the request is documented.
2.5 Key documents (patient rights, advance directive information, HIPAA notice, consent forms) shall be available in the prevalent languages of the agency's service area population.
## 3. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1 | Intake Coordinator | Assess and document the patient's preferred language during intake. If LEP is identified, document interpreter needs in the patient record and communicate to all assigned clinicians. | At intake. |
| 3.2 | Operations Director | Maintain a contract with a qualified telephonic or video interpreter service. Ensure service is available 24/7 for emergencies and during all business hours for routine care. | Continuous. |
| 3.3 | All Clinical Staff | For LEP patients, arrange interpreter services BEFORE the visit. Do not attempt to deliver clinical care, obtain consent, or provide patient education without qualified interpretation. | Before each visit with LEP patient. |
| 3.4 | All Clinical Staff | Document interpreter use in the visit note including: (a) language interpreted; (b) interpreter name and ID number; (c) method (in-person, phone, video). | At each visit using interpreter. |
| 3.5 | Operations Director | Track interpreter utilization monthly. Ensure available and timely service. Report utilization and any access issues to QAPI quarterly. | Monthly tracking; quarterly QAPI. |

## 4. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Preferred language documented for all patients | SOC chart audit | 100% |
| Interpreter services provided for all LEP patient visits | Quarterly audit | 100% |
| Interpreter use documented in visit notes | Chart audit | 100% |
| Key documents available in prevalent languages | Annual review | Compliant |

# OP-PA-004 — Cultural Competency in Service Delivery
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-PA-004 |
| Title | Cultural Competency in Service Delivery |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | PA — Patient Access & Experience |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Biennial |
| Access Tier | Tier 1 — Public |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for culturally sensitive and respectful service delivery across the diverse patient populations served by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Cultural competency is essential for effective patient communication, treatment adherence, patient satisfaction, and equitable care outcomes.
## 2. Policy Statements
2.1 All staff shall provide care and services with respect for the cultural, spiritual, and personal values, beliefs, and practices of each patient.
2.2 Cultural considerations shall be assessed as part of the comprehensive patient assessment at SOC and integrated into the plan of care.
2.3 The agency shall provide cultural competency training to all staff at orientation and annually thereafter per HR-TD-001.
2.4 The agency shall not impose cultural or religious practices on patients, and shall accommodate reasonable patient requests related to cultural or religious preferences in care delivery.
## 3. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1 | SOC Clinician | Assess cultural preferences during the comprehensive assessment including: (a) preferred language; (b) dietary preferences or restrictions; (c) religious/spiritual practices relevant to care; (d) cultural health beliefs or practices; (e) preferences regarding gender of caregiver; (f) family involvement preferences. Document in the patient record. | At SOC assessment. |
| 3.2 | All Clinical Staff | Incorporate documented cultural preferences into care delivery. If a cultural practice conflicts with a medical recommendation, discuss with the patient and document the discussion and patient's decision. | At each visit. |
| 3.3 | HR Director / Operations Director | Ensure cultural competency training is included in new employee orientation and annual mandatory training per HR-TD-001. | At hire; annually. |
| 3.4 | Operations Director | When feasible, match clinician-patient assignments considering language concordance and cultural familiarity. | At scheduling. |

## 4. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cultural assessment documented at SOC | Chart audit | ≥ 95% |
| Cultural competency training completed by all staff | Training records audit | 100% |
| No substantiated complaints of cultural insensitivity | Complaint tracking | 0 substantiated |

## Policy Header

| Subdomain | PA — Patient Access & Experience |

| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Biennial |
| Access Tier | Tier 1 — Public |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes protocols for respecting and safeguarding patient property and personal belongings during home health visits. Staff entering a patient's home are guests and must treat the patient's property with care and respect.
## 2. Policy Statements
2.1 All staff shall respect the patient's home, personal property, and belongings at all times during home health visits.
2.2 Staff shall not borrow, use, damage, or remove any patient property without explicit permission.
2.3 If patient property is accidentally damaged during a visit, the clinician shall immediately disclose the damage to the patient, document the incident, and report to the Operations Director.
2.4 Staff shall not accept gifts of significant monetary value (>$25) from patients. Small tokens of appreciation may be accepted with supervisory notification.
2.5 Any allegation of theft or intentional damage to patient property shall be reported to the Operations Director and Compliance Officer immediately and investigated per CO-CP-007.
## 3. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1 | All Clinical Staff | Upon entering the patient's home: (a) remove shoes if requested; (b) use provided supplies only (do not use patient's towels, utensils, etc. for agency purposes); (c) leave the environment as found; (d) properly dispose of any waste generated during the visit per RM-PS-002. | At every visit. |
| 3.2 | All Clinical Staff | If property is accidentally damaged, immediately: (a) inform the patient; (b) complete a Property Incident Report (Appendix A); (c) submit to Operations Director within 24 hours. | At time of incident. |
| 3.3 | Operations Director | Investigate all property damage or theft allegations. Coordinate with the Compliance Officer for theft allegations. Report findings to the Administrator. | Investigation within 7 days. |
| 3.4 | Administrator | Determine appropriate resolution for substantiated property damage claims including reimbursement or replacement. | Within 14 days of investigation completion. |

## 4. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No substantiated patient property complaints | Complaint tracking | 0 substantiated |
| All property incidents reported within 24 hours | Incident report tracking | 100% |

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for the operation and maintenance of the agency's physical office space, including workspace safety, access control, general maintenance, and administrative operations.
## 2. Policy Statements
2.1 The agency shall maintain its office facilities in a safe, clean, and professional condition that supports efficient operations and protects the confidentiality of patient information.
2.2 The agency office shall be accessible during posted business hours and have a clearly identified entrance for visitors, referral sources, and patients.
2.3 Patient records and PHI stored in the office (electronic or paper) shall be secured per CO-HP-001 and IT-SC-006.
2.4 The office shall be maintained in compliance with applicable fire safety, ADA accessibility, and OSHA workplace safety standards.
## 3. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1 | Operations Director | Maintain the office environment including: (a) regular cleaning schedule; (b) HVAC maintenance; (c) fire extinguisher inspection; (d) emergency exit signage; (e) first aid kit maintenance. | Continuous; inspections per schedule. |
| 3.2 | Operations Director | Post and maintain: (a) business hours; (b) agency licenses (California HCAI, Medicare certification); (c) patient rights information; (d) emergency exit maps; (e) required labor law posters. | Continuous. |
| 3.3 | Operations Director / IT Director | Ensure physical security of the office: (a) restricted access to records storage; (b) locked cabinets for paper PHI; (c) visitor sign-in log; (d) security system or monitoring during off-hours. | Continuous. |
| 3.4 | Operations Director | Conduct a facility safety inspection quarterly using the Facility Safety Inspection Checklist (Appendix A). Address any deficiencies within 30 days. | Quarterly. |

## 4. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quarterly facility inspection completed | Inspection checklist documentation | 100% |
| Required postings current | Visual inspection | 100% |
| PHI security measures in place | Annual HIPAA walkthrough | 100% |

## Policy Header

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for the operation and oversight of any branch offices or satellite locations operated by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Branch offices and sub-units must maintain the same standards of care, compliance, and documentation as the parent agency per 42 CFR § 484.105 and CMS enrollment requirements.
## 2. Policy Statements
2.1 Any branch office or satellite location operated by the agency shall be: (a) properly enrolled with CMS; (b) licensed by the California Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI) if required; (c) operated under the direct supervision of the parent agency's administration.
2.2 All policies applicable to the parent agency apply equally to all branch offices.
2.3 The parent agency shall maintain direct oversight of all clinical, operational, and compliance functions of branch offices.
2.4 Quality indicators and compliance metrics shall be monitored for each branch location separately and in aggregate.
## 3. Procedures

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1 | Administrator | Before establishing a branch office: (a) submit CMS-855A branch enrollment; (b) obtain state licensure if required; (c) establish staffing, space, and operational readiness. | Prior to opening. |
| 3.2 | Operations Director | Assign a branch coordinator or designee responsible for day-to-day operations of each branch location. The branch coordinator reports to the Operations Director. | At opening. |
| 3.3 | Operations Director | Conduct a site inspection of each branch office quarterly using the Facility Safety Inspection Checklist (OP-FM-001 Appendix A). | Quarterly. |
| 3.4 | Compliance Officer | Include all branch locations in the internal audit program per CO-RA-002. | Annually. |
| 3.5 | QAPI Coordinator | Monitor quality metrics for each branch separately. Report to QAPI and the Governing Body quarterly. | Quarterly. |
| 3.6 | Administrator | If the agency does not currently operate branch offices, document this status and maintain this policy as a reference for future expansion. | Current status documented. |

## 4. Compliance Monitoring

| Indicator | Method | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Branch CMS enrollment current | Annual verification | 100% |
| Branch inspections completed quarterly | Inspection records | 100% |
| Branch quality metrics reviewed quarterly | QAPI reports | 100% |

# OP-FM-003 — Vendor & Supplier Management
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-FM-003 |
| Title | Vendor & Supplier Management |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | FM — Facility & Administration |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2026-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |
| Classification Tier | ESSENTIAL |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 1 — Public |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for the selection, qualification, contracting, monitoring, and performance evaluation of vendors and suppliers providing goods, services, or contracted functions to Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective vendor management ensures the agency receives quality products and services, maintains regulatory compliance (including anti-kickback and Stark Law requirements per CO-FA-001), protects patient safety, controls costs, and satisfies applicable requirements of 42 CFR § 484.105 (Organization and Administration), 42 CFR § 484.100 (Compliance with Federal, State, and Local Laws), and OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies.
## 2. Scope
This policy applies to:
The Operations Director
The Administrator
The Compliance Officer
The CFO / Finance Director
All department heads or staff authorized to initiate vendor relationships or procurement
All current and prospective vendors, suppliers, and contracted service providers
This policy does not govern employment relationships (see HR-WM-002 for contractors and per diem staff) or Business Associate Agreements for HIPAA purposes (see CO-HP-005), though vendor qualification under this policy may be concurrent with BAA execution.
## 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Vendor | Any external individual, company, or organization that provides goods, services, or contracted functions to the agency in exchange for compensation. |
| Supplier | A vendor that provides physical products including medical supplies, equipment, office supplies, or technology hardware. |
| Contracted Service Provider | A vendor that provides professional or operational services including staffing agencies, interpreter services, answering services, IT managed services, consulting, or waste management. |
| Vendor Qualification | The process of evaluating a vendor's credentials, capabilities, compliance status, and suitability before entering into a business relationship. |
| Approved Vendor List (AVL) | The agency's maintained list of vendors that have been qualified, approved, and authorized for use. |
| Vendor Performance Evaluation | A periodic assessment of a vendor's adherence to contractual requirements, quality standards, timeliness, and regulatory compliance. |
| Exclusion Screening | Verification that a vendor (and its principals) does not appear on the OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE) or the System for Award Management (SAM) exclusion database. |

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an Approved Vendor List (AVL) of all vendors and suppliers authorized to provide goods or services to the agency.
4.2 No vendor shall be engaged, and no purchase order or contract shall be executed, until the vendor has been qualified through the agency's vendor qualification process, except for emergency procurements under Section 5.6.
4.3 All vendor relationships shall be documented through written contracts or purchase agreements that define: (a) scope of goods or services; (b) pricing and payment terms; (c) quality and performance standards; (d) compliance requirements; (e) termination provisions; (f) insurance and liability requirements; (g) Business Associate Agreement (if vendor will access PHI).
4.4 The agency shall not enter into any vendor relationship that could constitute a violation of the Anti-Kickback Statute or Stark Law. All vendor relationships involving referral sources, physicians, or healthcare entities shall be reviewed by the Compliance Officer before execution per CO-FA-001.
4.5 All vendors providing goods or services paid directly or indirectly by federal healthcare programs shall be screened against the OIG LEIE and SAM exclusion databases prior to engagement and monthly thereafter per HR-TA-003.
4.6 Vendor performance shall be evaluated at least annually. Vendors failing to meet performance standards shall be placed on corrective action or removed from the AVL.
4.7 The agency shall maintain vendor records for a minimum of 7 years per CO-HP-007.
## 5. Procedures
### 5.1 Vendor Identification and Selection

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Requesting Department Head | Identify the need for a vendor or supplier. Submit a Vendor Request Form (Appendix A) to the Operations Director including: (a) description of goods or services needed; (b) estimated annual spend; (c) any specific vendor candidates; (d) clinical or patient safety implications; (e) urgency level. | At time of identified need. |
| 5.1.2 | Operations Director | Review the request. If estimated annual spend exceeds $5,000, obtain at least 2 competitive quotes or proposals. If spend exceeds $25,000, obtain at least 3 competitive quotes and involve the CFO in evaluation. | Within 7 business days of request receipt. |
| 5.1.3 | Operations Director | Evaluate vendor candidates based on: (a) product/service quality; (b) pricing competitiveness; (c) references and reputation; (d) regulatory compliance history; (e) geographic service capability; (f) financial stability; (g) insurance coverage adequacy. | Within 14 business days. |
| 5.1.4 | Operations Director | Select the preferred vendor and proceed to qualification (Section 5.2). Document the selection rationale. | Upon completion of evaluation. |

### 5.2 Vendor Qualification

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Operations Director | Collect vendor qualification documentation using the Vendor Qualification Checklist (Appendix B): (a) W-9 or tax identification; (b) business license or registration; (c) professional licenses or certifications (if applicable); (d) certificate of insurance (general liability, professional liability, workers' compensation as applicable); (e) references (minimum 2 current clients); (f) compliance certifications or attestations; (g) product certifications or FDA registrations (for medical suppliers). | Within 14 business days of selection. |
| 5.2.2 | Compliance Officer | Perform exclusion screening: (a) verify vendor entity and principals against OIG LEIE; (b) verify against SAM exclusion database; (c) document results on the Vendor Qualification Checklist. If the vendor or any principal is excluded, the vendor shall not be engaged. | Within 7 business days of receiving vendor information. |
| 5.2.3 | Compliance Officer | For vendors involving referral sources, physicians, or healthcare entities: review the proposed relationship for Anti-Kickback and Stark Law compliance per CO-FA-001. Document the review and determination. | Within 14 business days; prior to contract execution. |
| 5.2.4 | Operations Director | If the vendor will access, create, receive, maintain, or transmit PHI, coordinate with the Compliance Officer to execute a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) per CO-HP-005 prior to any PHI access. | Prior to vendor access to PHI. |
| 5.2.5 | Operations Director | Upon successful qualification, add the vendor to the Approved Vendor List (Appendix C) with: (a) vendor name and contact; (b) goods/services provided; (c) contract effective date; (d) qualification date; (e) next review date; (f) exclusion screening dates. | Upon completion of qualification. |

### 5.3 Contract Execution

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | Operations Director / CFO | Execute a written contract or purchase agreement with all qualified vendors providing recurring goods or services exceeding $2,500 annually. The contract must include: (a) detailed scope of goods or services; (b) pricing, payment terms, and invoice requirements; (c) quality and performance standards; (d) compliance with all applicable laws and regulations; (e) requirement to notify agency of any exclusion, sanction, or material change; (f) right to audit records related to services provided; (g) termination provisions (for cause and without cause); (h) insurance requirements and indemnification; (i) confidentiality and PHI protection (BAA if applicable); (j) dispute resolution mechanism. | Prior to commencement of services. |
| 5.3.2 | Administrator | Approve all contracts with an annual value exceeding $25,000. Contracts exceeding $100,000 require Governing Body notification. | Prior to contract execution. |
| 5.3.3 | Operations Director | Maintain the original executed contract in the vendor file. Provide a copy to the CFO for financial tracking. | At time of execution. |

### 5.4 Ongoing Vendor Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | Compliance Officer | Screen all active vendors against the OIG LEIE and SAM exclusion databases monthly. Document screening results. If a vendor is found to be excluded, immediately notify the Operations Director and Administrator. Cease all transactions with the excluded vendor within 24 hours. | Monthly; immediate action upon exclusion finding. |
| 5.4.2 | Operations Director | Verify that all vendor insurance certificates remain current. Request updated certificates at least 30 days before expiration. Suspend services from any vendor with lapsed insurance. | 30 days before expiration; suspension upon lapse. |
| 5.4.3 | Operations Director / Requesting Department | Monitor vendor performance on an ongoing basis. Document any quality issues, delivery failures, compliance concerns, or service interruptions as they occur using the Vendor Performance Issue Log (Appendix D). | Continuous; documented at time of occurrence. |

### 5.5 Annual Vendor Performance Evaluation

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.5.1 | Operations Director | Conduct an annual performance evaluation for all vendors on the AVL using the Vendor Performance Evaluation Form (Appendix E). Evaluate: (a) quality of goods/services; (b) timeliness of delivery; (c) responsiveness to issues; (d) pricing competitiveness; (e) compliance and exclusion screening results; (f) insurance currency; (g) overall satisfaction. | Annually; within 60 days of contract anniversary or fiscal year end. |
| 5.5.2 | Operations Director | Assign a performance rating: SATISFACTORY — Vendor meets or exceeds expectations. Continue relationship. NEEDS IMPROVEMENT — Vendor has documented deficiencies. Issue a Vendor Corrective Action Notice (Appendix F) with a 30-day improvement timeline. UNSATISFACTORY — Vendor has critical or repeated deficiencies. Initiate vendor replacement and removal from the AVL. | At time of evaluation. |
| 5.5.3 | Operations Director | Report vendor performance evaluation results to the Administrator annually. Include recommendations for vendor changes, cost savings opportunities, or quality improvements. | Annually; within 30 days of evaluation completion. |

### 5.6 Emergency Procurement

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.6.1 | Operations Director | In emergency situations where immediate procurement is necessary to prevent harm to patients or ensure continuity of care, the Operations Director may authorize a single-source procurement without competitive bidding, provided: (a) the emergency is documented; (b) the vendor is screened against OIG/SAM before or within 24 hours of engagement; (c) the procurement amount does not exceed $10,000; (d) the Administrator is notified within 24 hours; (e) the vendor is subsequently qualified through the standard process within 30 days if the relationship will continue. | At time of emergency; follow-up qualification within 30 days. |
| 5.6.2 | Operations Director | Document the emergency procurement on the Emergency Procurement Authorization Form (Appendix G). | Within 24 hours of procurement. |

### 5.7 Vendor Termination

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.7.1 | Operations Director | Terminate vendor relationships when: (a) the vendor receives an UNSATISFACTORY performance rating and does not improve; (b) the vendor or its principals are found on the OIG/SAM exclusion list; (c) the vendor fails to maintain required insurance; (d) the vendor violates contract terms; (e) the vendor poses a risk to patient safety; (f) the agency no longer requires the vendor's goods or services. | Per contract termination provisions; immediate for exclusion or patient safety. |
| 5.7.2 | Operations Director | Document the termination reason. Notify the vendor in writing. Remove the vendor from the AVL. Ensure a replacement vendor is identified and qualified before termination if the goods/services are essential to operations. | Written notification per contract terms. |
| 5.7.3 | Operations Director | Retain terminated vendor records for minimum 7 years per CO-HP-007. | At time of termination. |

## 7. Compliance Monitoring
### 7.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All active vendors on AVL with completed qualification | Quarterly AVL audit | 100% |
| Monthly OIG/SAM exclusion screening completed | Monthly screening log review | 100% |
| All vendor insurance certificates current | Quarterly audit | 100% |
| Written contracts in place for vendors > $2,500 annual spend | Annual contract audit | 100% |
| Annual performance evaluation completed for all AVL vendors | Annual audit | 100% |
| Anti-kickback/Stark review completed for healthcare entity vendors | Compliance Officer records | 100% |
| BAA executed for all vendors accessing PHI | BAA tracking log | 100% |

### 7.2 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor engaged without qualification or exclusion screening | Federal program integrity risk; potential fraud liability; OIG sanction | Enforce AVL policy; no PO/payment without AVL status |
| Expired vendor insurance | Liability exposure for agency | Automated tracking with 30-day renewal reminders |
| No written contract for recurring vendor relationships | Unclear terms; no performance accountability; no audit rights | Require contracts for all vendors > $2,500 annually |
| Vendor exclusion not detected | Federal False Claims Act exposure; repayment liability | Monthly OIG/SAM screening with documented results |
| Referral-source vendor relationship not reviewed for AKS/Stark | Criminal and civil liability; program exclusion | Compliance Officer review required prior to contract execution |

## 10. Training Requirements
10.1 All staff authorized to initiate vendor relationships, procurement, or purchase orders shall receive training on this policy within 14 calendar days of hire or role assignment. Training shall cover: (a) vendor qualification requirements; (b) AVL policy and restrictions; (c) exclusion screening requirements; (d) anti-kickback and Stark Law awareness; (e) contract requirements; (f) emergency procurement procedures; (g) documentation requirements.
10.2 Annual refresher training shall be conducted for all staff with procurement authority and documented per HR-TD-001.
10.3 All staff completing this training shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix H) within 14 calendar days of training completion or policy revision.
## 11. Version Control
11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per EN-LC-001.
11.2 Only the most current approved version is valid. Superseded versions must be archived and marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."
11.3 Substantive revisions require: (a) Operations Director review and recommendation; (b) Administrator approval; (c) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days; (d) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.
11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections) may be approved by the Operations Director with notification to the Administrator.

# OP-FM-004 — Mail & Correspondence Management
## Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Policy ID | OP-FM-004 |
| Title | Mail & Correspondence Management |
| Domain | OP — Operations |
| Subdomain | FM — Facility & Administration |
| Version | 6.0 |
| Effective Date | 2025-07-10 |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2025-07-10 |
| Next Review Date | 2027-07-10 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version) |
| Classification Tier | GOOD TO HAVE |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Biennial |
| Access Tier | Tier 1 — Public |
| Policy Owner/Steward | Operations Director |

## 1. Purpose
This policy establishes standards for the receipt, processing, tracking, routing, and retention of all incoming and outgoing mail and official correspondence at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Proper mail management supports timely response to regulatory communications, physician orders, payer correspondence, patient communications, and legal documents. This policy ensures the agency meets documentation and communication requirements under 42 CFR § 484.105 (Organization and Administration) and HIPAA privacy requirements for handling correspondence containing Protected Health Information (PHI) per CO-HP-001.
## 2. Scope
This policy applies to:
All office staff responsible for mail handling
The Operations Director
The Administrator
The Compliance Officer (for regulatory and legal correspondence)
All department heads responsible for responding to correspondence within their functional area
This policy covers: (a) U.S. Postal Service mail; (b) courier/overnight deliveries (FedEx, UPS, etc.); (c) secure fax communications; (d) official agency correspondence sent externally. This policy does not govern electronic email (see OP-SL-005 and IT-UP-002) or clinical documentation transmission (see CL-CD-001).
## 3. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Official Correspondence | Any written communication sent or received by the agency in its official capacity including regulatory notices, legal documents, payer communications, physician communications, and patient correspondence. |
| Time-Sensitive Correspondence | Mail or correspondence requiring response or action within a defined deadline, including CMS survey notifications, legal notices, payer denial letters, and physician orders. |
| PHI-Containing Correspondence | Any mail or document that contains patient-identifiable health information subject to HIPAA privacy protections. |
| Mail Log | The agency's record of all incoming and outgoing official correspondence including date, sender/recipient, type, and routing. |
| Regulatory Correspondence | Communications from or to CMS, the Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC), California HCAI, the OIG, or any regulatory or accrediting body. |

## 4. Policy Statements
4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an organized system for receiving, logging, routing, and responding to all incoming mail and official correspondence.
4.2 All incoming mail shall be opened, sorted, logged, and routed to the appropriate department or individual on the day of receipt (or next business day if received on a weekend or holiday).
4.3 Time-sensitive correspondence shall be flagged, prioritized, and delivered to the responsible party immediately upon identification, with escalation if the responsible party is unavailable.
4.4 All correspondence containing PHI shall be handled, routed, and stored in compliance with HIPAA privacy requirements per CO-HP-001 and CO-HP-004.
4.5 All outgoing official correspondence shall be reviewed, approved, and documented before transmission.
4.6 The agency shall maintain a mail log for all incoming and outgoing official correspondence to support audit trails and regulatory compliance.
4.7 Fax communications containing PHI shall be transmitted only through the agency's secure fax system per OP-SL-005 and CO-HP-002.
## 5. Procedures
### 5.1 Incoming Mail Processing

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Designated Mail Handler | Collect all mail from the agency mailbox, courier deliveries, and secure fax queue each business day. | Daily by 10:00 AM. |
| 5.1.2 | Designated Mail Handler | Open and sort all incoming mail. Classify each item: (a) REGULATORY — from CMS, MAC, HCAI, OIG, accrediting body; (b) LEGAL — from attorneys, courts, law enforcement; (c) CLINICAL — physician orders, referrals, F2F documentation, lab results; (d) FINANCIAL — payer correspondence, EOBs, denial letters, payment notices; (e) PATIENT — patient correspondence, complaints, records requests; (f) GENERAL — office supplies, vendor communications, advertising. | At time of opening. |
| 5.1.3 | Designated Mail Handler | Log all incoming mail in the Incoming Mail Log (Appendix A). For each item, record: (a) date received; (b) sender name and organization; (c) classification; (d) brief description; (e) routed to (department/individual); (f) time-sensitive flag (yes/no); (g) response deadline (if identifiable). | At time of processing. |
| 5.1.4 | Designated Mail Handler | Flag and immediately deliver all time-sensitive correspondence to the responsible party: REGULATORY — Administrator and Compliance Officer immediately; LEGAL — Administrator immediately; Compliance Officer if compliance-related; CLINICAL (physician orders) — Clinical Manager / Intake immediately; FINANCIAL (denial letters with appeal deadlines) — CFO / Billing immediately. If the responsible party is unavailable, deliver to their designated backup. | Immediately upon identification. |
| 5.1.5 | Designated Mail Handler | Route all remaining correspondence to the appropriate department by end of the business day. Place in designated departmental mailboxes or deliver directly. | By end of business day. |
| 5.1.6 | Designated Mail Handler | Handle all PHI-containing correspondence in compliance with HIPAA: (a) do not leave PHI-containing mail unattended in open areas; (b) route directly to the responsible party in a sealed envelope or folder if hand-delivering; (c) log PHI-containing items with sufficient identifying information for tracking without exposing PHI in the mail log. | At all times. |

### 5.2 Time-Sensitive Correspondence Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.2.1 | Operations Director | Maintain a Time-Sensitive Correspondence Tracking Log (Appendix B) for all items requiring a response by a specific deadline. Track: (a) item description; (b) sender; (c) date received; (d) response deadline; (e) assigned to; (f) response date; (g) status. | Continuous; updated as items are received. |
| 5.2.2 | Operations Director | Review the Time-Sensitive Tracking Log weekly. Escalate any items within 7 days of their response deadline that have not been assigned or initiated. | Weekly. |
| 5.2.3 | Assigned Responsible Party | Respond to all time-sensitive correspondence within the required deadline. Document the response in the tracking log. | Per deadline. |
| 5.2.4 | Operations Director | If a response deadline will be missed, notify the Administrator immediately and document the reason. Implement expedited response. | Prior to deadline expiration. |

### 5.3 Outgoing Correspondence

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.3.1 | Originating Staff / Department | Prepare all outgoing official correspondence using agency letterhead. The correspondence must include: (a) agency name, address, and contact information; (b) date; (c) recipient name and address; (d) subject line; (e) body content; (f) signature of authorized representative; (g) enclosure notation if applicable. | At time of preparation. |
| 5.3.2 | Originating Staff / Department | Obtain required approval before sending: REGULATORY correspondence — Administrator and Compliance Officer approval; LEGAL correspondence — Administrator approval; coordinate with legal counsel per GV-EA-003; CLINICAL correspondence — Clinical Manager approval; FINANCIAL correspondence — CFO approval; GENERAL correspondence — Department Head approval. | Prior to sending. |
| 5.3.3 | Designated Mail Handler | Log all outgoing official correspondence in the Outgoing Mail Log (Appendix C). Record: (a) date sent; (b) recipient; (c) classification; (d) brief description; (e) method of delivery (USPS, courier, certified mail, fax); (f) tracking number (if applicable); (g) copy retained. | At time of sending. |
| 5.3.4 | Designated Mail Handler | For correspondence requiring proof of delivery (regulatory responses, legal notices, appeal submissions), use certified mail, return receipt requested, or courier with tracking and signature confirmation. | At time of sending. |
| 5.3.5 | Originating Staff / Department | Retain a copy of all outgoing correspondence in the appropriate departmental file and/or patient record as applicable. | At time of sending. |

### 5.4 Fax Management

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.4.1 | All Staff | Transmit faxes containing PHI only through the agency's secure HIPAA-compliant fax system per OP-SL-005 and CO-HP-002. | At all times. |
| 5.4.2 | All Staff | Use the agency's standard fax cover sheet (Appendix D) for all outgoing faxes. The cover sheet must include the HIPAA confidentiality notice. | For all outgoing faxes. |
| 5.4.3 | Designated Mail Handler | Retrieve incoming faxes from the secure fax queue at least 3 times per business day (morning, midday, end of day). Process per Section 5.1 procedures. | At least 3 times daily. |
| 5.4.4 | All Staff | Verify the recipient fax number before transmission. If a fax containing PHI is sent to the wrong number, immediately notify the Compliance Officer for breach assessment per CO-HP-003. | At time of sending; immediately upon error identification. |

### 5.5 Returned Mail and Undeliverable Correspondence

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.5.1 | Designated Mail Handler | When mail is returned as undeliverable, log the returned item and forward to the originating department. | At time of receipt. |
| 5.5.2 | Originating Department | Investigate the undeliverable mail. For patient correspondence: verify current address in the EHR, update as necessary, and re-send. For regulatory/legal correspondence: notify the Administrator and Compliance Officer immediately. | Within 2 business days; immediately for regulatory/legal. |

## 6. Documentation Requirements

| Requirement | Document / Record | Responsible Party | Location | Timeframe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Incoming mail log | Incoming Mail Log (Appendix A) | Designated Mail Handler | Operations file | Daily |
| Time-sensitive tracking | Time-Sensitive Correspondence Tracking Log (Appendix B) | Operations Director | Operations file | Continuous |
| Outgoing mail log | Outgoing Mail Log (Appendix C) | Designated Mail Handler | Operations file | At time of sending |
| Fax cover sheets | Standard fax cover sheet (Appendix D) | All Staff | Retained with correspondence | At time of fax |
| Copies of outgoing correspondence | Filed copies | Originating department | Departmental/patient files | At time of sending |
| Delivery confirmations | Certified mail receipts, courier tracking | Designated Mail Handler | Operations file | At time of receipt |

## 7. Compliance Monitoring

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All incoming mail logged on day of receipt | Weekly audit of mail log | ≥ 95% |
| Time-sensitive correspondence delivered immediately | Tracking log review | 100% |
| Time-sensitive responses completed by deadline | Tracking log review | ≥ 98% |
| PHI correspondence handled per HIPAA requirements | Quarterly audit | 100% |
| Outgoing regulatory/legal correspondence sent with proof of delivery | Quarterly audit | 100% |
| Fax cover sheet used for all outgoing faxes | Quarterly audit | 100% |

## 10. Training Requirements
10.1 All staff assigned mail handling responsibilities shall receive training on this policy within 14 calendar days of assignment. Training shall cover: (a) mail opening, sorting, and classification; (b) time-sensitive correspondence identification and escalation; (c) PHI handling requirements; (d) mail logging procedures; (e) fax management and HIPAA confidentiality notice requirements.
10.2 All staff shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix E) within 14 calendar days.
## 11. Version Control
Per EN-LC-001 standards. Only the current approved version is valid. Substantive revisions require Administrator approval and re-acknowledgment within 14 calendar days.
