CO-CP-004 — Code of Conduct & Ethics

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the Code of Conduct and Ethics ("Code") of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The Code defines the ethical standards, behavioral expectations, legal obligations, and prohibited conduct applicable to every individual who works for or on behalf of the agency. The Code is a foundational element of the Corporate Compliance Program (CO-CP-001) and reflects the agency's commitment to conducting all operations with honesty, integrity, and respect for patients, employees, referral partners, and payers.

3. Scope

This Code applies without exception to:

All Governing Body members

The Administrator and all senior leadership

All full-time, part-time, per diem, and contracted employees

All volunteers

All vendors, business associates, and contractors acting on behalf of the agency

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Every individual within the scope of this policy shall conduct themselves in accordance with the standards of this Code at all times, whether on or off agency premises, when representing the agency in any capacity.

4.2 Adherence to this Code is a condition of employment or contract with Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Violations are subject to disciplinary action up to and including termination or contract cancellation.

4.3 No one in a position of authority — including the Administrator or Governing Body members — may authorize conduct that violates this Code, applicable law, or regulation.

4.4 All workforce members have the affirmative obligation to report known or suspected violations of this Code through the mechanisms established in policy CO-CP-006.

4.5 No individual shall be retaliated against for good-faith reporting of a Code violation, per policy CO-CP-005.

5. Core Standards of Conduct

5.1 Patient-Centered Care and Dignity

All workforce members shall:

Treat every patient with dignity, respect, and compassion regardless of diagnosis, age, race, color, national origin, sex, disability, religion, or ability to pay.

Protect patient privacy and confidentiality at all times per policies CO-HP-001 and CO-HP-002.

Honor patient rights as defined in policy CL-PR-001.

Never exploit, abuse, neglect, or mistreat a patient. All suspected abuse, neglect, or exploitation shall be reported immediately per policies CL-PR-006 and HR-ER-009.

Provide only services that are ordered, medically necessary, and within their scope of practice.

5.2 Integrity in Billing and Documentation

All workforce members shall:

Document clinical services accurately, completely, and truthfully.

Never document services not actually rendered, alter clinical records to support billing, or fail to document care that was provided.

Never submit or participate in the submission of a false claim to Medicare, Medicaid, or any other payer.

Report suspected billing irregularities or documentation falsification through CO-CP-006.

5.3 Conflict of Interest

All workforce members shall:

Disclose any personal, financial, or professional interest that could conflict with the agency's interests or their professional obligations.

Never allow a conflict of interest to influence a patient care decision, business decision, or compliance determination.

Governing Body members shall comply with the full conflict of interest management requirements of policy GV-GB-003.

5.4 Gifts, Gratuities, and Kickbacks

All workforce members shall:

Never accept or offer gifts, meals, entertainment, or gratuities that exceed $25 per occurrence or $50 annually from any patient, vendor, referral source, or competitor.

Never offer, pay, solicit, or receive anything of value in exchange for patient referrals, in violation of the Anti-Kickback Statute (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b).

Report any solicitation of a kickback or improper referral arrangement immediately to the Compliance Officer.

5.5 Confidentiality and Privacy

All workforce members shall:

Never access, use, or disclose patient health information beyond the minimum necessary for their assigned duties.

Never discuss patient information in non-private settings (hallways, vehicles, social settings).

Never share login credentials, access patient records on behalf of another, or circumvent system access controls.

Report any known or suspected breach of patient information per policy CO-HP-003.

5.6 Workplace Respect and Anti-Harassment

All workforce members shall:

Treat colleagues, supervisors, and subordinates with respect and professionalism at all times.

Never engage in harassment, discrimination, or hostile conduct based on any protected characteristic.

Report harassment or discrimination per policy HR-ER-004.

5.7 Compliance with Laws and Regulations

All workforce members shall:

Comply with all applicable federal and state laws, regulations, and agency policies relevant to their role.

Never perform, authorize, or conceal any act that they know or reasonably believe violates applicable law.

Cooperate fully with all internal compliance audits and investigations.

5.8 Stewardship of Agency Resources

All workforce members shall:

Use agency resources (equipment, supplies, technology, time) only for legitimate agency business purposes.

Never misappropriate, steal, or misuse agency property.

Report waste, misuse, or misappropriation of agency resources through CO-CP-006.

5.9 Social Media and Public Communications

All workforce members shall:

Never post patient information, clinical photographs, or identifiable patient details on any social media platform.

Never make public statements that misrepresent the agency's services, credentials, or compliance status.

Comply with policy IT-UP-003 for all social media and public communications.

6. Reporting Violations

6.1 All workforce members have an affirmative obligation to report suspected violations of this Code, applicable law, or agency policy.

6.2 Reports may be made through any of the following mechanisms (per policy CO-CP-006):

Direct contact with the Compliance Officer

Agency compliance hotline (anonymous option available)

Direct contact with the Governing Body Chair (for matters involving the Compliance Officer or Administrator)

6.3 Reports may be made anonymously. Anonymous reports will be investigated to the extent practicable given the information provided.

6.4 No individual will be retaliated against for making a good-faith compliance report, per policy CO-CP-005.

7. Consequences of Violations

Discipline shall be applied consistently regardless of seniority, role, or tenure. The Administrator shall be notified of all Level 2 and Level 3 violations within 24 hours. The Governing Body shall be notified of all Level 3 violations within 24 hours.

8. Procedures — Acknowledgment and Distribution

9. Documentation Requirements

CO-CP-005 — Whistleblower Protection & Non-Retaliation

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the protections afforded to individuals who, in good faith, report suspected violations of law, regulation, agency policy, or the Code of Conduct (CO-CP-004), and prohibits retaliation of any kind against such individuals. Effective compliance programs depend on a workforce that feels safe reporting concerns. This policy provides the legal and operational framework for non-retaliation consistent with the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. § 3730), applicable California whistleblower statutes (California Labor Code § 1102.5), and OIG Compliance Program Guidance.

3. Scope

This policy applies to all workforce members of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., including Governing Body members, the Administrator, all employees, contractors, volunteers, and business associates. It applies to all reports of suspected violations, regardless of whether the report ultimately results in a finding of wrongdoing.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. strictly prohibits retaliation of any form against any individual who, in good faith, reports a suspected compliance violation, cooperates with a compliance investigation, or refuses to participate in conduct they reasonably believe violates law or agency policy.

4.2 Retaliation is defined broadly and includes but is not limited to: termination, demotion, suspension, reduction in hours or pay, reassignment, harassment, intimidation, exclusion from meetings, negative performance evaluations influenced by the report, or any other adverse employment or contractual action.

4.3 The protection of this policy applies to all good-faith reporters regardless of whether the reported concern is ultimately substantiated.

4.4 An individual who knowingly makes a false or malicious report with the intent to harm another individual or the agency is not protected by this policy and is subject to disciplinary action per CO-CP-004.

4.5 The Governing Body shall be directly notified of any alleged retaliation against a reporter within 24 hours of the allegation. The Compliance Officer may not serve as the sole investigator if they are the subject of the retaliation allegation.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 How to Make a Protected Report

6.2 Confidentiality of Reporter Identity

6.3 Non-Retaliation Enforcement

6.4 Workforce Communication of Rights

CO-CP-006 — Compliance Hotline & Reporting Mechanisms

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the multiple accessible mechanisms through which any workforce member, patient, family member, vendor, or business associate may report suspected compliance violations, fraud, waste, or abuse to Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The existence of accessible, well-publicized reporting mechanisms is a required element of the Corporate Compliance Program under OIG guidance. Effective reporting channels are essential to the agency's ability to detect, investigate, and correct compliance violations promptly.

3. Scope

This policy applies to all individuals who interact with Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. — including workforce members, patients, family members, vendors, business associates, and members of the public who have reason to report a compliance concern.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain multiple accessible reporting mechanisms at all times, including at minimum: a compliance hotline (with anonymous option), a direct email to the Compliance Officer, and a physical mailbox.

4.2 All reporting mechanisms shall be publicized to all workforce members at hire, in annual training, and through posted notices in accessible locations.

4.3 All reports received through any mechanism shall be logged, assigned a tracking number, and responded to within the timeframes established in this policy.

4.4 Anonymous reports shall be accepted and investigated to the extent practicable given the information provided. The agency shall not attempt to identify anonymous reporters.

4.5 No individual who makes a good-faith report through any mechanism shall be retaliated against, per policy CO-CP-005.

4.6 Reports involving the Compliance Officer shall be directed to the Governing Body Chair. Reports involving the Administrator shall be directed to the Compliance Officer and Governing Body Chair simultaneously.

CO-CP-007 — Compliance Investigation Process

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the standardized process for initiating, conducting, documenting, and closing compliance investigations at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A structured, consistent investigation process is essential to ensure that reported concerns are addressed promptly, that evidence is properly preserved and assessed, that confidentiality is maintained, that corrective action is implemented where warranted, and that the agency fulfills its obligations under the False Claims Act, OIG guidance, and applicable federal and state law.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All compliance investigations initiated under the reporting mechanisms of CO-CP-006

All self-identified compliance concerns identified through internal auditing (CO-RA-002)

All retaliation investigations under CO-CP-005

All investigations directed by the Governing Body

All investigations of potential fraud, waste, or abuse under CO-FA-003

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Every compliance report or self-identified concern shall be evaluated for investigation within 5 business days of receipt.

4.2 Formal investigations shall be initiated within 7 calendar days of receipt of a compliance report that, upon triage, warrants investigation.

4.3 All compliance investigations shall be documented in writing from initiation through closure.

4.4 All investigation records are confidential compliance documents. Access shall be restricted to the Compliance Officer, legal counsel (when engaged), and the Governing Body.

4.5 The Compliance Officer shall preserve investigation records under a litigation hold protocol if there is any indication that civil or criminal proceedings may arise from the subject matter.

4.6 The agency shall cooperate fully and promptly with any government investigation. All document requests or inquiries from government agencies shall be immediately routed to the Compliance Officer and legal counsel.

CO-CP-008 — Compliance Training & Education

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy mandates initial and ongoing compliance training and education for all workforce members of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective compliance training is a foundational element of the Corporate Compliance Program (CO-CP-001) and is required by OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies. Training ensures that all workforce members understand their individual compliance obligations, the agency's standards of conduct, applicable laws and regulations, reporting mechanisms, and the consequences of non-compliance.

3. Scope

This policy applies to all workforce members of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. including Governing Body members, the Administrator, all clinical and administrative employees, contractors, per diem staff, and volunteers. Role-specific training requirements are defined in Section 6.3.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 All workforce members shall complete compliance orientation training within 14 calendar days of hire or contract commencement.

4.2 All workforce members shall complete annual compliance refresher training within 30 calendar days of the start of each calendar year.

4.3 Completion of required compliance training is a condition of continued employment or contract. Failure to complete training within the required timeframe shall result in escalation per Section 6.5.

4.4 Training shall be delivered in a manner and language accessible to all workforce members. The agency shall provide interpreter assistance for workforce members with limited English proficiency upon request.

4.5 All training completions shall be documented with the workforce member's name, role, training module, completion date, and assessment score (if applicable).

CO-RA-001 — Regulatory Change Monitoring & Implementation

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy mandates the systematic monitoring of federal, state, and local regulatory changes affecting Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. and establishes a defined process for assessing the impact of regulatory changes on agency operations, policies, and training, and implementing required updates within defined timeframes. Regulatory non-compliance resulting from undetected regulatory changes constitutes a significant survey and financial risk. This policy ensures the agency maintains continuous compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, HIPAA, California home health regulations, OIG guidance, and all other applicable regulatory frameworks.

3. Scope

This policy applies to the Compliance Officer, Administrator, Director of Nursing, Revenue Cycle Director, HR Director, IT Director, and all department heads whose operational areas are subject to regulatory oversight.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a systematic regulatory monitoring program that tracks all regulatory changes affecting the agency's operations from CMS, OIG, DHHS, California HCAI, California DHCS, and other applicable bodies.

4.2 All identified regulatory changes with an effective date within 90 days shall be triaged for impact within 10 business days of identification.

4.3 Policy revisions required by regulatory changes shall be completed and approved within 30 calendar days of the regulatory change effective date, or earlier if the change imposes immediate compliance obligations.

4.4 Workforce notification and training on regulatory changes shall be completed within 30 calendar days of policy revision.

4.5 The Compliance Officer shall present a regulatory change summary to the Governing Body at each quarterly meeting.

CO-RA-002 — Internal Compliance Auditing Program

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the internal compliance auditing program of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Internal auditing is a required element of the Corporate Compliance Program (CO-CP-001) and provides the agency's primary mechanism for proactively identifying compliance deficiencies, billing errors, documentation gaps, and operational non-conformities before they result in government action, survey deficiencies, or financial penalties. This policy defines the scope, methodology, frequency, reporting, and corrective action requirements for all internal compliance audits.

3. Scope

This policy applies to all audit activities conducted by or on behalf of the Compliance Officer including billing audits, clinical documentation audits, OASIS accuracy audits, HIPAA compliance audits, exclusion screening audits, and policy acknowledgment audits. It does not govern external audits by CMS, OIG, or other regulatory bodies (see CO-RA-003).

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an active internal compliance auditing program with an annual risk-based audit work plan approved by the Compliance Committee.

4.2 All audit findings shall be documented in writing and reported to the Compliance Committee and Governing Body per the escalation standards of this policy.

4.3 All deficiencies identified through auditing shall be addressed through corrective action plans per policy QA-AE-003 within 14 calendar days of audit report finalization.

4.4 Corrective action effectiveness shall be validated through re-audit within 90 calendar days of CAP implementation.

4.5 All audit records are compliance documents and shall be maintained for a minimum of 7 years per policy CO-HP-007.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Annual Audit Work Plan

6.2 Audit Execution — Standard Protocol

6.3 Audit Types and Minimum Standards

6.4 Findings Reporting and Escalation

6.5 Corrective Action and Re-Audit

7. Documentation Requirements (COMPLETED)

8. Compliance Measurement

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Common Failure Points and Mitigation

9. References

10. Training Requirements

The Compliance Officer and all individuals who conduct or assist with internal compliance audits shall complete training on audit methodology, documentation standards, and regulatory requirements applicable to each audit area prior to conducting their first audit.

The Compliance Officer shall complete at minimum 8 hours of continuing compliance education annually, including audit-related content, with documentation retained in the compliance file.

All department heads whose areas are subject to audit shall receive orientation to the audit process, their responsibilities during an audit, and CAP development requirements within 30 calendar days of assuming their role.

Annual refresher training on the audit program shall be included in the compliance training curriculum per CO-CP-008.

11. Version Control

This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001. Only the most current approved version is valid. Any substantive revision requires: (a) Governing Body approval documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all applicable workforce members within 14 calendar days; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001. Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Compliance Officer with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

CO-RA-003 — External Audit & Survey Readiness

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the continuous survey readiness program of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Survey readiness is the state of operational preparedness in which the agency can demonstrate compliance with all applicable Conditions of Participation (42 CFR Part 484), state licensure requirements, and accreditation standards at any point in time — including unannounced CMS surveys. This policy ensures the agency maintains documented evidence of compliance, conducts mock surveys, prepares staff for surveyor interactions, and responds promptly and effectively to external audit and survey findings.

3. Scope

This policy applies to the Compliance Officer, Administrator, Director of Nursing, all department heads, all clinical and administrative staff who may interact with external surveyors, and all personnel responsible for maintaining documentation that may be reviewed during external audits or surveys.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain continuous survey readiness at all times. Survey readiness is not an event-driven activity; it is a continuous operational standard.

4.2 The agency shall conduct at minimum one comprehensive mock survey annually and one focused mock survey per quarter, targeting areas identified as high-risk through internal audit findings, OIG Work Plan priorities, or prior survey deficiencies.

4.3 All staff shall be trained on surveyor interaction protocols including: (a) greeting and badge verification; (b) immediate notification of the Administrator and Compliance Officer; (c) answering only questions within their scope of knowledge; (d) providing only requested documentation; (e) never volunteering information beyond the specific question asked.

4.4 All external survey findings shall be treated with the same urgency as internal audit findings. Plans of Correction shall be developed, implemented, and monitored within CMS-required timeframes.

4.5 The agency shall maintain a Survey Readiness Binder (physical and/or electronic) accessible at the main office at all times containing all documents surveyors are likely to request.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Survey Readiness Binder Maintenance

6.2 Mock Survey Program

6.3 Staff Survey Interaction Training

6.4 Response to External Survey Findings

6.5 Response to External Audits (MAC, ZPIC/UPIC, OIG, RAC)

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Measurement

9. References

10. Training Requirements

All workforce members shall receive survey interaction training during compliance orientation within 14 calendar days of hire per CO-CP-008.

All workforce members shall receive annual survey readiness refresher training.

The Administrator shall conduct at least one unannounced survey readiness drill annually.

The Compliance Officer shall receive training on CMS survey protocol (SOM Appendix B) within 30 calendar days of designation.

11. Version Control

Per EN-LC-001 standards. Only the most current approved version is valid. Substantive revision requires Governing Body approval and re-acknowledgment within 14 calendar days.

CO-RA-004 — Medicare Conditions of Participation Compliance

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy mandates continuous compliance with all applicable Medicare Conditions of Participation (CoP) for Home Health Agencies as codified in 42 CFR Part 484. Compliance with CoPs is the foundational legal requirement for Medicare certification and the agency's authority to provide and be reimbursed for home health services. This policy establishes the monitoring, accountability, and reporting framework that ensures every Condition and Standard is met at all times — not solely during survey periods.

3. Scope

This policy applies to the Governing Body, Administrator, Director of Nursing, Compliance Officer, all department heads, and all workforce members whose functions relate to any Condition of Participation.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain continuous compliance with all Conditions of Participation in 42 CFR Part 484 as a condition of Medicare certification.

4.2 The agency shall maintain a CoP Compliance Matrix (Appendix A) mapping each Condition and Standard to the responsible party, the implementing agency policy, and the monitoring mechanism.

4.3 The Compliance Officer shall conduct an annual CoP compliance assessment and present findings to the Governing Body at the Q1 quarterly meeting.

4.4 Any identified gap in CoP compliance shall be treated as a High-priority finding requiring corrective action within 14 calendar days per QA-AE-003.

4.5 The Governing Body shall receive a CoP compliance status report at each quarterly meeting as part of the compliance report per CO-CP-001.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.4 Regulatory Change Response

8. Compliance Measurement

9. References

10. Training Requirements

All department heads shall receive orientation to this policy and their CoP compliance responsibilities within 30 calendar days of assuming their role.

The Compliance Officer shall include CoP compliance awareness in the annual compliance training curriculum per CO-CP-008.

The Governing Body shall receive an annual CoP compliance briefing at the Q1 meeting.

CO-RA-007 — Sanctions & Enforcement Response

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the agency's response protocol for regulatory sanctions, citations, enforcement actions, civil money penalties, or other adverse regulatory actions imposed by CMS, OIG, state regulatory bodies, or accrediting organizations. Prompt, structured response to enforcement actions is essential to preserve the agency's Medicare certification, state licensure, and operational viability.

3. Scope

Applies to the Governing Body, Administrator, Compliance Officer, Director of Nursing, legal counsel, and all personnel involved in responding to enforcement actions.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Any regulatory sanction, citation, enforcement action, civil money penalty, or notice of termination received by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall be treated as the highest-priority agency matter requiring immediate executive response.

4.2 The Governing Body shall be notified within 24 hours of receipt of any enforcement action.

4.3 Legal counsel shall be engaged within 48 hours for any enforcement action that may affect Medicare certification, state licensure, or impose financial penalties exceeding $10,000.

4.4 The Compliance Officer shall maintain an Enforcement Action Response Log (Appendix A) documenting all enforcement actions, response activities, and outcomes.

4.5 All enforcement action response documentation is privileged and confidential.

CO-FA-001 — Anti-Kickback & Stark Law Compliance

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes safeguards to prevent violations of the federal Anti-Kickback Statute (AKS — 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b)) and the Physician Self-Referral Law (Stark Law — 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn). Both statutes prohibit certain financial arrangements between healthcare providers that could influence patient referrals for services reimbursed by federal healthcare programs. Violations carry severe civil, criminal, and exclusion penalties.

3. Scope

Applies to all Governing Body members, the Administrator, all employees, contractors, vendors, referral sources, and any individual or entity that provides, receives, or facilitates patient referrals to or from Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall not offer, pay, solicit, or receive any remuneration — directly or indirectly, in cash or in kind — to induce or reward patient referrals for services covered by Medicare, Medicaid, or any federal healthcare program.

4.2 The agency shall not enter into any financial arrangement with a referring physician or physician group that does not satisfy a recognized AKS safe harbor or Stark Law exception.

4.3 All referral source relationships shall be reviewed by the Compliance Officer for AKS/Stark compliance prior to formalization and at least annually thereafter.

4.4 All marketing and referral development activities shall comply with this policy and shall not involve: (a) payments or gifts to referral sources in exchange for referrals; (b) free or below-market-value services to referral sources; (c) entertainment or meals exceeding $25 per occurrence or $50 per year per referral source individual; (d) any arrangement where compensation varies based on the volume or value of referrals.

4.5 Any suspected AKS or Stark violation shall be reported immediately through CO-CP-006 and investigated per CO-CP-007.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Referral Relationship Review

6.2 Marketing and Referral Development Standards

6.3 Monitoring and Auditing

6.4 Suspected Violation Response

8. Compliance Measurement

CO-FA-002 — False Claims Act Awareness & Prevention

Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the agency's education and prevention program for compliance with the Federal False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729–3733), the California False Claims Act (California Government Code §§ 12650–12656), and the 60-day overpayment refund obligation under 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7k(d). The FCA imposes significant civil and criminal liability for knowingly submitting false or fraudulent claims to the federal government.

3. Scope

Applies to all workforce members, with particular emphasis on clinical staff who document services, billing staff who submit claims, and leadership who oversee operations.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall not knowingly present, or cause to be presented, a false or fraudulent claim for payment to Medicare, Medicaid, or any other federal or state healthcare program.

4.2 The agency shall not knowingly make, use, or cause to be made or used a false record or statement material to a false or fraudulent claim.

4.3 The agency shall identify and refund overpayments to CMS within 60 calendar days of identification, as required by 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7k(d).

4.4 All workforce members shall receive FCA education during orientation and annually per CO-CP-008.

4.5 The agency's whistleblower protections (CO-CP-005) apply to all FCA-related reports.

CO-HP-001 — HIPAA Privacy Program

Policy Header

2. Purpose

Establishes the agency's comprehensive HIPAA Privacy Program in compliance with the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164, Subparts A and E). The Privacy Program ensures the confidentiality of protected health information (PHI) while enabling appropriate use and disclosure for treatment, payment, and healthcare operations.

3. Scope

All workforce members, business associates, vendors, and any individual who creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI on behalf of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 The agency shall maintain a HIPAA Privacy Program that protects all PHI in any form (oral, written, electronic).

4.2 The Compliance Officer shall serve as the Privacy Officer (or designate a qualified individual).

4.3 The agency shall maintain a current Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP) and provide it to all patients at the start of care.

4.4 PHI shall be used and disclosed only as permitted by the HIPAA Privacy Rule, with the minimum necessary standard applied to all uses and disclosures.

4.5 Patient rights under HIPAA shall be honored including: access, amendment, accounting of disclosures, restrictions, and confidential communications.

4.6 All workforce members shall receive HIPAA privacy training at orientation and annually.

CO-HP-004 — Minimum Necessary Standard

Policy Header

2. Purpose

Defines the minimum necessary standard for PHI access, use, and disclosure per 45 CFR § 164.502(b) and § 164.514(d). The agency shall make reasonable efforts to limit PHI to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 The agency shall identify workforce members who need access to PHI and the categories/conditions of PHI each role requires.

4.2 For routine and recurring disclosures: standard protocols shall limit PHI to the minimum necessary.

4.3 For non-routine requests: individual review and approval by the Privacy Officer is required.

4.4 The minimum necessary standard does not apply to: (a) disclosures to or requests by a healthcare provider for treatment; (b) disclosures to the individual; (c) uses or disclosures authorized by the individual; (d) disclosures to HHS for compliance investigation; (e) uses or disclosures required by law.

2. Purpose

Mandates BAA execution, content requirements, and monitoring for all entities accessing PHI on the agency's behalf per 45 CFR § 164.502(e) and § 164.504(e).

4. Policy Statement

4.1 The agency shall not disclose PHI to any business associate without a current, executed BAA.

4.2 All BAAs shall contain the elements required by 45 CFR § 164.504(e)(2).

4.3 The Compliance Officer shall maintain a BAA Registry and conduct annual review of all BAAs.

4.4 Any business associate breach or non-compliance shall be addressed per the BAA terms and CO-HP-003.

Defines procedures for fulfilling patient requests to access, amend, or receive an accounting of disclosures of their health information per 45 CFR §§ 164.524, 164.526, and 164.528.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Patients have the right to access their PHI in a designated record set within 30 calendar days of request.

4.2 Patients have the right to request amendment of their PHI. The agency shall respond within 60 calendar days.

4.3 Patients have the right to receive an accounting of disclosures not for TPO within 60 calendar days.

CO-DC-001 — Assessment Audit Trail and Data Integrity

Policy Header

2. Purpose

Requires all assessment entries, modifications, and coding decisions to be captured in a timestamped, version-controlled audit trail to support data integrity, regulatory compliance, and fraud prevention.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 All clinical assessment entries and OASIS coding decisions shall be captured in a system-generated, immutable audit trail.

4.2 Every modification to an assessment after initial entry shall be documented with: original value, modified value, modifying user, timestamp, and reason for change.

4.3 No assessment data shall be deleted from the audit trail. Corrections shall follow CO-DC-003 standards.

4.4 The Compliance Officer shall have access to all audit trails for compliance monitoring purposes.

4. Policy Statement

CO-DC-003 — Late Entry, Correction & Amendment Standards

Policy Header

2. Purpose

Defines standards for late entries, error corrections, and amendments to clinical and administrative records to maintain documentation integrity and legal defensibility.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Original documentation shall never be deleted, obliterated, or rendered unreadable.

4.2 Late entries shall be clearly labeled as "LATE ENTRY" with the current date/time and the date of the event being documented.

4.3 Corrections shall use single-line strikethrough (for paper) or system correction function (for electronic), with the original entry preserved, the correction clearly marked, the correcting author identified, and the reason for correction documented.

4.4 Amendments shall be clearly labeled, reference the original entry, and include the amending author and date.

4.5 No correction or amendment shall be made under pressure from billing, coding, or administrative personnel to alter clinical findings.

CO-DC-004 — Clinical, Documentation, and Billing Alignment Audit

Policy Header

2. Purpose

Establishes a triangulation audit process verifying alignment between physician orders, visit delivery documentation, and billed claims. Misalignment among these three sources is a primary indicator of billing fraud, documentation falsification, or systemic operational failure.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 The agency shall conduct quarterly triangulation audits comparing: (a) physician orders (services ordered); (b) clinical visit documentation (services documented as delivered); (c) billed claims (services billed to payer).

4.2 All three sources must be aligned. Any mismatch constitutes a deficiency requiring investigation.

4.3 Variance types include: (a) services billed but not documented; (b) services documented but not ordered; (c) services ordered but not delivered; (d) coding discrepancies between documentation and billing.

# DOMAIN_ CL — Clinical Operations (6)



DOMAIN: CL — Clinical Operations

CL-CP-001 — Plan of Care Development & Approval

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for developing, approving, implementing, and maintaining an individualized plan of care (POC) for every patient admitted to home health services at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The plan of care is the foundational clinical document that authorizes, defines, and guides all services delivered to a patient during a certification period. It is simultaneously a clinical roadmap, a legal authorization for skilled services, and a billing instrument — any deficiency in its development, physician approval, or content directly compromises patient safety, regulatory compliance, and reimbursement integrity.

This policy ensures compliance with 42 CFR § 484.60 — Condition of Participation: Care Planning, Coordination, and Quality of Care, which mandates that a plan of care be established and periodically reviewed by a physician for every patient receiving home health services. It also ensures compliance with CMS PDGM episode management requirements, OASIS data collection obligations, and the agency's documentation and billing alignment standards.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All registered nurses (RNs) responsible for completing the comprehensive assessment and establishing the plan of care

All clinical disciplines contributing to the plan of care (PT, OT, SLP, MSW, HHA)

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

All intake and admissions staff who initiate the plan of care process

Physicians and allowed practitioners who review and approve plans of care

The Medical Records and Health Information staff

The Revenue Cycle team responsible for billing based on the approved plan of care

This policy applies at Start of Care (SOC), Resumption of Care (ROC), and Recertification (RECERT) for every patient served by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. It does not govern individual visit notes, which are governed by CL-CD-001, or OASIS-specific data collection requirements, which are governed by CL-OA-001 through CL-OA-019.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall establish a written, individualized plan of care for every patient admitted to home health services prior to or at the initiation of services, as required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a).

4.2 The plan of care shall be developed by the registered nurse responsible for the patient's care in collaboration with the patient, the patient's caregiver(s), the patient's attending physician or allowed practitioner, and all clinical disciplines involved in the patient's care.

4.3 No skilled home health services shall be provided to a patient without a physician-approved plan of care. Verbal orders for services may be initiated prior to written physician signature, provided the verbal order is received, documented, and authenticated in compliance with policy CL-CP-004 (Verbal Order Receipt & Authentication).

4.4 The plan of care shall be signed and dated by the physician or allowed practitioner before the agency submits a claim for Medicare home health services. For initial certification periods, the physician must sign the plan of care — which may be the OASIS-generated CMS-485 or equivalent — within the timeframe required by CMS.

4.5 The plan of care shall contain all elements required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a), as defined in Section 5 of this policy and detailed in Appendix A.

4.6 The plan of care shall be patient-centered, based on the findings of the comprehensive assessment (CL-CA-001), and shall reflect the patient's goals, functional limitations, and individual clinical needs.

4.7 No services shall be provided that are not authorized by the plan of care and a corresponding physician order. Any service not reflected in the current plan of care requires a new or amended physician order before the service is rendered, except in clinical emergencies where safety requires immediate action followed by immediate physician notification per CL-CP-003.

4.8 The plan of care shall be reviewed, revised, and recertified at least every 60 calendar days and whenever a significant change in the patient's condition warrants modification, per policy CL-CP-002.

4.9 The physician-approved plan of care, the OASIS assessment, the physician orders, and all visit documentation must be internally consistent. Discrepancies between these documents constitute documentation integrity failures governed by policy CO-DC-004.

4.10 Only the most current physician-approved version of a patient's plan of care shall be operative. Superseded plan versions shall be retained in the clinical record but clearly marked as no longer active.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Initiating the Plan of Care Process at Start of Care

6.2 Required Elements of the Plan of Care

The plan of care for each patient shall contain, at minimum, all of the following elements as required by 42 CFR § 484.60(a) and CMS billing requirements. Absence of any required element constitutes a documentation deficiency subject to correction per CO-DC-003.

6.3 Physician Approval Process

6.4 Multidisciplinary Coordination in Plan of Care Development

6.5 Patient and Caregiver Engagement in Plan of Care

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under the State Operations Manual (SOM) Appendix B will specifically verify under Tag G160 (42 CFR § 484.60):

Evidence that a plan of care exists for every patient. Surveyors will request clinical records and verify that a written, physician-approved plan of care exists for each active patient and for each certification period of sampled past patients. Missing plans of care or unsigned plans are Condition-level deficiency risks.

Evidence that the plan of care contains all required elements. Surveyors will review plans of care for completeness per 42 CFR § 484.60(a). Commonly cited deficiencies include: missing homebound status narrative, vague or unmeasurable goals, incomplete medication lists, and visit frequencies that do not match delivered services.

Evidence that the plan of care is patient-centered and individualized. Surveyors distinguish between plans that are genuinely tailored to the patient and plans that appear to be templated without individualization. Cookie-cutter goal language (e.g., "patient will improve") without patient-specific metrics is a common deficiency.

Evidence of physician approval. Surveyors will verify physician signatures on plans of care and cross-reference with service dates to confirm that signed plans of care predate or accompany the services billed. Surveys will also verify that the certifying physician is eligible (not employed by or financially related to the agency in a prohibited manner).

Evidence that the plan of care is consistent with services delivered. Surveyors will compare ordered visit frequencies against actual visit delivery records. Significant and unexplained variances are cited as documentation integrity failures and potential False Claims Act concerns.

Evidence of patient participation. Surveyors may interview patients and caregivers about their knowledge of their plan of care and whether they were involved in developing their goals.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 State Requirements

9.4 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 All registered nurses responsible for conducting SOC assessments and developing plans of care shall receive competency-validated training on plan of care development requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter. Training shall be conducted by the Director of Nursing or a qualified designee and shall include: (a) all required elements of the plan of care per 42 CFR § 484.60(a); (b) ICD-10 primary diagnosis selection for PDGM; (c) SMART goal-writing for home health; (d) physician order management and the verbal order process; (e) plan of care transmission and tracking; (f) common survey deficiencies and how to avoid them; (g) the agency's EHR plan of care workflow.

10.2 All other clinical disciplines (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) shall receive orientation to plan of care processes relevant to their discipline-specific contributions within 14 calendar days of hire, covering: (a) how to read and confirm the plan of care; (b) their obligation not to deliver services outside the plan of care; (c) how to initiate a discipline-specific order change request through the assigned RN.

10.3 All personnel within scope of this policy shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix B) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new hire/appointment.

10.4 The Director of Nursing shall verify training completion and competency for all RNs in plan of care development prior to their independently conducting SOC assessments. Competency shall be documented using the SOC Competency Assessment Tool (Appendix D).

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

CL-CP-002 — Plan of Care Review & Update

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy mandates the periodic review and update of every patient's plan of care throughout the episode of home health care, at each recertification period, and whenever a significant change in the patient's condition warrants modification. The plan of care is not a static document. It must be a living clinical instrument that evolves with the patient's condition, reflects the patient's current functional status and goals, and accurately represents the services being delivered at any point during the certification period. A plan of care that does not reflect the patient's current clinical reality fails its primary function as both a clinical guide and a billing authorization document, and constitutes a documentation compliance failure under 42 CFR § 484.60.

This policy ensures that plans of care at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. are reviewed at defined intervals, that clinical changes trigger prompt plan modifications with corresponding physician orders, and that the recertification process is completed within the regulatory timeline established by CMS.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All registered nurses managing active patient caseloads

All clinical disciplines (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) providing services under the plan of care

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

Clinical Coordinators responsible for recertification tracking

Physicians and allowed practitioners who review and sign updated plans of care

Medical Records and Revenue Cycle staff involved in episode management

This policy applies during every active certification period and at every recertification for all patients served by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 The plan of care for every active patient shall be formally reviewed by the responsible registered nurse at a minimum of every 30 calendar days during the certification period, regardless of whether a change is indicated.

4.2 The plan of care shall be comprehensively reviewed and updated at each recertification period — no later than every 60 calendar days — and the updated plan of care shall be transmitted to and signed by the certifying physician within the recertification timeline defined in policy CL-CP-008.

4.3 A plan of care modification shall be initiated within 24 hours whenever any of the following significant change conditions are identified: (a) a new diagnosis or significant worsening of an existing diagnosis; (b) a new medication, medication change, or medication discontinuation that affects the clinical picture; (c) a change in the patient's functional status that affects the type, frequency, or intensity of services needed; (d) a new physician order that adds, removes, or modifies any service; (e) a hospitalization, emergency department visit, or other inpatient event; (f) a patient or caregiver-reported change in condition or safety concern; (g) a fall or other adverse event; (h) a change in the patient's discharge goals or the clinical outlook for discharge.

4.4 All modifications to the plan of care shall be supported by a corresponding physician order. No change in service type, frequency, or discipline shall be implemented before a verbal or written physician order is obtained per policy CL-CP-003.

4.5 The updated and physician-approved plan of care shall be internally consistent with all OASIS data collected during the applicable assessment time point and with all visit documentation in the patient's clinical record.

4.6 The Director of Nursing shall conduct a supervisory review of all active patient plans of care no less than every 30 calendar days to identify cases where the plan of care is outdated, services do not match orders, or recertification is approaching without a completed assessment.

4.7 A LUPA (Low Utilization Payment Adjustment) risk review shall be integrated into the plan of care review process to identify patients at risk of not meeting the minimum visit threshold, per policy QA-PI-006.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Routine 30-Day Plan of Care Review

6.2 Mid-Episode Plan of Care Modification (Significant Change)

6.3 Recertification Plan of Care Review

6.4 Documentation of Discharge Planning Integration

6.5 LUPA Risk Monitoring Integration

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors will specifically examine:

Evidence that plans of care are reviewed at least every 60 days (and more frequently as indicated). Surveyors will check clinical records for documented reviews. A plan of care that is unchanged from SOC through a full 60-day episode without any documented review is a strong indicator of passive care management and will be cited.

Evidence that significant clinical changes prompt plan modifications. Surveyors will identify patients who had hospitalizations, significant medication changes, or new diagnoses during the episode and verify that the plan of care was updated. An unchanged plan following a clinical change is a common deficiency.

Evidence that all plan modifications are physician-ordered. Surveyors will cross-reference changes in service type or frequency between the original and current plan of care with the physician orders on file. Service changes without supporting orders are a False Claims Act risk and a CMS deficiency.

Evidence of recertification within the required window. Surveyors will request all OASIS assessments and cross-reference their dates with the certification period dates. Recertification assessments outside the Day 56–60 window are a documentation compliance failure and may affect billing.

Evidence that plans of care reflect the patient's actual current condition. Surveyors will compare the plan of care goals and functional status descriptions against visit notes from the same period. A plan describing a patient as "independent in ambulation" while visit notes document the patient as bed-bound is a documentation integrity failure.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 All registered nurses shall receive training on plan of care review requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter, including: (a) the criteria for significant change in condition; (b) the structured 30-day review process and required documentation; (c) the recertification assessment window and timeline; (d) the LUPA risk review process; (e) the EHR Plan of Care Review Note documentation standard.

10.2 The Director of Nursing shall receive training on supervisory review obligations, including the monthly caseload review process and escalation procedures, at hire and annually thereafter.

10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix A) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new appointment.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained per policy EN-LC-001. Only the most current approved version is valid. Superseded versions shall be archived as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.2 Substantive revisions require Governing Body approval documented in meeting minutes, re-acknowledgment by all in-scope personnel within 14 calendar days, and policy index update per EN-TG-001.

11.3 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with Governing Body notification at the next regular meeting.

CL-CP-003 — Physician Orders & Order Management

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for obtaining, documenting, managing, and authenticating all physician orders at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Every skilled home health service, treatment, medication, and clinical intervention delivered to a patient must be authorized by a valid, current physician order. The physician order is the legal authorization for clinical action — without it, services are not reimbursable under Medicare, are not defensible clinically, and may constitute unauthorized practice. This policy ensures that all physician orders are obtained before services are rendered (except in clinical emergencies followed immediately by physician notification), are properly documented in the clinical record, are authenticated within required timeframes, and are maintained in a manner that supports the clinical record's integrity, billing compliance, and survey defensibility.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All registered nurses and licensed vocational nurses receiving, transcribing, or documenting physician orders

All clinical disciplines (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) receiving discipline-specific orders

Physicians, nurse practitioners, clinical nurse specialists, and physician assistants issuing orders

Medical Records staff responsible for order management in the EHR

Clinical Coordinators managing physician order tracking

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

Revenue Cycle staff verifying order support for billed services

This policy does not govern OASIS assessment time points or recertification processes specifically (see CL-CA-004 and CL-CP-008), though all orders generated at those junctures fall under this policy.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 No skilled home health service shall be provided to any patient without a valid, current physician order authorizing that service. This requirement applies to all disciplines, all visit types, and all clinical interventions including medications, treatments, procedures, equipment, and supplies.

4.2 All physician orders shall be obtained from a physician, nurse practitioner, clinical nurse specialist, or physician assistant who is legally authorized to practice in California, who is not excluded from participation in federal healthcare programs, and who does not have a financial relationship with the agency that violates the Stark Law or Anti-Kickback Statute.

4.3 Written orders from the physician are the preferred format. Verbal orders are permissible when a written order cannot be obtained in advance of a clinical need, provided they are received and documented per policy CL-CP-004 and authenticated by the physician within the timeframes specified in Section 6.3.

4.4 All orders shall be specific, legible, dated, and signed (for written orders) or documented and authenticated (for verbal orders). Orders containing ambiguous language, missing elements, or requiring clinical interpretation shall not be executed without clarification from the ordering physician.

4.5 All orders in effect for a patient shall be current, consistent with the active plan of care, and reflected in the patient's medication and treatment lists. No order may be executed beyond its effective date or outside its specified scope without renewal or modification.

4.6 The agency shall maintain a complete and organized Order Management Record in each patient's clinical record, documenting every order received, the date received, the ordering physician, and the authentication status.

4.7 Physician orders and the services delivered under those orders must be in alignment. The Revenue Cycle team shall not bill for any service that is not supported by a dated, authenticated physician order on file, consistent with policy CO-DC-004.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Obtaining Physician Orders — General Requirements

6.2 Written Order Management

6.3 Verbal Order Authentication

6.4 Emergency Orders

6.5 Order Changes and Discontinuation

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

Surveyors will request clinical records and cross-reference every service in visit notes against the physician orders on file. They will specifically verify that verbal orders are authenticated and that no service was rendered outside the scope of an active order. Missing or unauthenticated orders linked to billed services are False Claims Act risk items and are commonly referred for further investigation.

8.3 Common Failure Points

10.1 All clinicians authorized to receive physician orders shall receive competency-validated training on order management requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter, including: (a) what constitutes a valid written vs. verbal order; (b) the elements required for a complete order; (c) the order clarification process for ambiguous orders; (d) the verbal order authentication requirement and timeline; (e) the EHR Order Management workflow; (f) consequences of executing services without orders.

10.2 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix A) within 14 calendar days of the effective date, any revision, or hire.

CL-CP-004 — Verbal Order Receipt & Authentication

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the protocols for receiving, reading back, documenting, and authenticating verbal orders (including telephone orders) at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Verbal orders are a necessary and accepted component of home health clinical practice, particularly in situations where a patient's clinical condition changes between visits and a written order cannot be obtained before a clinical action is needed. However, verbal orders carry significant risk of miscommunication, transcription error, and authentication failure — each of which can result in patient harm, documentation compliance failures, and billing integrity violations. This policy ensures that every verbal order is handled with a standardized, auditable protocol that protects patient safety, fulfills the California Nursing Practice Act requirements for verbal order management, and supports the agency's documentation integrity standards.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All registered nurses authorized to receive verbal orders from physicians and allowed practitioners

Licensed vocational nurses who receive verbal orders within their California BPC § 2859 scope limitations

All physicians, nurse practitioners, clinical nurse specialists, and physician assistants issuing verbal orders

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

Medical Records staff managing verbal order authentication in the EHR

Clinical Coordinators tracking pending verbal order authentications per CL-CP-009

Revenue Cycle staff who must confirm authentication before billing

This policy does not apply to orders received in fully written form at the time of issuance. It applies to any order — including plan of care modifications, medication changes, service additions or discontinuations, treatment orders, and discharge orders — that is communicated orally and requires transcription by the receiving clinician.

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Only a registered nurse (RN) or a licensed vocational nurse (LVN) acting within the scope of practice defined by California Business and Professions Code § 2725 (RN) and § 2859 (LVN) may receive and transcribe verbal orders at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. No other clinical discipline shall receive or transcribe verbal orders for clinical services requiring physician authorization.

4.2 All verbal orders shall be received using the standard Read-Back Protocol defined in Section 6.1 of this policy. A verbal order is not valid and shall not be documented as received until the read-back is completed and the ordering physician confirms the order as accurately transcribed.

4.3 Verbal orders shall be documented in the patient's Order Management Record in the EHR within 24 hours of receipt, or before the end of the clinical shift in which the order was received, whichever is sooner.

4.4 Every verbal order shall be authenticated — reviewed, confirmed, and signed by the ordering physician — within 7 calendar days of the verbal order being given. This requirement is mandatory and non-negotiable. Services rendered under an unauthenticated verbal order that has not been authenticated within 7 calendar days are not billable and are subject to overpayment assessment.

4.5 The agency shall maintain an active verbal order authentication tracking system per policy CL-CP-009 that identifies every pending verbal order, the date received, the authentication deadline, and the current status.

4.6 No verbal order shall be executed if the transcribing clinician has any doubt about the accuracy of the transcription, the clinical appropriateness of the order, or the identity of the ordering physician. In cases of doubt, the clinician shall contact the Director of Nursing before proceeding.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Verbal Order Receipt — Read-Back Protocol

6.2 Verbal Order Documentation in the EHR

6.3 Authentication Tracking and Follow-Up

6.4 LVN Limitations on Verbal Orders

6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

Surveyors will select patients with active verbal orders and examine whether: the read-back is documented, the order is entered within the required timeframe, and the physician signature is on file within the authentication period. They will also ask clinical staff to demonstrate their read-back process. An inability to describe the read-back process is a training deficiency citation under 42 CFR § 484.60.

Auditors from the MAC or OIG will specifically look for verbal orders on claims that have not been authenticated, as these constitute unsupported billed services.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.4 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 All RNs and LVNs shall receive competency-validated training on verbal order receipt and the read-back protocol within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter. Competency validation shall require demonstrated proficiency in the read-back protocol in a simulation or role-play format.

10.2 LVNs shall receive specific training on the scope limitations for verbal order receipt at hire and annually.

10.3 All personnel within scope shall acknowledge this policy within 14 calendar days of the effective date, any revision, or hire.

11. Version Control

Maintained per EN-LC-001. Substantive revisions require Governing Body approval. Non-substantive revisions approved by Administrator.

CL-CP-005 — Coordination of Care

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy mandates the coordination of services among all disciplines involved in a patient's care at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. and with external providers — including physicians, hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, pharmacies, community agencies, and other healthcare entities — involved in the patient's overall care. Coordination of care is not merely a documentation requirement; it is a clinical and ethical imperative that directly affects patient outcomes, patient safety, and the efficiency of care delivery. Fragmented care — where disciplines operate in silos, where the attending physician is not kept current on the patient's status, or where the home health team is unaware of care provided by other providers — creates clinical risk, medication errors, unnecessary hospitalizations, and documentation inconsistencies that threaten billing integrity. This policy ensures that Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. operates as a fully integrated member of the patient's care team at all times.

This policy implements the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.60(c) — Standard: Coordination of Care, which requires that the agency coordinates services provided and makes referrals to appropriate community resources.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All registered nurses managing patient care

All clinical disciplines (PT, OT, SLP, MSW) providing patient services

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Medical Social Worker (primary community resource coordination role)

Operations staff managing scheduling and visit logistics

The attending physician and referring providers

Intake and discharge planning staff

4. Policy Statement

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall ensure that all services provided to each patient are coordinated among all disciplines involved in the patient's care and with all external providers who contribute to the patient's overall health management.

4.2 The assigned registered nurse shall serve as the primary care coordinator for each patient, responsible for ensuring that all disciplines contributing to the patient's care are aware of the current plan of care, recent clinical changes, and the patient's progress toward goals.

4.3 Care coordination shall be documented in the patient's clinical record and shall include: (a) interdisciplinary communications regarding clinical status, plan changes, and goal progress; (b) communications with the attending physician, including all notifications of significant changes; (c) communications with external providers including hospitals, SNFs, pharmacies, and community agencies; (d) referrals to community resources.

4.4 The agency shall maintain ongoing, proactive communication with the patient's attending physician throughout the episode. At minimum, the physician shall be notified of: (a) any significant change in the patient's condition; (b) any new diagnosis identified during home health; (c) any medication concern or adverse reaction; (d) any patient safety risk identified during home assessment; (e) the patient's progress at recertification; (f) the patient's discharge status and estimated discharge date.

4.5 When a patient is transitioning from an inpatient setting to home health, the agency shall obtain and review all available discharge documentation, including discharge summaries, medication reconciliation records, and follow-up physician appointment schedules, to ensure continuity of the care plan.

4.6 The Medical Social Worker (MSW), when involved in a patient's care, shall serve as the primary coordinator for community resource referrals, support service linkage, and psychosocial needs coordination.

4.7 A formal interdisciplinary care coordination communication shall occur no later than 14 calendar days after SOC for any patient receiving three or more disciplines, and at any point when a significant change in condition occurs.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Internal Interdisciplinary Coordination

6.2 Physician Communication

6.3 Transition from Inpatient Setting

6.4 External Provider Coordination

6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors will examine care coordination documentation under Tag G160 (42 CFR § 484.60). They will interview patients and caregivers to assess whether the patient felt their care was coordinated and whether the patient knew who to contact with concerns. They will look for documented physician communications, care conferences, and community resource referrals. The absence of physician contact notes in a complex patient's clinical record is a commonly cited deficiency.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.4 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training & Acknowledgment Requirements

10.1 All clinical staff shall receive training on care coordination requirements within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter, covering: the 24-hour physician notification requirement; the care conference requirement; community resource referral documentation; and warm handoff procedures.

10.2 All personnel within scope shall acknowledge this policy within 14 calendar days of the effective date, revision, or hire.
