EN-TG-001 — Enterprise Policy Taxonomy & Classification Governance

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the authoritative policy taxonomy structure, domain classification system, naming conventions, subdomain architecture, and coding standards governing all policies within Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The enterprise policy taxonomy serves as the canonical framework for organizing, classifying, locating, and managing all agency policies. This policy ensures that the agency maintains a structured, consistent, and auditable policy inventory that supports regulatory compliance, survey readiness, operational efficiency, and IBM Knowledge Catalog governance artifact alignment. Without a governed taxonomy, policies become disorganized, duplicated, misclassified, or lost — creating direct risk to regulatory compliance and patient safety.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Compliance Officer (primary taxonomy steward)

The Administrator

All Domain Owners and Subdomain Owners as defined in the Enterprise Policy Taxonomy Framework v6.0

All personnel who develop, review, approve, classify, or publish agency policies

All departments that maintain policies within the enterprise framework

Any external consultants or contractors engaged in policy development or governance system implementation

This policy does not apply to clinical protocols, standing orders, or procedure-level documents unless those documents are elevated to policy status through the policy development process (GV-PM-001).

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a single, authoritative enterprise policy taxonomy that serves as the canonical classification system for all agency policies.

4.2 The taxonomy shall be organized in a three-level hierarchy: Domain → Subdomain → Policy, with each policy assigned a unique identifier following the format [XX]-[XX]-[NNN] where [XX] is a two-letter domain code, [XX] is a two-letter subdomain code, and [NNN] is a three-digit sequential number.

4.3 The Compliance Officer shall serve as the Enterprise Taxonomy Steward with sole authority to create, modify, merge, split, or retire domain codes, subdomain codes, and policy ID assignments.

4.4 No policy shall be published, distributed, or enforced unless it has been assigned a valid taxonomy classification and policy ID by the Enterprise Taxonomy Steward.

4.5 The taxonomy shall align with IBM Knowledge Catalog governance artifact standards including hierarchical namespace coding, artifact property completeness, and lifecycle status tracking.

4.6 Every policy within the taxonomy shall carry the following mandatory metadata fields: Policy ID, Title, Domain, Subdomain, Classification Tier (REQUIRED / ESSENTIAL / RECOMMENDED / GOOD TO HAVE), Access Tier (Tier 1–4), Status (ACTIVE / DRAFT / UNDER REVIEW / DEPRECATED), Review Cycle (Annual / Biennial / Triggered), and Policy Owner/Steward.

4.7 The Domain Code Dictionary and Subdomain Dictionary shall be maintained as controlled reference tables within the Enterprise Policy Taxonomy Framework document. Changes to these dictionaries require Compliance Officer approval and documentation in the Taxonomy Change Log (Appendix A).

4.8 Duplicate, overlapping, or redundant policies are prohibited. The Enterprise Taxonomy Steward shall conduct an annual redundancy audit and resolve any identified overlaps through merger, retirement, or scope clarification.

4.9 Only the most current approved version of this policy and the Enterprise Policy Taxonomy Framework shall be considered valid. Superseded versions must not be used for any operational or compliance purpose.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Taxonomy Structure Maintenance

6.2 Classification Tier Assignment

6.3 Access Tier Assignment

6.4 IBM Metadata Compliance

6.5 Naming Convention Standards

6.6 Annual Taxonomy Audit

6.7 Taxonomy Change Control

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring & Audit

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under SOM Appendix B will assess the agency's policy organization and accessibility:

Evidence that the agency maintains an organized, retrievable policy system. Surveyors expect to locate any requested policy quickly. A governed taxonomy ensures rapid retrieval.

Evidence that policies are current, properly identified, and version-controlled. Surveyors will check for version dates, approval signatures, and evidence that superseded versions are not in circulation.

Evidence that policies are accessible to staff who need them. The access tier system ensures appropriate visibility while maintaining confidentiality.

Evidence that the agency has a systematic approach to policy management. Surveyors view disorganized or inconsistent policy systems as indicators of broader operational issues.

Evidence that policy metadata supports regulatory cross-referencing. Surveyors may request policies by regulatory citation (e.g., "show me your policy for 42 CFR § 484.65"). A mapped taxonomy enables immediate retrieval.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 IBM Standards

9.4 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All personnel within scope of this policy (Section 3) shall receive training on the taxonomy structure, naming conventions, classification tier system, access tier system, and change request process within 14 calendar days of initial assignment to a policy development or governance role.

10.2 Annual refresher training shall be conducted for all Domain Owners and Subdomain Owners covering: (a) current taxonomy structure; (b) any changes since last training; (c) IBM metadata requirements; (d) Taxonomy Change Request process.

10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix D) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new assignment.

10.4 The Compliance Officer shall maintain a training completion log and report any non-compliance to the Administrator within 7 calendar days of the training deadline.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision requires: (a) review and approval by the Compliance Officer and Administrator; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the Enterprise Policy Taxonomy Framework and Master Policy Index.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Compliance Officer with notification to the Administrator. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.

EN-TG-002 — Regulatory Cross-Reference & Mapping

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy mandates the systematic mapping of all agency policies to applicable federal, state, and local regulatory requirements, accreditation standards, and industry guidelines. The regulatory cross-reference matrix ensures that: (a) every regulatory requirement is addressed by at least one agency policy; (b) every agency policy is linked to its authorizing regulatory basis; (c) gaps in regulatory coverage are identified and remediated; (d) regulatory changes are traceable to affected policies; and (e) CMS surveyors can rapidly identify the policy addressing any specific Condition of Participation or regulatory standard. Without a maintained cross-reference matrix, the agency cannot demonstrate systematic regulatory compliance and is at risk for survey deficiencies.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Compliance Officer (primary owner of the cross-reference matrix)

The Administrator

All Domain Owners responsible for policies that map to regulatory requirements

All personnel involved in regulatory change monitoring (per CO-RA-001)

All personnel responsible for policy development or revision (per GV-PM-001)

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a Regulatory Cross-Reference Matrix that maps every agency policy to its applicable regulatory requirements and maps every applicable regulatory requirement to the agency policy or policies that address it.

4.2 The cross-reference matrix shall cover, at minimum: (a) 42 CFR Part 484 — Home Health Agency Conditions of Participation; (b) HIPAA Privacy Rule, Security Rule, and Breach Notification Rule; (c) OSHA standards applicable to home health operations; (d) OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies; (e) CMS State Operations Manual interpretive guidelines; (f) applicable California state home health licensure requirements; (g) accreditation standards (if applicable).

4.3 The Compliance Officer shall update the cross-reference matrix within 30 calendar days of any: (a) new policy creation; (b) policy revision that changes regulatory scope; (c) policy retirement; (d) new or amended regulation affecting the agency; (e) new CMS interpretive guidance.

4.4 No regulatory gap — a regulatory requirement not addressed by any agency policy — shall remain unresolved for more than 60 calendar days from identification. A Regulatory Gap Remediation Plan (Appendix B) shall be initiated within 7 calendar days of gap identification.

4.5 The cross-reference matrix shall be presented to the Governing Body annually with a gap analysis report identifying: (a) any unaddressed regulatory requirements; (b) any policies without regulatory basis (candidates for retirement or reclassification); (c) changes since the last report.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

10. Training Requirements

10.2 Annual refresher training for Domain Owners covering any matrix changes, gap analysis results, and regulatory changes affecting their domain.

10.3 Policy acknowledgment (Appendix D) within 14 calendar days of effective date, revision, or new assignment.

EN-LC-001 — Policy Lifecycle Management & Version Control

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines the complete policy lifecycle from initial creation through review, revision, approval, distribution, archival, and retirement — with mandatory version control and change documentation at every stage. A governed lifecycle ensures that: (a) all policies are current, accurate, and reflect the latest regulatory requirements; (b) superseded versions are removed from circulation; (c) every change is traceable with full audit trail; (d) the agency can demonstrate during CMS surveys that a disciplined policy governance process exists; and (e) IBM Knowledge Catalog governance lifecycle standards (Draft → Active → Under Review → Deprecated) are met.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Compliance Officer (lifecycle process owner)

The Administrator

All Domain Owners and Subdomain Owners

All personnel who author, review, approve, publish, or manage agency policies

The Governing Body (for REQUIRED-tier policy approval)

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Every policy within Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall follow a defined lifecycle with the following stages: DRAFT → ACTIVE → UNDER REVIEW → (return to ACTIVE or advance to DEPRECATED).

4.2 Only policies with ACTIVE status may be used for operational, compliance, or regulatory purposes. DRAFT policies have no operational authority. UNDER REVIEW policies remain in force until the review cycle produces a revised ACTIVE version or a decision to deprecate. DEPRECATED policies are archived and may not be used.

4.3 Every policy shall be assigned a version number following semantic versioning: Major.Minor format (e.g., 1.0, 1.1, 2.0). Major version increments (1.0 → 2.0) indicate substantive content changes. Minor version increments (1.0 → 1.1) indicate non-substantive changes (formatting, typos, cross-reference updates).

4.4 Every version change shall be documented in a Version History Log (Appendix A) embedded within the policy document, recording: version number, date, author, change description, and approval authority.

4.5 Superseded versions shall be archived with a watermark or header stating "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE" and the date of supersession. Superseded versions shall be retained for a minimum of 7 years per CO-HP-007.

4.6 Only one version of any policy may carry ACTIVE status at any time.

4.7 The Compliance Officer shall maintain a Master Version Registry (Appendix B) documenting the current version number, effective date, and status of every policy in the enterprise taxonomy.

4.8 Distribution of new or revised policies shall be documented, and acknowledgment shall be obtained from all applicable personnel within 14 calendar days per GV-PM-003.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Policy Creation (DRAFT Stage)

6.2 Policy Review and Approval (DRAFT → ACTIVE)

6.3 Policy Distribution (Post-Approval)

6.4 Policy Review Cycle (ACTIVE → UNDER REVIEW → ACTIVE)

6.6 Version Control Standards

10.2 Annual refresher for Domain Owners covering overdue review escalation, version numbering standards, and any process changes.

10.3 Policy acknowledgment (Appendix E) within 14 calendar days.

EN-LC-002 — Policy Exception & Waiver Management

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the formal process for requesting, evaluating, approving, documenting, and time-limiting exceptions or waivers to established policies within Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Policy exceptions are sometimes operationally necessary due to unique circumstances, but uncontrolled exceptions create compliance risk, inconsistency, and audit exposure. This policy ensures that every exception is: (a) formally requested; (b) risk-assessed; (c) approved by appropriate authority; (d) documented with specific conditions and time limits; (e) tracked to expiration; and (f) reviewed for potential permanent policy amendment.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All agency staff, contractors, and leadership who seek an exception to any established agency policy

The Compliance Officer (exception process owner and approver for most exceptions)

The Administrator (approver for REQUIRED-tier exceptions not involving regulatory mandates)

The Governing Body (approver for exceptions to regulatory-mandated requirements — limited circumstances)

All Domain Owners who may receive exception requests within their domain

Critical limitation: No exception may be granted that would cause the agency to violate any federal or state law, regulation, CMS Condition of Participation, or HIPAA requirement. Regulatory mandates are not subject to waiver.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 No deviation from an established agency policy shall be practiced without a formally approved Policy Exception/Waiver. Informal, verbal, or undocumented exceptions are prohibited.

4.2 Every exception request shall be submitted in writing using the Policy Exception/Waiver Request Form (Appendix A) and routed to the Compliance Officer for evaluation.

4.3 No exception may be granted that would cause violation of any federal or state law, regulation, CMS Condition of Participation, HIPAA Privacy Rule, HIPAA Security Rule, OSHA standard, or state licensure requirement. Such requests shall be denied with written explanation.

4.4 Approval authority for exceptions is determined by the classification tier of the policy to which the exception applies:

4.5 Every approved exception shall specify: (a) the exact scope (who, what, where); (b) the conditions under which the exception applies; (c) the maximum duration (not to exceed 180 calendar days without re-evaluation); (d) mitigating controls to manage risk during the exception period; (e) the review/expiration date.

4.6 All approved exceptions shall be logged in the Policy Exception Register (Appendix B) and monitored for expiration.

4.7 Upon expiration, each exception shall be reviewed. The Compliance Officer shall determine: (a) the exception is no longer needed (close); (b) the exception should be renewed (requires new approval cycle); or (c) the underlying policy should be amended to permanently accommodate the condition (initiate triggered review per EN-LC-001__

4.8 The Compliance Officer shall report all active and expired exceptions to the Administrator quarterly and to the Governing Body annually.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Exception Request Submission

6.2 Exception Evaluation

6.3 Exception Approval

6.4 Exception Monitoring and Expiration

6.5 Reporting

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring & Audit

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Common Failure Points

9. References

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All supervisory and management staff shall receive training on the exception request process, including the prohibition against informal exceptions and the regulatory mandate exclusion.

10.2 The Compliance Officer and all Domain Owners shall receive training on the risk assessment methodology and approval authority matrix.

10.3 Policy acknowledgment (Appendix C) within 14 calendar days.

11. Version Control

Per EN-LC-001 standards.

EN-LC-003 — Policy Assignment and Role-Based Applicability Governance

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines the formal process for assigning policies to specific workforce roles, managing role-based applicability, and governing the reassignment of policies when roles change, policies are revised, or organizational structure evolves. Without governed policy assignment, staff may be unaware of policies that apply to them, may receive policies irrelevant to their role, or may miss critical compliance requirements. This policy ensures every employee, contractor, and governing body member knows exactly which policies apply to them and that assignment is traceable, documented, and enforced.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Compliance Officer (assignment process owner)

The Administrator

All Domain Owners and Subdomain Owners

HR Director (coordinates role-based assignment with onboarding and role changes)

All agency employees, contractors, per diem staff, and governing body members

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Every policy in the enterprise taxonomy shall have a defined applicability scope specifying which workforce roles, departments, or personnel categories are subject to that policy.

4.2 The Compliance Officer shall maintain a Policy-Role Assignment Matrix (Appendix A) that maps every policy to its applicable workforce roles.

4.3 Upon hire, role change, promotion, or transfer, the HR Director (in coordination with the Compliance Officer) shall ensure the employee receives and acknowledges all policies applicable to their new role within 14 calendar days.

4.4 When a policy is created, revised, or retired, the Compliance Officer shall review and update the Policy-Role Assignment Matrix to reflect any changes in applicability.

4.5 Access to policies shall be governed by the Access Tier system (EN-TG-001, Section C4). Staff shall have access only to policies within their authorized access tier and applicable to their role.

4.6 Contractors and per diem staff shall be assigned the same policy set as equivalent permanent employees in the same role, plus any contractor-specific policies (e.g., HR-WM-002__

4.7 The Compliance Officer shall conduct an annual Policy Assignment Audit (Appendix B) verifying that all personnel have acknowledged all policies applicable to their current role.

EN-LC-004 — Policy Retirement and Obsolescence Management

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines the formal criteria, process, and documentation requirements for retiring policies that are obsolete, superseded, no longer applicable, or redundant. Failure to retire outdated policies creates direct compliance risk: staff may follow superseded requirements, surveyors may encounter conflicting policies, and the agency's policy inventory loses credibility. This policy ensures that retirement is governed, documented, and that all downstream effects (cross-references, assignments, taxonomy, regulatory mapping) are addressed systematically.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Compliance Officer (retirement process owner)

The Administrator

All Domain Owners and Subdomain Owners

The Governing Body (for REQUIRED-tier policy retirements)

4. Policy Statements

4.1 A policy shall be retired when it meets one or more of the following criteria: (a) the regulatory requirement it addresses has been repealed or replaced; (b) the policy has been superseded by a new or revised policy; (c) the operational function the policy governs no longer exists; (d) the policy is redundant with another policy and has been merged; (e) the annual taxonomy audit identifies the policy as an orphan with no continuing purpose.

4.2 Policy retirement shall follow the formal retirement process described in this policy. Policies shall not be informally deleted, removed, or ignored.

4.3 Retirement of a REQUIRED-tier policy requires Governing Body approval. Retirement of ESSENTIAL-tier policies requires Administrator approval. Retirement of RECOMMENDED and GOOD TO HAVE policies requires Compliance Officer approval.

4.4 Upon retirement: (a) the policy's status shall be changed to DEPRECATED in the taxonomy and Master Version Registry; (b) the Policy ID shall be added to the Reserved ID Registry per EN-TG-001 (never reused); (c) the Regulatory Cross-Reference Matrix shall be updated per EN-TG-002; (d) the Policy-Role Assignment Matrix shall be updated per EN-LC-003; (e) all cross-references in other policies shall be updated; (f) the retired policy shall be archived with "DEPRECATED — NOT FOR USE" marking; (g) all personnel previously assigned the policy shall be notified.

4.5 Retired policies shall be retained in the archive for a minimum of 7 years per CO-HP-007.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.2 Retirement Evaluation

6.3 Retirement Approval

6.4 Retirement Execution

8.2 Common Failure Points

9. References

10. Training Requirements

This policy establishes standard metrics for measuring policy compliance across the enterprise, defines reporting formats and frequencies, sets escalation thresholds, and mandates a dashboard reporting structure that gives leadership real-time visibility into the health of the agency's policy governance system. Without defined metrics, the agency cannot objectively measure whether policies are being followed, acknowledged, reviewed on time, or effectively governing operations.

EN-CM-002 — Inter-Domain Policy Coordination & Conflict Resolution

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines the process for identifying and resolving conflicts, inconsistencies, overlaps, or gaps between policies across different domains within the enterprise taxonomy. In a 244-policy framework spanning 10 domains, cross-domain conflicts are inevitable without proactive coordination. Unresolved conflicts create contradictory requirements for staff, compliance confusion, and survey risk. This policy establishes a systematic identification process, a resolution methodology, an escalation hierarchy, and documentation requirements.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Compliance Officer (conflict resolution process owner and final arbitrator for most conflicts)

The Administrator (escalation authority)

All Domain Owners and Subdomain Owners

The Governing Body (final escalation for unresolvable conflicts)

4. Policy Statements

4.1 No two policies within the enterprise taxonomy shall contain contradictory requirements applicable to the same personnel, function, or process. Where conflicts are identified, they shall be resolved per this policy.

4.2 Inter-domain policy conflicts shall be identified through: (a) annual taxonomy audit (EN-TG-001); (b) policy review cycles (GV-PM-002); (c) new policy creation/revision (EN-LC-001); (d) staff or Domain Owner reports; (e) audit findings or survey observations.

4.3 The Compliance Officer shall maintain a Policy Conflict Register (Appendix A) documenting all identified conflicts, status, and resolution.

4.4 Resolution of inter-domain conflicts follows a defined hierarchy: (a) direct negotiation between affected Domain Owners; (b) Compliance Officer mediation; (c) Administrator decision; (d) Governing Body final resolution.

4.5 When policies from different domains contain overlapping but not contradictory requirements, the Compliance Officer shall determine whether the overlap should be: (a) maintained (each policy serves a distinct purpose despite overlap); (b) consolidated (merge into one policy per EN-LC-004/EN-TG-001); or (c) cross-referenced (each policy references the other to eliminate duplication).

4.6 Regulatory mandates always take precedence. If one policy reflects a regulatory requirement and a conflicting policy does not, the regulatory policy controls.

4.7 The Compliance Officer shall conduct an annual Inter-Domain Coordination Review and report results to the Administrator.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Conflict Identification

6.2 Conflict Resolution — Domain Owner Negotiation (Level 1)

6.3 Conflict Resolution — Compliance Officer Mediation (Level 2)

6.4 Conflict Resolution — Administrator Decision (Level 3)

6.5 Conflict Resolution Implementation

The agency has a systematic process for managing cross-domain policy relationships. Surveyors view a coordinated policy system as evidence of mature governance.

# FN-BC-001 — Medicare Billing & Claims Submission



FN-BC-001 — Medicare Billing & Claims Submission

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes standards for the accurate, timely, and compliant submission of Medicare claims for home health services provided by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Proper billing practices are a fundamental requirement of Medicare participation and a core component of the agency's corporate compliance program. Every claim submitted to Medicare must reflect only services that were actually rendered, are clinically supported by complete contemporaneous documentation, were physician-ordered, and meet all Medicare coverage requirements under 42 CFR Part 484 and the Patient-Driven Groupings Model (PDGM). Inaccurate or fraudulent billing exposes the agency to False Claims Act liability, Civil Monetary Penalties, Medicare exclusion, and criminal prosecution. This policy ensures the agency satisfies the requirements of 42 CFR Part 424 (Conditions for Medicare Payment), the CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual, and the OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

All billing coordinators and billing specialists

All certified coders performing diagnosis coding or PDGM classification

Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (for clinical documentation completeness and clinical billing correlation)

Compliance Officer (for audit, monitoring, and investigation functions)

Administrator

QAPI Coordinator (for billing quality metrics integration)

Any contracted billing service, clearinghouse, or third-party entity performing billing functions on behalf of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

This policy does not apply to:

Direct patient care delivery staff except to the extent that their documentation directly supports the billing process. Clinical documentation requirements supporting billing are governed by CL-CD-001 through CL-CD-004, CL-OA-001 through CL-OA-019, and CL-CA-001 through CL-CA-007.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall submit Medicare claims only for services that: (a) were actually and completely rendered by a qualified clinician; (b) are supported by complete, contemporaneous, authenticated clinical documentation in the medical record; (c) were ordered by an eligible physician or allowed practitioner through a signed Plan of Care; (d) meet all Medicare coverage criteria including homebound status, skilled care need, and medical necessity; and (e) are coded accurately per current ICD-10-CM guidelines and PDGM classification rules.

4.2 No claim shall be submitted for any service where the required physician certification, face-to-face encounter documentation, OASIS transmission acceptance, or clinical visit documentation is incomplete, expired, or not on file at the time of claim submission.

4.3 All claims shall be submitted within the CMS timely filing deadline (currently 12 months from the date of service) and shall comply with all HIPAA electronic transaction standards (837I institutional claim format).

4.4 The Revenue Cycle Director shall maintain a claims submission calendar, tracking log, and pre-billing verification system for all open episodes to prevent missed filing deadlines and ensure complete documentation support before any claim is released.

4.5 Any claim identified as potentially inaccurate, unsupported by documentation, or otherwise questionable shall be placed on billing hold immediately. Held claims shall not be submitted until the deficiency is resolved, documented, and cleared by the Revenue Cycle Director.

4.6 The agency shall never upcode, unbundle, duplicate bill, bill for services not rendered, or manipulate coding to maximize reimbursement beyond what documentation supports. Any such conduct constitutes grounds for immediate termination and referral to the Compliance Officer for investigation under policies CO-FA-003 and CO-CP-007.

4.7 All billing personnel shall complete initial and annual training on Medicare billing requirements, PDGM payment methodology, False Claims Act obligations, and agency billing policies, with documented competency validation, per policy CO-CP-008.

4.8 Claims submission processes shall be integrated with the agency's corporate compliance program (CO-CP-001), documentation audit program (CO-DC-002), and triangulation audit process (CO-DC-004) to ensure continuous alignment between clinical care delivery, clinical documentation, and billed claims.

4.9 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Superseded versions must not be used for any operational, billing, or compliance purpose. Any revision requires re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Pre-Billing Verification Process

6.1.1 Prior to submitting any final claim (Request for Final Payment) for any 30-day payment period, the Billing Coordinator shall complete the Pre-Billing Verification Checklist (Appendix A) and obtain Revenue Cycle Director sign-off.

6.1.2 The pre-billing verification shall confirm all of the following:

6.1.3 If any verification item cannot be confirmed as compliant, the claim shall be placed on billing hold immediately. The Revenue Cycle Director shall notify the Director of Nursing in writing within 24 hours of any clinical documentation deficiency preventing claim submission, and the Compliance Officer within 24 hours of any compliance-related hold.

6.1.4 Billing holds shall be logged in the Billing Hold Log (Appendix B) with: patient name, Medicare number, episode dates, hold date, hold reason, responsible party for resolution, expected resolution date, and actual resolution date.

6.1.5 Documentation of the completed Pre-Billing Verification Checklist shall be maintained in the agency's billing system or compliance file as an audit trail entry for each 30-day payment period, retained for a minimum of 7 years.

6.2 Claims Submission Process

6.3 Post-Submission Monitoring

6.4 Timely Filing Compliance

6.5 Billing Integrity Controls

6.6 Escalation Matrix

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors and MAC auditors reviewing the agency's billing practices will specifically verify:

Evidence that the agency has a billing quality control process. Surveyors will request evidence of pre-billing verification procedures. Agencies that cannot demonstrate a structured verification process risk Standard-level deficiency under 42 CFR § 484.100 (compliance with federal laws).

Evidence that billed services match clinical documentation. Auditors will compare billed claims to visit notes, Plan of Care orders, and OASIS assessments. Any mismatch between billed services and clinical documentation will be cited.

Evidence that physician certification is complete before billing. Auditors will verify that the signed 485 is on file and dated appropriately for each billed period.

Evidence that face-to-face encounter documentation supports billing. Auditors will review F2F documentation for completeness and validity.

Evidence that coding is supported by the medical record. OIG/RAC auditors will specifically test whether ICD-10 codes billed on claims match physician-documented diagnoses. Unsupported codes will result in overpayment demand.

Evidence that billing staff have received compliance training. Surveyors may request training records for billing personnel.

Evidence that billing concerns are reported and investigated. Compliance program auditors (OIG) will look for evidence of a functioning reporting system and investigation process.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 OIG Guidance

9.4 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All billing coordinators, coding personnel, and the Revenue Cycle Director shall complete initial training on this policy within 14 calendar days of hire or assignment to billing functions. Initial training shall be conducted by the Revenue Cycle Director or Compliance Officer and must cover: (a) Medicare home health billing requirements and PDGM payment methodology; (b) the pre-billing verification process and use of Appendix A; (c) claims submission procedures; (d) billing hold procedures; (e) timely filing requirements and escalation protocol; (f) prohibited billing practices; (g) False Claims Act liability and penalties; (h) the obligation and process for reporting billing concerns.

10.2 All billing personnel shall complete annual refresher training covering the topics above plus any CMS billing rule changes effective in the current year. Annual training shall include a competency assessment (minimum passing score: 80%).

10.3 All personnel within scope of this policy shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix D) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new hire/assignment.

10.4 The Revenue Cycle Director shall maintain a training tracking log documenting training dates, topics, competency scores, and acknowledgment dates for all billing personnel. Training non-compliance shall be reported to the CFO and HR Director within 7 calendar days of any deadline lapse.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, billing, or compliance purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision requires: (a) review by the CFO and Compliance Officer; (b) approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (c) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (d) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the CFO with notification to the Compliance Officer and the Governing Body at the next regular meeting. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.

FN-BC-002 — Claims Denial Management & Appeals

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes a systematic, comprehensive process for tracking, analyzing, categorizing, appealing, and preventing Medicare claims denials at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Unmanaged denials result in revenue loss, cash flow disruption, and undetected systemic billing or documentation deficiencies. Every denial — regardless of amount — must be investigated for root cause because even small denials may indicate patterns of non-compliance that, if uncorrected, constitute systemic billing errors or False Claims Act exposure. This policy ensures that every denial is reviewed within defined timeframes, appropriately appealed when meritorious, written off only when justified and authorized, and analyzed for root cause to drive continuous improvement through the agency's QAPI program.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

All billing coordinators and billing specialists

All certified coders

Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (for clinical denial review)

Compliance Officer (for denial pattern analysis and compliance correlation)

Administrator

QAPI Coordinator (for denial trending integration with quality program)

Any contracted billing service performing denial management functions

This policy does not apply to:

Non-Medicare denials from commercial payers or Medicare Advantage plans are managed using similar principles but may have different appeal timelines and processes. Revenue Cycle Director shall maintain payer-specific appeal protocols for non-Medicare payers.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a formal denial management program that tracks 100% of Medicare claim denials from initial receipt through final resolution (paid on appeal, written off with authorization, or all appeal levels exhausted).

4.2 Every denial shall be reviewed within 5 business days of receipt to determine: (a) the denial reason code and category; (b) whether the denial is technically or clinically valid; (c) whether the denial is appealable; (d) the appropriate level and strategy of appeal; (e) whether the denial reflects a systemic documentation, coding, or billing deficiency requiring broader corrective action.

4.3 All clinical denials (medical necessity, homebound status, documentation insufficiency, coverage criteria) shall be reviewed jointly by the Revenue Cycle Director and Director of Nursing before any appeal decision or write-off is authorized. The Director of Nursing's clinical assessment of appeal merit shall be documented.

4.4 The agency shall pursue all meritorious appeals through the full Medicare administrative appeals process. No claim with a legitimate clinical and documentation basis shall be written off without exhausting at least the Redetermination (Level 1) level of appeal.

4.5 No clinical denial shall be written off without the countersignature of the CFO and a written rationale documenting why the denial is valid or why appeal would be non-meritorious. The Write-Off Authorization Form (Appendix C) is required.

4.6 Denial trending data shall be reported to the CFO monthly, included in the quarterly compliance report to the Governing Body per GV-GB-001 §6.2.3, and integrated with QAPI performance monitoring per QA-PI-002.

4.7 Any single denial category accounting for more than 3% of total claims submitted in any 90-day period shall trigger a formal root cause analysis and corrective action plan within 30 calendar days per QA-AE-002 and QA-AE-003.

4.8 The Revenue Cycle Director shall maintain current knowledge of all Medicare appeal deadlines, appeal level requirements, and amount-in-controversy thresholds, updated annually.

4.9 ADR (Additional Documentation Request) responses shall be treated as the highest priority billing activity. All ADR deadlines shall be tracked on a separate ADR log with escalation protocol.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Denial Receipt and Logging

6.2 Denial Classification

6.2.1 The Revenue Cycle Director shall classify each denial within 3 business days of logging using the following standardized category system:

6.3 Appeal Merit Assessment

6.4 Medicare Administrative Appeals Process

6.4.1 Level 1 — Redetermination (MAC)

6.4.2 Level 2 — Reconsideration (QIC)

6.4.3 Level 3 — ALJ Hearing (OMHA)

6.4.4 Levels 4 and 5

Level 4 (Medicare Appeals Council) and Level 5 (Federal District Court) shall be pursued only upon written authorization from both the CFO and Administrator, with legal counsel engagement required. The decision to proceed to Level 4 or 5 shall be reported to the Governing Body.

6.5 ADR Response Protocol

6.6 Denial Trending and Root Cause Analysis

6.7 Escalation Matrix

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor and Auditor Expectations

MAC/RAC auditors will request documentation supporting denied and overturned claims. Agencies must demonstrate a functioning denial management process with tracking, appeals, and trending.

OIG compliance auditors expect evidence that denial patterns are analyzed for systemic root causes and that the agency has a corrective action process. Agencies that simply accept denials without investigation risk a finding of inadequate compliance program.

CMS surveyors reviewing 42 CFR § 484.100 (compliance with federal laws) will look for evidence that billing processes include quality control and error correction.

CERT auditors will request complete medical records for sampled claims. Non-response results in automatic improper payment finding.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All billing coordinators, coding personnel, and the Revenue Cycle Director shall receive training on the denial management process within 14 calendar days of hire or assignment. Training shall cover: (a) denial logging requirements; (b) denial category classification; (c) appeal merit assessment process; (d) Medicare appeals process (all 5 levels); (e) appeal timeline requirements; (f) ADR response protocol; (g) write-off authorization requirements; (h) denial trending and RCA triggers; (i) False Claims Act implications of billing patterns.

10.2 The Director of Nursing shall receive training on clinical denial review responsibilities and the clinical argument development process.

10.3 Annual refresher training on denial management procedures, updated appeal thresholds and deadlines, and denial trending results.

10.4 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix E) within 14 calendar days.

11. Version Control

FN-BC-003 — Patient Billing & Financial Responsibility

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes comprehensive standards for patient billing, financial responsibility notification, Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage (ABN) issuance, billing statement management, and collection of patient financial obligations at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Under 42 CFR § 484.50(a)(3), patients must be informed of expected payment sources and any charges for which the patient may be responsible. Patients have a fundamental right to understand their financial responsibility before and during the receipt of services. The agency has a legal, ethical, and regulatory obligation to bill patients accurately, transparently, and in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and consumer protection laws.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

All billing coordinators and billing specialists

All intake coordinators (financial screening at admission)

Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (ABN clinical determinations)

Compliance Officer

Administrator

Any contracted billing or collection service acting on behalf of the agency

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall provide every patient (or authorized representative) with a clear, written explanation of their financial responsibility — including applicable insurance benefits, cost-sharing obligations, and any anticipated non-covered services — prior to or at the time of admission, before services begin.

4.2 The agency shall inform each patient of the toll-free CMS Home Health Hotline number and the agency's own billing inquiry contact information at admission per 42 CFR § 484.50(a)(3).

4.3 Advance Beneficiary Notices of Noncoverage (ABNs) shall be issued to Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries using the current CMS-mandated form (CMS-R-131) whenever the agency has reason to believe a specific item or service will not be covered by Medicare. ABNs shall be issued before the non-covered service is provided and shall never be used as routine pre-admission documents or blanket waivers.

4.4 Patient billing statements shall be accurate, itemized, clearly readable, and include the agency's billing inquiry contact information. Statements shall be issued monthly for all open patient balances.

4.5 The agency shall not discriminate in billing practices based on race, color, national origin, disability, age, sex, religion, or any other protected characteristic under federal or state law.

4.6 Patient billing complaints and disputes shall be received, investigated, and resolved within 14 calendar days of receipt, documented per policy OP-PA-001, and shall not result in any interruption of clinically necessary services during the dispute period.

4.7 Collection activities shall be conducted in compliance with the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA) and applicable California state debt collection laws. No collection activity shall be initiated while a valid billing dispute is pending or a charity care application is under review.

4.8 No patient shall be denied medically necessary services due to inability to pay without first being screened for charity care or financial assistance eligibility per policy FN-FP-004.

4.9 All financial responsibility documentation shall be maintained in the patient's billing record and retained per CO-HP-007.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Financial Responsibility Notification at Admission

6.2 Advance Beneficiary Notice (ABN) Process

6.3 Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage (NOMNC)

6.4 Patient Billing Statements

6.5 Billing Disputes

6.6 Patient Collection Process

6.7 Escalation Matrix

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All intake coordinators and billing staff shall receive training on this policy within 14 calendar days of hire or assignment. Training shall cover: (a) patient financial responsibility notification requirements; (b) ABN issuance criteria, process, and prohibitions; (c) NOMNC requirements; (d) billing statement standards; (e) billing dispute handling; (f) collection process and FDCPA requirements; (g) charity care screening obligation.

10.2 Annual refresher training on ABN requirements and current CMS ABN form.

10.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix E within 14 calendar days.

11. Version Control

Per EN-LC-001. Substantive revisions require CFO review, Compliance Officer review, and Governing Body approval. Re-acknowledgment within 14 calendar days.

YOUR MEDICARE HOME HEALTH BENEFITS

If you are a Medicare fee-for-service beneficiary:

Medicare covers skilled nursing, physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, medical social work, and home health aide services when: (1) you are under the care of a physician; (2) you have a documented need for skilled care; (3) you meet the homebound criteria; and (4) the home health agency is Medicare-certified.

FN-BC-004 — Overpayment Identification & Refund

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

Federal law — specifically Section 1128J(d) of the Social Security Act, as added by Section 6402(a) of the Affordable Care Act, and codified at 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7k(d) and implementing regulation 42 CFR § 401.305 — requires Medicare providers to report and return identified overpayments within 60 calendar days of the date the overpayment is identified. Failure to report and return an identified overpayment within this 60-day window creates a "reverse false claim" under the False Claims Act, exposing the agency to treble damages and per-claim penalties of up to $27,894 per violation (2025 adjusted amount). This obligation extends 6 years from the date the overpayment was received.

This policy establishes the mandatory process for identifying, investigating, quantifying, reporting, and returning all Medicare and Medicaid overpayments at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. within full compliance with the 60-day rule. There are no exceptions to this requirement. No amount is too small to report. No business justification exists for retaining a known overpayment.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

All billing coordinators, billing specialists, and certified coders

Compliance Officer (overpayment investigation, reporting, 60-day tracking)

Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (clinical review of clinically-driven overpayments)

Administrator

Governing Body (notification of material overpayments per GV-GB-001)

Any contractor performing billing, coding, or compliance functions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall report and return any identified overpayment to Medicare or Medicaid within 60 calendar days of the date the overpayment is identified, without exception, as required by 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7k(d) and 42 CFR § 401.305.

4.2 An overpayment is "identified" when the agency has, or should have through the exercise of reasonable diligence, determined that it has received funds to which it is not entitled under applicable payment rules. The identification date is the date the agency first had credible information creating an obligation to investigate — not the date quantification is completed.

4.3 Upon receipt of any credible information suggesting a potential overpayment, the agency shall commence a reasonable diligence investigation. Reasonable diligence shall include: (a) a timely, good-faith investigation; (b) quantification of the overpayment; and (c) a determination of the cause. Reasonable diligence shall be completed within a maximum of 6 months from receipt of credible information, except in extraordinary circumstances documented by the Compliance Officer.

4.4 The 60-day refund clock begins on the date the agency first received credible information triggering an investigation obligation — even if quantification is not yet complete. The agency shall exercise reasonable diligence within this 60-day window whenever possible, or shall report and refund the estimated amount within 60 days with a final reconciliation to follow.

4.5 No identified overpayment shall be retained, offset against future claims, delayed in refund, or concealed. Deliberate delay, concealment, or failure to return an identified overpayment is a violation of the False Claims Act and this policy, constituting grounds for immediate termination and referral for legal action.

4.6 All identified or suspected overpayments shall be reported to the Compliance Officer immediately upon identification. The Compliance Officer shall maintain a centralized Overpayment Tracking Log (Appendix B) and oversee the investigation and refund process.

4.7 Overpayments exceeding $5,000 individually, or $10,000 in aggregate within any 12-month period, shall be reported to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting. Any overpayment associated with potential fraud shall be reported to the Governing Body within 48 hours.

4.8 The agency shall consider voluntary self-disclosure to the OIG Self-Disclosure Protocol for any overpayment resulting from potential fraud, kickback, or Stark Law violation. The decision to self-disclose shall be made by the Compliance Officer, CFO, and Administrator in consultation with legal counsel.

4.9 Overpayment identification processes shall be integrated into: (a) monthly payment reconciliation per FN-BC-007; (b) the internal documentation audit program per CO-DC-002; (c) the triangulation audit per CO-DC-004; (d) coding accuracy audits per FN-CM-001/002; (e) denial pattern analysis per FN-BC-002; and (f) the financial compliance monitoring program per FN-FP-007.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Sources of Overpayment Identification

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor and Auditor Expectations

OIG compliance program auditors will specifically request evidence that the agency has a functioning overpayment identification and refund process. Agencies that cannot demonstrate a formal process risk a finding of inadequate compliance program.

RAC/CERT/UPIC auditors issue overpayment demands; surveyors will verify that the agency responded timely and refunded amounts owed.

CMS surveyors reviewing 42 CFR § 484.100 (compliance with federal laws) will look for evidence that the agency self-identifies and returns overpayments.

OIG auditors will test whether the agency's lookback extends the full 6-year period required by regulation.

DOJ attorneys investigating False Claims Act matters will seek evidence of when the agency first became aware of the overpayment versus when (and if) it was returned.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 CMS and OIG Guidance

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All billing coordinators, coding personnel, and the Revenue Cycle Director shall receive initial training on the 60-day overpayment rule within 14 calendar days of hire or assignment to billing functions. Training shall be conducted by the Compliance Officer and must cover: (a) the legal basis of the 60-day rule (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7k(d), 42 CFR § 401.305); (b) the definition of "identified" and "identification date"; (c) the reasonable diligence standard; (d) the 6-year lookback period; (e) the reverse false claim consequences of failure to report and return; (f) the obligation and process for reporting potential overpayments to the Compliance Officer within 24 hours; (g) prohibited conduct (retention, concealment, delay); (h) the investigation and refund process under this policy.

10.2 The Compliance Officer shall provide annual refresher training to all billing, coding, and revenue cycle personnel, plus the Director of Nursing, Administrator, and CFO. Annual training shall include: current penalty amounts, recent enforcement actions, and any CMS/OIG guidance updates.

10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix F) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new hire/assignment.

10.4 The Compliance Officer shall maintain a training tracking log. Training non-compliance shall be reported to the CFO and HR Director within 7 calendar days.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the current approved version is valid. Superseded versions must be archived and marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Substantive revisions require: (a) Compliance Officer and CFO review; (b) Governing Body approval documented in meeting minutes; (c) re-acknowledgment by all in-scope personnel within 14 calendar days; (d) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the CFO with notification to the Compliance Officer and Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

FN-BC-005 — Pre-Claim Review Compliance

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the agency's readiness framework and operational procedures for compliance with any CMS Pre-Claim Review (PCR) demonstration program applicable to home health services in California or any other state in which Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. operates. CMS has implemented PCR demonstrations in selected states to reduce improper payments in the home health industry. While PCR may not be currently active in all jurisdictions, CMS retains the authority to expand or reinstate PCR programs at any time. This policy ensures Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. has a documented, operationally ready process for immediate PCR compliance upon CMS activation, minimizing disruption to patient care and revenue cycle operations.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

All billing coordinators and billing specialists

Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

Compliance Officer

Administrator

All certified coders

All clinical documentation staff supporting PCR submissions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a state of operational readiness for PCR compliance such that the agency can implement full PCR submission within 30 calendar days of CMS announcement of a PCR program affecting the agency's service area.

4.2 When a PCR program is active and applicable to the agency, all non-excepted home health episodes shall be submitted for pre-claim review prior to final claim submission. No final claim shall be submitted for a PCR-required episode without a provisional affirmation or affirmation from the PCR reviewer.

4.3 The Revenue Cycle Director shall designate a PCR Coordinator responsible for monitoring CMS PCR announcements, managing PCR submissions, tracking decisions, and managing resubmissions and appeals.

4.4 PCR submissions shall contain all required documentation as specified by the CMS PCR program requirements, which typically include: (a) a completed PCR request form; (b) the Plan of Care (485); (c) physician certification; (d) face-to-face encounter documentation; (e) OASIS assessment; (f) clinical documentation supporting medical necessity, homebound status, and skilled care need.

4.5 The agency shall maintain a PCR Decision Tracking Log for all submitted episodes and shall not bill any episode where the PCR determination is "non-affirmation" unless the non-affirmation is successfully appealed through the PCR reconsideration process.

4.6 Non-affirmation of a PCR request does not prohibit the agency from providing or continuing services if clinically necessary, but it does prevent Medicare billing until the decision is overturned or the underlying documentation deficiency is corrected and the request is resubmitted.

4.7 The Compliance Officer shall monitor PCR non-affirmation rates and patterns monthly. A non-affirmation rate exceeding 10% shall trigger a root cause analysis within 30 calendar days.

4.8 All PCR-related processes shall be integrated with the agency's pre-billing verification (FN-BC-001 §6.1), documentation standards (CL-CD-001 through CL-CD-004), and the corporate compliance program (CO-CP-001).

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 PCR Readiness Monitoring

6.2 PCR Submission Process (When PCR Program Is Active)

6.3 PCR Decision Processing

6.4 Non-Affirmation Response

6.5 Patient Care Continuity During PCR

6.6 PCR Trending and Root Cause Analysis

6.7 Escalation Matrix

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations and CMS Authority

9.2 CMS Guidance

9.3 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 When a PCR program is activated, all billing, coding, and clinical documentation staff shall receive PCR-specific training within 30 calendar days of program activation. Training shall cover: (a) PCR program requirements and submission process; (b) required documentation elements; (c) clinical documentation quality standards specific to PCR; (d) non-affirmation response procedures; (e) the prohibition on billing non-affirmed episodes; (f) patient care continuity obligations.

10.2 The Director of Nursing shall conduct targeted clinical documentation training focused on homebound status, medical necessity, and skilled care need documentation — the three most common PCR non-affirmation drivers nationally.

10.3 Annual refresher training while PCR is active, including review of non-affirmation patterns and corrective actions.

10.4 All personnel within scope shall sign Appendix D within 14 calendar days.

11. Version Control

Per EN-LC-001. This policy has a Triggered review cycle — reviewed upon CMS PCR program activation, modification, or termination. Substantive revisions require CFO and Compliance Officer review, Governing Body approval, and re-acknowledgment within 14 calendar days.

FN-BC-006 — Request for Anticipated Payment (RAP) / Notice of Admission (NOA) Management

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes standards for timely and accurate submission of the Notice of Admission (NOA) to Medicare for all home health episodes at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective January 1, 2022, CMS replaced the Request for Anticipated Payment (RAP) with the NOA under the Patient-Driven Groupings Model (PDGM). The NOA is a one-time electronic notification submitted to the Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) within 5 calendar days of the start of care (SOC) date that notifies Medicare of the patient's admission to home health services. Unlike the former RAP, the NOA does not generate a payment — it establishes the episode in the Medicare payment system and is a prerequisite for final claim submission. Failure to submit a timely NOA results in a reduction of the final payment for the affected 30-day period. This policy ensures 100% compliance with NOA submission requirements to prevent payment reductions and ensure uninterrupted revenue cycle operations.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

All billing coordinators and billing specialists

Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (SOC date coordination)

Compliance Officer

Intake Coordinators (admission date tracking)

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall submit a Notice of Admission (NOA) to the MAC within 5 calendar days of the start of care date for every new Medicare home health episode (SOC) and every Resumption of Care (ROC) episode, as required by CMS.

4.2 The NOA is a one-time submission per beneficiary per period of care. It is NOT required for subsequent 30-day periods within the same period of care (recertifications within a continuous episode) unless the patient is readmitted after a discharge.

4.3 If the NOA is submitted after the 5-calendar-day window but within 30 calendar days of the SOC/ROC date, the final payment for the first 30-day period is reduced by a percentage amount established by CMS (currently 1/30th of the full payment amount for each day the NOA is late).

4.4 If the NOA is not submitted within 30 calendar days of the SOC/ROC date, the episode is not established in the Medicare system and no payment can be made for the first 30-day period. This constitutes a permanent revenue loss.

4.5 The Revenue Cycle Director shall maintain an NOA Submission Tracking Dashboard monitoring: (a) SOC/ROC dates; (b) NOA submission dates; (c) NOA acceptance confirmation; (d) timely submission compliance rate.

4.6 The Billing Coordinator shall confirm NOA acceptance by the MAC through the clearinghouse acknowledgment (999/277CA transactions) within 2 business days of submission.

4.7 NOA submission requires the following minimum data elements: (a) Medicare beneficiary number; (b) provider NPI and CCN; (c) SOC or ROC date; (d) type of admission (SOC vs. ROC); (e) physician NPI. The agency shall ensure all required data elements are accurate at the time of submission.

4.8 The NOA submission process shall be tightly integrated with the intake/admission workflow so that the NOA can be submitted within 24 hours of SOC whenever possible, with a maximum of 5 calendar days.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 NOA Submission Process

6.2 Timeliness Monitoring and Escalation

6.3 NOA for Specific Scenarios

6.4 Root Cause Analysis for Late or Missed NOAs

7. Documentation Requirements

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All billing coordinators and the Revenue Cycle Director shall receive training on NOA requirements within 14 calendar days of hire. Training shall cover: (a) NOA vs. RAP distinction; (b) the 5-day submission deadline; (c) payment reduction consequences for late submission; (d) permanent payment loss for missed submission; (e) NOA data element requirements; (f) submission and confirmation process; (g) escalation protocols.

10.2 All intake coordinators and admitting clinicians shall receive training on their obligation to notify the billing department of the SOC/ROC date on the same day as the first visit.

10.3 Annual refresher training for all billing staff.

FN-BC-007 — Payment & Reimbursement Reconciliation

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the mandatory process for reconciling expected Medicare and other payer reimbursements against actual payments received by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Payment reconciliation is a critical internal control that ensures: (a) the agency receives the correct PDGM payment for every billed 30-day period; (b) underpayments are identified and pursued; (c) overpayments are identified and reported/returned within 60 days per FN-BC-004 and 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7k(d); (d) payment anomalies are investigated for root cause; (e) revenue cycle performance is accurately measured and reported to agency leadership and the Governing Body. Without systematic reconciliation, the agency cannot detect payment errors — whether in the agency's favor (creating overpayment liability) or against the agency (creating revenue loss). Both scenarios carry financial, regulatory, and compliance consequences.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

All billing coordinators and billing specialists

Compliance Officer (overpayment identification linkage)

Administrator

QAPI Coordinator (revenue cycle performance integration)

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall perform payment reconciliation for 100% of Medicare claims within 30 calendar days of payment receipt (remittance advice date).

4.2 The Revenue Cycle Director shall maintain a Payment Reconciliation Worksheet (Appendix A) for every 30-day payment period comparing: (a) expected PDGM payment (based on the claim's PDGM classification — clinical grouping, functional level, comorbidity adjustment, timing, and admission source); (b) actual payment received per the Medicare Remittance Advice (835 transaction); (c) any adjustments, offsets, or sequestration reductions applied.

4.3 Any payment discrepancy exceeding $100 between the expected PDGM payment and the actual payment received shall be investigated within 10 business days. The investigation shall determine whether the discrepancy is due to: (a) correct CMS adjustment (sequestration, outlier, LUPA, PEP); (b) agency coding or billing error; (c) MAC processing error; (d) overpayment to the agency; or (e) underpayment to the agency.

4.4 Identified underpayments shall be pursued through the appropriate channel: (a) MAC inquiry for processing errors; (b) appeal per FN-BC-002 for denied amounts; (c) replacement claim for agency billing errors.

4.5 Identified overpayments shall be immediately referred to the Compliance Officer for processing per FN-BC-004 (60-Day Overpayment Rule).

4.6 The Revenue Cycle Director shall produce a Monthly Payment Reconciliation Summary Report (Appendix B) by the 20th of each month covering the prior month's payments. The report shall be reviewed by the CFO within 5 business days.

4.7 Quarterly payment reconciliation data shall be included in the financial report to the Governing Body per GV-GB-001 §6.2.5.

4.8 Non-Medicare payer payments (Medicare Advantage, Medi-Cal, commercial) shall also be reconciled monthly against contracted rates or fee schedules per FN-FP-001.

FN-CM-001 — PDGM Classification & Coding Accuracy

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes standards for accurate Patient-Driven Groupings Model (PDGM) classification of all Medicare home health 30-day payment periods at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. PDGM determines payment through five classification elements: admission source and timing, clinical grouping (based on the principal diagnosis), functional impairment level (based on OASIS functional items), comorbidity adjustment (based on secondary diagnoses), and episode timing (early vs. late periods). Accurate PDGM classification is essential because: (a) it determines the agency's reimbursement — incorrect classification results in either overpayment (creating 60-day rule liability) or underpayment (revenue loss); (b) it is directly tied to the accuracy of ICD-10 coding and OASIS assessment data; (c) CMS auditors, RACs, and OIG specifically target PDGM classification accuracy as a key audit area; (d) systematic misclassification constitutes False Claims Act exposure. This policy ensures every PDGM element is verified, documented, and traceable to the clinical record.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

All certified coders performing diagnosis coding or PDGM classification

Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (OASIS accuracy affecting functional level)

All OASIS-authorized clinicians (functional scoring)

Compliance Officer (coding audit oversight)

Billing Coordinators (pre-billing verification of PDGM)

QAPI Coordinator (coding quality integration)

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Every 30-day payment period billed to Medicare by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall be classified under PDGM using accurate, documentation-supported data for all five classification elements.

4.2 PDGM classification shall be performed or verified by a certified coder (CCS, CCS-P, CPC, CPC-H, HCS-D, or equivalent nationally recognized coding credential) for every 30-day period before the final claim is submitted per FN-BC-001 §6.1.2.10.

4.3 The principal diagnosis code driving the clinical grouping shall be the primary reason for the home health episode and must be supported by physician documentation in the Plan of Care and the clinical record per FN-CM-002.

4.4 The functional impairment level shall be derived from OASIS functional assessment items completed per CL-OA policies. OASIS functional data used for PDGM classification must be accurate, contemporaneous, and unmodified for payment purposes.

4.5 The comorbidity adjustment shall be based on secondary diagnosis codes that are: (a) actively addressed during the episode; (b) documented by the physician; (c) coded to the highest specificity per ICD-10-CM guidelines; and (d) verified by a certified coder.

4.6 Admission source (institutional vs. community) and timing (early vs. late) shall be verified against the patient's actual admission history and prior claims data.

4.7 The agency shall NEVER: (a) select a principal diagnosis primarily to maximize payment rather than to reflect the primary reason for care; (b) manipulate OASIS functional scores to increase the functional impairment level for payment purposes; (c) add secondary diagnoses not supported by physician documentation to trigger a higher comorbidity adjustment; (d) misrepresent admission source or timing. Any such conduct constitutes upcoding and is prohibited per FN-BC-001 §4.6 and CO-FA-003.

4.8 Quarterly PDGM classification audits shall be conducted per §6.4 to verify accuracy across all five classification elements. Audit results shall be reported to the CFO and Compliance Officer.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 PDGM Classification Process

6.2 Clinical Grouping Verification

6.3 Functional Impairment Level Verification

6.4 Quarterly PDGM Classification Audit

6.5 Escalation Matrix

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.2 Common Failure Points

9. References

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All certified coders shall receive initial training on PDGM classification within 14 calendar days of hire. Training shall cover: (a) PDGM payment methodology and all five classification elements; (b) CMS PDGM grouper logic; (c) clinical grouping determination from ICD-10 codes; (d) functional impairment scoring from OASIS items; (e) comorbidity adjustment determination; (f) admission source verification; (g) timing determination; (h) PDGM Classification Worksheet completion; (i) prohibition on upcoding and coding for payment; (j) False Claims Act liability for coding errors.

10.2 Annual refresher training including CMS PDGM updates, rate changes, and grouper changes effective each calendar year.

10.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

FN-CM-002 — ICD-10 Coding Standards & Accuracy

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes comprehensive standards for ICD-10-CM diagnosis coding at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. to ensure that all diagnosis codes assigned to home health episodes are accurate, supported by physician documentation in the medical record, coded to the highest specificity per the ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines, and compliant with all applicable federal coding regulations. Accurate diagnosis coding is critical because: (a) the principal diagnosis determines the PDGM clinical grouping and directly affects payment per FN-CM-001; (b) secondary diagnoses determine comorbidity adjustments; (c) inaccurate coding constitutes potential False Claims Act liability; (d) coding accuracy is a primary OIG and RAC audit target for home health agencies; (e) diagnosis codes drive clinical quality measures reported through OASIS.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All certified coders performing diagnosis coding

CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager (physician documentation adequacy)

All OASIS-authorized clinicians (diagnosis selection during assessment)

Compliance Officer (coding audit oversight)

All physicians ordering home health services (documentation of diagnoses)

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All diagnosis codes assigned to home health episodes at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall comply with the current ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting as published by NCHS and CMS, and the HIPAA code set standards (45 CFR § 162.1002).

4.2 Every diagnosis code — principal and secondary — must be supported by physician documentation in the medical record. Coders shall not assign diagnosis codes based solely on clinical assessment by non-physician clinicians unless the physician has acknowledged and documented the diagnosis.

4.3 The principal diagnosis shall represent the primary reason the patient is receiving home health services. Selection of the principal diagnosis shall follow the CMS OASIS Guidance Manual and ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for sequencing in home health.

4.4 All diagnosis codes shall be assigned to the highest level of specificity available in the current ICD-10-CM code set. Unspecified codes shall be used only when clinical documentation does not provide sufficient detail for a more specific code, and a physician query has been attempted.

4.5 Only certified coders (holding CCS, CCS-P, CPC, CPC-H, HCS-D, or equivalent nationally recognized credential) shall perform final diagnosis code assignment and verification for billing purposes. Clinicians may select preliminary diagnosis codes during OASIS completion, but final coding for billing shall be verified by a certified coder.

4.6 Coders shall query the physician when documentation is ambiguous, incomplete, or insufficient to assign an accurate code. Queries shall be documented in the coding record. Coders shall not assign codes based on assumptions or clinical inference not documented by the physician.

4.7 Quarterly coding accuracy audits shall be conducted per §6.4 with a minimum accuracy standard of 95%.

4.8 The agency shall NEVER: (a) assign diagnosis codes not documented by the physician; (b) assign codes to maximize reimbursement rather than reflect the documented clinical picture; (c) use unspecified codes when more specific codes are available and documentation supports them; (d) assign resolved or inactive diagnoses as current conditions; (e) change physician-documented diagnoses without physician authorization. Any such conduct constitutes coding fraud.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.2 Specificity Requirements

10.3 Annual coding refresher with competency assessment (≥80% pass rate).
