OP-FM-003 — Vendor & Supplier Management

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes standards for the selection, qualification, contracting, monitoring, and performance evaluation of vendors and suppliers providing goods, services, or contracted functions to Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective vendor management ensures the agency receives quality products and services, maintains regulatory compliance (including anti-kickback and Stark Law requirements per CO-FA-001), protects patient safety, controls costs, and satisfies applicable requirements of 42 CFR § 484.105 (Organization and Administration), 42 CFR § 484.100 (Compliance with Federal, State, and Local Laws), and OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies.

2. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Operations Director

The Administrator

The Compliance Officer

The CFO / Finance Director

All department heads or staff authorized to initiate vendor relationships or procurement

All current and prospective vendors, suppliers, and contracted service providers

This policy does not govern employment relationships (see HR-WM-002 for contractors and per diem staff) or Business Associate Agreements for HIPAA purposes (see CO-HP-005), though vendor qualification under this policy may be concurrent with BAA execution.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an Approved Vendor List (AVL) of all vendors and suppliers authorized to provide goods or services to the agency.

4.2 No vendor shall be engaged, and no purchase order or contract shall be executed, until the vendor has been qualified through the agency's vendor qualification process, except for emergency procurements under Section 5.6.

4.3 All vendor relationships shall be documented through written contracts or purchase agreements that define: (a) scope of goods or services; (b) pricing and payment terms; (c) quality and performance standards; (d) compliance requirements; (e) termination provisions; (f) insurance and liability requirements; (g) Business Associate Agreement (if vendor will access PHI).

4.4 The agency shall not enter into any vendor relationship that could constitute a violation of the Anti-Kickback Statute or Stark Law. All vendor relationships involving referral sources, physicians, or healthcare entities shall be reviewed by the Compliance Officer before execution per CO-FA-001.

4.5 All vendors providing goods or services paid directly or indirectly by federal healthcare programs shall be screened against the OIG LEIE and SAM exclusion databases prior to engagement and monthly thereafter per HR-TA-003.

4.6 Vendor performance shall be evaluated at least annually. Vendors failing to meet performance standards shall be placed on corrective action or removed from the AVL.

4.7 The agency shall maintain vendor records for a minimum of 7 years per CO-HP-007.

5. Procedures

5.1 Vendor Identification and Selection

5.2 Vendor Qualification

5.3 Contract Execution

5.4 Ongoing Vendor Monitoring

5.5 Annual Vendor Performance Evaluation

5.6 Emergency Procurement

5.7 Vendor Termination

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring

7.1 How Compliance Is Measured

7.2 Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

9. Cross-Referenced Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All staff authorized to initiate vendor relationships, procurement, or purchase orders shall receive training on this policy within 14 calendar days of hire or role assignment. Training shall cover: (a) vendor qualification requirements; (b) AVL policy and restrictions; (c) exclusion screening requirements; (d) anti-kickback and Stark Law awareness; (e) contract requirements; (f) emergency procurement procedures; (g) documentation requirements.

10.2 Annual refresher training shall be conducted for all staff with procurement authority and documented per HR-TD-001.

10.3 All staff completing this training shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix H) within 14 calendar days of training completion or policy revision.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version is valid. Superseded versions must be archived and marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Substantive revisions require: (a) Operations Director review and recommendation; (b) Administrator approval; (c) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days; (d) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections) may be approved by the Operations Director with notification to the Administrator.

OP-FM-004 — Mail & Correspondence Management

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes standards for the receipt, processing, tracking, routing, and retention of all incoming and outgoing mail and official correspondence at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Proper mail management supports timely response to regulatory communications, physician orders, payer correspondence, patient communications, and legal documents. This policy ensures the agency meets documentation and communication requirements under 42 CFR § 484.105 (Organization and Administration) and HIPAA privacy requirements for handling correspondence containing Protected Health Information (PHI) per CO-HP-001.

2. Scope

This policy applies to:

All office staff responsible for mail handling

The Operations Director

The Administrator

The Compliance Officer (for regulatory and legal correspondence)

All department heads responsible for responding to correspondence within their functional area

This policy covers: (a) U.S. Postal Service mail; (b) courier/overnight deliveries (FedEx, UPS, etc.); (c) secure fax communications; (d) official agency correspondence sent externally. This policy does not govern electronic email (see OP-SL-005 and IT-UP-002) or clinical documentation transmission (see CL-CD-001).

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain an organized system for receiving, logging, routing, and responding to all incoming mail and official correspondence.

4.2 All incoming mail shall be opened, sorted, logged, and routed to the appropriate department or individual on the day of receipt (or next business day if received on a weekend or holiday).

4.3 Time-sensitive correspondence shall be flagged, prioritized, and delivered to the responsible party immediately upon identification, with escalation if the responsible party is unavailable.

4.4 All correspondence containing PHI shall be handled, routed, and stored in compliance with HIPAA privacy requirements per CO-HP-001 and CO-HP-004.

4.5 All outgoing official correspondence shall be reviewed, approved, and documented before transmission.

4.6 The agency shall maintain a mail log for all incoming and outgoing official correspondence to support audit trails and regulatory compliance.

4.7 Fax communications containing PHI shall be transmitted only through the agency's secure fax system per OP-SL-005 and CO-HP-002.

5. Procedures

5.1 Incoming Mail Processing

5.2 Time-Sensitive Correspondence Management

5.3 Outgoing Correspondence

5.4 Fax Management

5.5 Returned Mail and Undeliverable Correspondence

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring

8. Regulatory References

9. Cross-Referenced Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All staff assigned mail handling responsibilities shall receive training on this policy within 14 calendar days of assignment. Training shall cover: (a) mail opening, sorting, and classification; (b) time-sensitive correspondence identification and escalation; (c) PHI handling requirements; (d) mail logging procedures; (e) fax management and HIPAA confidentiality notice requirements.

10.2 All staff shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix E) within 14 calendar days.

11. Version Control

Per EN-LC-001 standards. Only the current approved version is valid. Substantive revisions require Administrator approval and re-acknowledgment within 14 calendar days.

OP-FM-005 — Emergency Operations & Business Continuity

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes the agency's comprehensive Emergency Preparedness Plan, Emergency Operations, and Business Continuity framework for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. as required by 42 CFR § 484.102 — Condition of Participation: Emergency Preparedness. CMS requires all Medicare- and Medicaid-participating home health agencies to develop and maintain a comprehensive emergency preparedness program based on an all-hazards approach. This policy ensures the agency can: (a) protect the safety and well-being of patients and staff during emergencies; (b) maintain continuity of essential services; (c) communicate effectively with patients, staff, external authorities, and the community; (d) recover operations following a disaster or emergency; (e) comply with all applicable federal, state, and local emergency preparedness requirements.

2. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body

The Administrator

The Operations Director

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Compliance Officer

The IT Director / CISO

All clinical and administrative staff

All contracted or per diem staff

All patients and caregivers served by the agency

This policy applies to all types of emergencies including but not limited to: natural disasters (earthquakes, wildfires, floods, severe storms), technological hazards (power outages, cyberattacks, EHR system failure), public health emergencies (pandemics, infectious disease outbreaks per OP-SL-006), workplace violence, active threats, and any event that disrupts normal agency operations.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall develop, maintain, and implement a comprehensive, all-hazards Emergency Preparedness Plan (EPP) per 42 CFR § 484.102.

4.2 The EPP shall be reviewed and updated at least annually by the Emergency Management Team and approved by the Governing Body at the third quarterly meeting per GV-GB-001 § 6.2.6.1.

4.3 The agency shall conduct a Hazard Vulnerability Analysis (HVA) at least annually to identify and prioritize potential emergencies based on the agency's geographic location, patient population, and operational profile.

4.4 The agency shall designate an Emergency Management Team with clearly defined roles and responsibilities for emergency response, communication, and recovery.

4.5 The agency shall conduct emergency preparedness training for all staff at orientation and annually thereafter per HR-TD-005.

4.6 The agency shall conduct at least 2 emergency preparedness exercises per year — one community-based (if available) or facility-based tabletop exercise and one operations-based exercise per RM-EP-002.

4.7 The agency shall maintain a communication plan that ensures the ability to contact all patients, staff, and external authorities during an emergency.

4.8 The agency shall maintain cooperative agreements or arrangements with local emergency management agencies, other healthcare providers, and community organizations to support emergency response.

4.9 The agency shall prioritize patient safety above all other considerations during any emergency. No administrative concern shall override clinical necessity.

4.10 The agency shall maintain business continuity capabilities with defined Recovery Time Objectives for all essential functions.

5. Procedures

5.1 Emergency Preparedness Plan Development and Maintenance

5.2 Emergency Management Team and Command Structure

5.3 Emergency Activation and Response

5.4 Business Continuity

Essential Functions and Recovery Time Objectives:

5.5 Emergency Communication Plan

5.6 Training and Testing

5.7 Deactivation and Recovery

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring

7.1 How Compliance Is Measured

7.2 Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

9. Cross-Referenced Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All staff shall receive emergency preparedness training within 14 calendar days of hire. Training shall cover: (a) the agency's Emergency Preparedness Plan; (b) activation and notification procedures; (c) individual roles and responsibilities during emergencies; (d) patient triage and prioritization; (e) communication procedures and emergency contacts; (f) EHR downtime procedures; (g) location of emergency supplies and reference materials; (h) California-specific hazards (earthquake, wildfire response).

10.2 Annual refresher training shall be conducted for all staff and documented per HR-TD-001 and HR-TD-005.

10.3 All Emergency Management Team members shall receive enhanced training on their specific emergency roles, including tabletop exercise participation, at least annually.

10.4 All staff completing this training shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix F) within 14 calendar days of training completion or policy revision.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version is valid. Superseded versions must be archived and marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Substantive revisions require: (a) Emergency Management Team review; (b) Administrator recommendation; (c) Governing Body approval documented in meeting minutes; (d) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days; (e) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Operations Director with notification to the Administrator and documentation at the next Governing Body meeting.

QA-PG-001 — QAPI Program Establishment & Governance

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the agency's Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI) program as a formalized, data-driven, and governing body–directed system for continuous quality monitoring, performance improvement, and patient safety assurance at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The QAPI program is the central mechanism through which the agency identifies opportunities for improvement, implements evidence-based interventions, monitors outcomes, and sustains gains across all operational and clinical domains. This policy ensures the agency satisfies the requirements set forth in 42 CFR § 484.65 — Condition of Participation: Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement, which mandates that a home health agency must develop, implement, evaluate, and maintain an effective, ongoing, agency-wide, data-driven QAPI program.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

The Agency Administrator

The QAPI Coordinator (designated program lead)

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

All members of the QAPI Committee

The Compliance Officer

All clinical, administrative, and support staff whose work contributes to or is measured by the QAPI program

All contracted and per diem staff providing services on behalf of the agency

Exclusion: This policy does not govern the detailed methodology of individual Performance Improvement Projects (PIPs), which is addressed in QA-PI-001, nor adverse event investigation procedures, which are addressed in QA-AE-001 and QA-AE-002. This policy establishes the governance framework within which those activities operate.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall establish, maintain, and continuously operate an agency-wide QAPI program that reflects the complexity of the agency's organization and services, as required by 42 CFR § 484.65(a).

4.2 The QAPI program shall be governed by the Governing Body, which retains ultimate accountability for the program's effectiveness, resource allocation, and strategic direction. The Governing Body shall not delegate this ultimate accountability.

4.3 The Governing Body shall designate a qualified QAPI Coordinator with defined authority, dedicated time, and sufficient resources to administer the QAPI program on a day-to-day basis.

4.4 The QAPI program shall be data-driven, utilizing measurable indicators derived from clinical outcomes, patient safety events, operational performance, patient experience, regulatory compliance, and financial data to identify priorities and evaluate improvement interventions.

4.5 The QAPI program shall integrate and coordinate with the agency's compliance program (CO-CP-001), risk management program (RM-ER-001), infection prevention and control program (CL-SD-016), and all clinical and operational domains to ensure a unified quality and safety framework.

4.6 The QAPI program shall maintain a written QAPI plan, approved annually by the Governing Body per policy QA-PG-002, that defines the program's goals, measurable indicators, performance improvement project requirements, committee structure, reporting schedule, and accountability framework.

4.7 All agency staff — clinical, administrative, and contracted — are responsible for participating in quality improvement activities within their scope of practice and role, and for reporting quality concerns, adverse events, and near-misses through established channels.

4.8 The QAPI program shall comply with all applicable CMS Conditions of Participation, state regulatory requirements, and accreditation standards. The agency shall not operate any service line or clinical program outside the scope of QAPI monitoring.

4.9 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Superseded versions must not be used for any operational or compliance purpose. Any revision to this policy requires Governing Body approval and re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 QAPI Program Establishment

6.2 QAPI Committee Structure and Function

6.3 Governing Body QAPI Oversight

6.4 QAPI Program Integration

6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey under SOM Appendix B will specifically verify:

Evidence that a QAPI program exists and functions. Surveyors will request the QAPI plan, QAPI Program Description, and committee meeting minutes. An agency that cannot produce these documents will face an immediate Condition-level inquiry under 42 CFR § 484.65.

Evidence that the QAPI program is agency-wide. Surveyors will verify that all service lines — not just nursing — are monitored by the QAPI program. A program limited to a single discipline will be cited as non-compliant.

Evidence that the QAPI program is data-driven. Surveyors will look for measurable indicators, dashboards, trending data, and documented analysis. Programs that rely solely on anecdotal discussion without data will be cited.

Evidence that the Governing Body exercises oversight. Surveyors will cross-reference QAPI Committee reports with Governing Body minutes to verify that the Governing Body receives, reviews, discusses, and acts upon quality data. Passive receipt of reports without documented discussion or action is a common deficiency.

Evidence that performance improvement projects exist. Surveyors will request documentation of active and completed PIPs including methodology, data, and results. An agency with no active PIPs will be cited.

Evidence that adverse events are identified, reported, and acted upon. Surveyors will review the adverse event reporting process, investigation records, and corrective action documentation.

Evidence that the QAPI program leads to measurable improvement. Surveyors will look for documented improvement trends, not just identification of problems. A program that identifies issues but shows no improvement over time will be cited for ineffectiveness.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations (42 CFR Part 484)

9.2 CMS Guidance

CMS State Operations Manual, Appendix B — Guidance to Surveyors: Provides interpretive guidelines for survey of 42 CFR § 484.65 compliance; defines surveyor expectations for QAPI program evidence, data use, and governing body involvement.

CMS OASIS-E2 Guidance Manual: OASIS outcome data serves as a primary data source for the QAPI program.

CMS Home Health Quality Reporting Program (HH QRP): Defines quality measures reported publicly on Home Health Compare; QAPI program must monitor these measures.

9.3 OIG Guidance

OIG Compliance Program Guidance for Home Health Agencies: Establishes expectation that quality monitoring is integrated with the compliance program and that the governing body receives regular quality performance reports.

9.4 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All QAPI Committee members shall receive orientation to this policy and the QAPI program structure within 14 calendar days of appointment to the committee. Orientation shall be conducted by the QAPI Coordinator and must cover: (a) QAPI program purpose and regulatory basis; (b) committee member responsibilities; (c) quality indicator definitions and dashboard interpretation; (d) PIP methodology overview; (e) adverse event reporting and escalation; (f) documentation expectations; (g) CMS survey expectations for QAPI evidence.

10.2 All agency staff (clinical, administrative, and contracted) shall receive QAPI awareness training during initial orientation per HR-TA-005 and annually thereafter per HR-TD-001. Training must cover: (a) the purpose and structure of the QAPI program; (b) staff responsibility for reporting quality concerns, adverse events, and near-misses; (c) how to report through established channels; (d) the non-punitive culture of quality reporting; (e) how QAPI data is used to improve care.

10.3 All personnel within scope of this policy shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new assignment.

10.4 The QAPI Coordinator shall maintain a training tracking log documenting all QAPI-related training including: attendee name, training topic, date, trainer, and completion status. Training completion rates shall be reported to the Governing Body as part of the quarterly QAPI Performance Report.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version of this policy, as reflected in the policy header, is valid for any operational, compliance, or regulatory purpose. All superseded versions must be archived and clearly marked as "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Any substantive revision to this policy requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body, documented in meeting minutes; (b) re-acknowledgment by all personnel within scope, within 14 calendar days of the revised effective date; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions (formatting, typographical corrections, updated cross-references) may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting. Non-substantive revisions do not require re-acknowledgment.

12. Appendices

Appendix D: QAPI Action Item Tracker Template

QA-PG-002 — QAPI Plan Development & Annual Review

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy mandates the development, content requirements, approval process, and annual review of a written QAPI plan for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The QAPI plan is the agency's actionable roadmap for quality improvement — translating the governance structure established in QA-PG-001 into defined goals, measurable indicators, performance improvement priorities, committee responsibilities, and reporting timelines for each calendar year. This policy ensures the agency satisfies the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.65(a) and (e), which require the governing body to ensure the QAPI program has a written plan with defined goals and measurable outcomes, and that the governing body approves the plan and ensures adequate resources for its execution.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

The Agency Administrator

The QAPI Coordinator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

All QAPI Committee members

The Compliance Officer

All department heads and supervisors responsible for achieving QAPI plan goals

Exclusion: This policy defines QAPI plan content, approval, and review requirements. It does not govern the execution of individual PIPs (QA-PI-001) or specific quality indicator monitoring procedures (QA-PI-002), though the QAPI plan must define priorities for both.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a written QAPI plan that is reviewed, updated, and approved by the Governing Body annually, at the first quarterly meeting of each calendar year.

4.2 The QAPI plan shall define the agency's quality improvement priorities for the plan year based on data analysis of the prior year's performance, regulatory requirements, patient population characteristics, and identified areas of risk.

4.3 The QAPI plan shall include measurable goals with defined performance thresholds, responsible parties, monitoring frequency, and expected outcomes for each priority area.

4.4 The QAPI plan shall identify a minimum of two (2) active Performance Improvement Projects (PIPs) at all times, proportionate to the scope and complexity of the agency's services, as required by 42 CFR § 484.65(d).

4.5 The QAPI plan shall not be treated as a static document. The QAPI Coordinator shall update the plan as needed throughout the year in response to: (a) new adverse event trends; (b) significant regulatory changes; (c) CMS survey findings; (d) Governing Body directives. All mid-year modifications must be documented, approved by the QAPI Committee, and reported to the Governing Body at the next quarterly meeting.

4.6 The QAPI plan year shall align with the calendar year (January 1 through December 31). The plan for the upcoming year must be finalized and submitted to the Governing Body for approval no later than December 15 of the preceding year.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Annual QAPI Plan Development

6.2 Required QAPI Plan Content

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors will specifically verify:

A written QAPI plan exists for the current period. Surveyors will request the plan and verify it covers the current year with defined goals and indicators.

The plan was approved by the Governing Body. Surveyors will cross-reference the plan with Governing Body minutes to verify documented approval.

The plan is data-driven. Surveyors will verify that priority selection was based on data analysis, not arbitrary selection.

Goals are measurable. Surveyors will look for specific, quantifiable targets — not vague aspirational statements.

The plan is operationalized. Surveyors will compare plan goals with actual QAPI Committee activities and meeting minutes to verify the plan drives action.

The plan is reviewed and evaluated. Surveyors will look for evidence that the prior year's plan was evaluated and that results informed the current plan.

QA-PG-003 — QAPI Committee Structure & Meeting Requirements

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines the composition, authority, operating procedures, documentation standards, and escalation requirements for the QAPI Committee at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The QAPI Committee is the operational body responsible for translating the QAPI program governance (QA-PG-001) and annual plan (QA-PG-002) into executed quality improvement activities. This policy ensures the committee functions as a structured, accountable, multidisciplinary forum for data review, decision-making, and quality improvement action consistent with the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.65.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator (Committee Chair)

All QAPI Committee members (standing and ad hoc)

The Agency Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Compliance Officer (standing invitee)

All department heads and supervisors who participate in or present to the QAPI Committee

Exclusion: This policy governs committee structure and operations. The content of the QAPI plan is governed by QA-PG-002. Individual PIP execution is governed by QA-PI-001. Adverse event investigation methodology is governed by QA-AE-002.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a standing multidisciplinary QAPI Committee that serves as the primary operational body for quality assessment and performance improvement activities.

4.2 The QAPI Committee shall be chaired by the QAPI Coordinator. In the absence of the QAPI Coordinator, the Director of Nursing shall serve as acting chair.

4.3 The QAPI Committee shall meet no fewer than 12 times per calendar year (monthly). Special meetings shall be convened when urgent quality or safety matters arise.

4.4 Committee membership shall include representation from all active clinical disciplines, administration, and compliance to ensure agency-wide perspective in quality monitoring.

4.5 All committee decisions, directives, and action items shall be documented in formal meeting minutes with assigned responsible parties, deadlines, and follow-up requirements.

4.6 The QAPI Committee shall serve as the primary conduit for escalating quality and safety concerns to the Governing Body through the quarterly QAPI Performance Report prepared by the QAPI Coordinator.

4.7 Committee attendance shall be monitored. Members who miss 3 or more meetings within a 12-month period without documented cause shall be replaced.

4.8 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

QA-PI-001 — Performance Improvement Project Management

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines the requirements for selecting, designing, implementing, monitoring, and documenting Performance Improvement Projects (PIPs) at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. PIPs are the primary mechanism through which the agency translates quality data analysis into targeted, measurable improvement in specific areas of clinical care, operational performance, or patient safety. This policy ensures the agency satisfies 42 CFR § 484.65(c) and (d), which require the agency to conduct performance improvement activities focused on high-priority areas, implement and track PIPs proportionate to the agency's scope and complexity, and demonstrate measurable improvement over time.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

All QAPI Committee members

All PIP leads and team members

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Administrator

All department heads whose areas are the subject of a PIP

All staff participating in PIP data collection, intervention, or implementation activities

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a minimum of two (2) active PIPs at all times, proportionate to the scope and complexity of the agency's services, as required by 42 CFR § 484.65(d).

4.2 At least one active PIP shall address a clinical outcome or patient safety topic. The second PIP may address clinical, operational, compliance, or patient experience areas.

4.3 PIPs shall be selected based on data analysis identifying areas of underperformance, adverse trends, high-risk processes, or areas with the greatest potential for patient impact. PIP selection shall not be arbitrary.

4.4 Each PIP shall follow a structured quality improvement methodology (Plan-Do-Study-Act [PDSA], or equivalent evidence-based methodology approved by the QAPI Committee) and shall include: (a) a defined problem statement based on data; (b) measurable goals with numeric targets; (c) root cause analysis or contributing factor analysis; (d) specific, implementable interventions; (e) defined data collection plan; (f) monitoring schedule; (g) evaluation criteria; (h) sustainment plan.

4.5 Each PIP shall have a designated PIP Lead who is accountable for project execution, data collection, reporting, and achievement of measurable goals. The PIP Lead shall report progress to the QAPI Committee monthly.

4.6 PIP results shall be documented and reported to the Governing Body through the quarterly QAPI Performance Report. Completed PIPs shall include a final evaluation with demonstrated outcomes and sustainment plan.

4.7 PIPs that fail to demonstrate measurable progress within the defined evaluation timeframe shall be subject to reassessment by the QAPI Committee, including consideration of methodology revision, resource reallocation, or project redesign.

4.8 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

6. Procedures

6.2 PIP Design and Charter

6.3 PIP Implementation and Monitoring

QA-PI-002 — Quality Indicator Monitoring & Reporting

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the agency's quality indicator dashboard, monitoring frequency, data analysis methodology, performance thresholds, reporting requirements, and escalation triggers for adverse performance trends at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Quality indicators are the quantifiable measures through which the QAPI program tracks agency performance, identifies improvement opportunities, and evaluates the impact of interventions. This policy ensures compliance with 42 CFR § 484.65(b), which requires the agency to use quality indicator data, including measures derived from OASIS, to monitor the effectiveness of care and identify opportunities for improvement.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

All QAPI Committee members

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Administrator

All department heads and supervisors responsible for data collection or indicator performance

All clinical staff whose work generates indicator data

The Compliance Officer

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a defined set of quality indicators organized into a Quality Indicator Dashboard that is reviewed at each QAPI Committee meeting and reported to the Governing Body quarterly.

4.2 Quality indicators shall span the following domains at minimum: (a) clinical outcomes; (b) patient safety; (c) process compliance; (d) patient experience; (e) utilization and efficiency; (f) workforce competency.

4.3 Each quality indicator shall have a defined performance threshold. Thresholds shall be established using: (a) national benchmarks (CMS Home Health Compare, HHCAHPS national averages); (b) state comparative data; (c) agency historical performance; or (d) regulatory standards. Thresholds shall be reviewed and updated annually during QAPI plan development.

4.4 Any quality indicator that falls below its defined threshold for 2 consecutive reporting periods shall trigger mandatory corrective action analysis by the QAPI Committee, documented in committee minutes.

4.5 Any quality indicator that falls below its defined threshold for 3 consecutive reporting periods without documented improvement shall be escalated to the Governing Body per QA-PG-001 Section 6.5.

4.6 Quality indicator data shall be trended over time (minimum 12-month rolling trend) to identify patterns, seasonal variations, and the impact of improvement interventions.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Quality Indicator Selection and Dashboard Design

6.2 Data Collection and Analysis

6.3 Reporting

6.4 Corrective Action Triggers

6.5 Escalation

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

QA-PI-003 — Clinical Outcome Benchmarking

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy requires Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. to systematically compare its clinical outcomes against national benchmarks, CMS quality measures, and state comparative data, and to document a structured response to identified underperformance. External benchmarking provides the objective context necessary to evaluate whether agency performance reflects acceptable quality of care, regardless of internal trend direction. This policy supports the QAPI program's data-driven mandate under 42 CFR § 484.65(b) and (c) by ensuring the agency does not operate in isolation from industry performance standards.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

All QAPI Committee members

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Administrator

All clinical supervisors responsible for outcome-driving care areas

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall compare its clinical outcomes against national and state benchmarks at least quarterly, using data from CMS Home Health Compare, CASPER/iQIES reports, HHCAHPS, and other recognized comparative data sources.

4.2 Benchmarking shall encompass, at minimum: (a) CMS-publicly reported quality measures; (b) patient outcome measures derived from OASIS; (c) patient experience measures from HHCAHPS; (d) Star Ratings and Home Health Compare composite scores.

4.3 When agency performance falls below national benchmarks on any publicly reported measure, the QAPI Committee shall conduct a documented analysis and develop a response plan within 30 calendar days.

4.4 Benchmarking results shall be reported to the Governing Body quarterly as part of the QAPI Performance Report.

4.5 Benchmark targets shall be incorporated into the annual QAPI plan per QA-PG-002.

4.6 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

QA-PI-004 — Data-Driven Decision Making

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy requires that all quality improvement initiatives, operational changes, and resource allocation decisions at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. be supported by documented data analysis rather than anecdotal observation, assumption, or convenience. Data-driven decision making is the foundational principle of the QAPI program and ensures that the agency's limited resources are directed toward interventions with the greatest evidence of impact. This policy operationalizes 42 CFR § 484.65(b), which requires the use of quality indicator data to monitor and improve care effectiveness.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Governing Body

The Administrator

The QAPI Coordinator and QAPI Committee

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

All department heads and supervisors who propose or approve operational, clinical, or quality improvement changes

The Compliance Officer

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All quality improvement decisions — including PIP selection, corrective action development, policy modifications based on quality concerns, resource reallocation, process changes, and staff education priorities — shall be supported by documented data analysis.

4.2 Decisions presented to the QAPI Committee or Governing Body for approval must include: (a) the data source(s); (b) the analysis performed; (c) the findings; (d) the recommended action with rationale linked to findings.

4.3 Anecdotal observations and individual experiences are valued as input for generating hypotheses and identifying potential areas of concern. However, they shall not serve as the sole basis for resource allocation, process changes, or corrective actions without supporting data analysis.

4.4 The agency shall maintain data literacy among all QAPI Committee members and department heads through training on data interpretation, basic statistical concepts, and evidence-based decision-making practices.

4.5 Data integrity is a prerequisite for data-driven decisions. The agency shall ensure data accuracy, completeness, and timeliness through defined quality controls per CO-DC-001 and CL-OA-005.

4.6 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Decision Criteria and Documentation Requirements

6.2 Data Analysis Standards

6.3 Data Literacy and Training

6.4 Escalation

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

Surveyors will: (1) ask how the agency uses data to drive quality improvement; (2) review QAPI Committee minutes for evidence that data analysis precedes decisions; (3) look for documented data analysis in PIP charters and corrective action plans; (4) assess whether decisions are data-driven or anecdote-driven.

8.3 Common Failure Points

QA-PI-005 — Staff Competency Integration with QAPI

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy links staff competency evaluation results to the QAPI program at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. to ensure that individual and aggregate competency data are systematically used to identify training needs, inform performance improvement priorities, and drive system-level improvements. Competency gaps that remain unaddressed become quality gaps. This policy ensures that clinical competency is not evaluated in isolation (within HR) but is actively integrated into the agency's quality monitoring and improvement framework, consistent with 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program scope and data use) and 42 CFR § 484.80 (home health aide competency requirements).

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The HR Director

All QAPI Committee members

All department heads and clinical supervisors responsible for competency evaluation

All clinical staff subject to competency evaluation (RNs, LVNs, therapists, MSWs, HHAs)

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Staff competency evaluation results shall be reported to the QAPI Committee at least quarterly as a standing data input to the QAPI program.

4.2 The QAPI Coordinator and the Director of Nursing / HR Director shall collaborate to identify competency patterns — both strengths and deficiencies — that have implications for patient care quality, safety, and outcomes.

4.3 When competency evaluation data reveals a systemic pattern (defined as the same competency deficiency identified in 3 or more staff members within a 12-month period, or a single deficiency that correlates with an adverse event), the QAPI Committee shall determine whether a PIP, targeted education, process redesign, or other system-level intervention is warranted.

4.4 Competency evaluation focus areas shall be informed by QAPI data, including adverse event types, quality indicators below threshold, PIP focus areas, and CMS survey findings. The QAPI Coordinator shall provide input to the DON/HR annually on recommended competency evaluation focus areas for the upcoming year.

4.5 Individual competency deficiencies shall be addressed through the performance management and remediation process per HR-TD-003 and HR-ER-001. This policy governs only the aggregate analysis and system-level response within the QAPI framework.

4.6 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

QA-PI-006 — Visit Utilization & LUPA Risk Management Program

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes a cross-functional QAPI program integrating clinical, scheduling, and financial data to monitor visit utilization patterns, identify Low Utilization Payment Adjustment (LUPA) risk episodes early, and implement coordinated interventions to ensure physician-ordered services are delivered as planned at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. LUPA episodes — those where the number of visits delivered falls below the CMS-defined threshold — represent both a clinical risk (patients not receiving ordered care) and a financial risk (reduced reimbursement). This policy ensures that visit utilization is managed as a quality of care issue, not merely a billing concern, consistent with 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program scope), 42 CFR § 484.60 (care planning and coordination), and 42 CFR § 484.55 (comprehensive assessment).

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Administrator

The CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

All QAPI Committee members

All scheduling and intake staff

All clinical staff responsible for visit delivery (RNs, LVNs, therapists, MSWs, HHAs)

All clinical supervisors

Exclusion: This policy governs the QAPI monitoring and intervention framework for visit utilization. Individual billing procedures for LUPA episodes are governed by FN-BC-001 and FN-CM-005. Clinical visit frequency determination is governed by CL-CP-001 and CL-SD-025.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a structured, data-driven visit utilization monitoring program integrated within the QAPI framework that identifies episodes at risk of LUPA and coordinates clinical, scheduling, and financial interventions to ensure ordered services are delivered.

4.2 Visit utilization monitoring shall be treated as a patient care quality issue. Failure to deliver physician-ordered visits is a care delivery deficiency that affects clinical outcomes, not merely a revenue concern.

4.3 The agency shall maintain a real-time or near-real-time LUPA risk dashboard that identifies episodes approaching the LUPA visit threshold, enabling proactive intervention before the episode closes.

4.4 A cross-functional LUPA Prevention Team — comprising clinical, scheduling, and revenue cycle representatives — shall be designated to review LUPA risk episodes weekly and coordinate interventions.

4.5 All LUPA episodes that close shall be subject to a retrospective root cause analysis to determine whether the LUPA resulted from: (a) a clinically appropriate low-utilization case; (b) a scheduling failure; (c) a patient-driven factor (refusal, hospitalization, no-show); (d) a clinician-driven factor (missed visits, documentation gaps); or (e) a system failure (staffing shortage, communication breakdown).

4.6 LUPA rate shall be a standing quality indicator on the QAPI dashboard per QA-PI-002 with a defined performance threshold, and shall be reported to the Governing Body quarterly.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 LUPA Risk Monitoring System

6.2 LUPA Prevention Team Structure and Function

6.3 Proactive Intervention for At-Risk Episodes

6.4 Retrospective LUPA Root Cause Analysis

6.5 QAPI Committee and Governing Body Reporting

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors evaluating care coordination and quality will verify: (1) the agency monitors whether ordered visits are delivered; (2) missed visits are documented with reasons; (3) the agency has a process for ensuring patients receive planned care; (4) patterns of under-delivery are identified and addressed through the QAPI program; (5) LUPA management is framed as a quality issue, not solely a billing concern.

8.3 Common Failure Points

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All LUPA Prevention Team members shall receive orientation to this policy, the LUPA Risk Dashboard, root cause classification methodology, and intervention protocols within 14 calendar days of appointment. Orientation shall be conducted by the QAPI Coordinator or CFO designee.

10.2 All clinical staff (RNs, LVNs, therapists, MSWs, HHAs) shall receive training during annual mandatory training (per HR-TD-001) on: (a) the relationship between visit delivery and patient outcomes; (b) their responsibility to deliver ordered visits and document barriers; (c) the prohibition against non-clinically-justified visit front-loading; (d) how to report scheduling conflicts or barriers to the scheduling coordinator.

10.3 All scheduling and intake staff shall receive training on LUPA risk identification, dashboard alert response procedures, and their role in proactive rescheduling within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter.

10.4 All personnel within scope of this policy shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new assignment.

10.5 The QAPI Coordinator shall maintain a training tracking log documenting all LUPA-related training including attendee name, topic, date, trainer, and completion status.

QA-PI-007 — Staff Competency Impact on Patient Outcomes

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy requires Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. to establish a measurable linkage between staff competency evaluation results and patient outcome data. While QA-PI-005 establishes the integration of competency data into the QAPI program for pattern identification and system-level response, this policy goes further by mandating specific metrics that demonstrate training effectiveness, quantify the relationship between competency performance and clinical outcomes, and trigger targeted education and performance improvement initiatives when gaps are identified. This policy ensures the agency can demonstrate to CMS surveyors that its competency program does not merely "check the box" but actively drives measurable quality improvement, consistent with 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI data-driven improvement) and 42 CFR § 484.80 (home health aide training and competency).

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The HR Director

All QAPI Committee members

All clinical supervisors responsible for competency evaluation and outcome monitoring

All clinical staff subject to competency evaluation (RNs, LVNs, therapists, MSWs, HHAs)

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain defined metrics that link staff competency evaluation performance to patient outcome data, enabling the agency to demonstrate that its training and competency programs produce measurable quality improvement.

4.2 The agency shall track at least three (3) Competency-Outcome Linkage Metrics annually, each pairing a competency evaluation area with a corresponding patient outcome indicator.

4.3 When competency-outcome linkage analysis reveals a statistically or clinically meaningful correlation between a competency gap and an adverse outcome trend, the QAPI Committee shall initiate a targeted intervention within 30 calendar days.

4.4 Training effectiveness shall be measured not only by competency evaluation pass rates but by subsequent improvement in the correlated patient outcome indicator following education or remediation.

4.5 Competency-outcome linkage data shall be reported to the Governing Body annually as part of the year-end QAPI evaluation per QA-PG-002.

4.6 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

QA-AE-001 — Adverse Event Identification & Reporting

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines what constitutes an adverse event, near-miss, and sentinel event at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., establishes mandatory reporting requirements, defines investigation expectations, and ensures that adverse event data is systematically captured, analyzed, and used to drive quality improvement through the QAPI program. Adverse event identification and reporting is the foundation of patient safety. This policy ensures the agency satisfies the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program data use and patient safety), 42 CFR § 484.60 (quality of care), and applicable California state mandatory reporting requirements.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All agency staff — clinical, administrative, contracted, and per diem

All QAPI Committee members

The QAPI Coordinator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Administrator

The Compliance Officer

The Risk Manager

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a non-punitive adverse event reporting culture that encourages all staff to report adverse events, near-misses, and safety concerns without fear of retaliation.

4.2 All adverse events, near-misses, and sentinel events occurring during or related to agency services shall be reported, documented, and investigated per the procedures in this policy.

4.3 Adverse event reporting is mandatory for all agency staff. Failure to report a known adverse event is a violation of this policy and may result in disciplinary action per HR-ER-002.

4.4 Adverse event data shall be a standing data input to the QAPI program. The QAPI Committee shall review adverse event trends monthly and the Governing Body shall receive a summary quarterly.

4.5 Sentinel events shall be reported to the Governing Body within 72 hours and shall trigger a mandatory root cause analysis per QA-AE-002.

4.6 The agency shall comply with all applicable California state mandatory reporting requirements for adverse events.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

QA-AE-002 — Root Cause Analysis Process

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the methodology, team composition, documentation requirements, and completion standards for conducting Root Cause Analyses (RCAs) at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. An RCA is a structured, retrospective investigative process used to identify the fundamental systemic cause(s) of adverse events, sentinel events, or persistent quality failures — moving beyond the immediate or apparent cause to uncover the underlying process, system, or organizational factors that allowed the event to occur. RCA is mandatory for all Level 4 (Serious Harm) and Level 5 (Sentinel Event) adverse events per QA-AE-001, and may be directed by the QAPI Committee for any event or pattern deemed significant. This policy supports compliance with 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program effectiveness and data use) and 42 CFR § 484.60 (quality of care).

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

All individuals appointed to RCA teams

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Administrator

The Risk Manager

The Compliance Officer

All QAPI Committee members

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall conduct a formal Root Cause Analysis for all Level 4 (Serious Harm) and Level 5 (Sentinel Event) adverse events as classified per QA-AE-001.

4.2 The QAPI Committee may direct an RCA for any event, pattern, or systemic failure it determines warrants formal root cause investigation, regardless of severity classification.

4.3 RCAs shall be conducted by a multidisciplinary team using a structured methodology that focuses on systems and processes, not individual blame.

4.4 Each RCA must produce identified root cause(s), contributing factors, and a Corrective Action Plan (per QA-AE-003) with measurable outcomes and defined accountability.

4.5 RCAs shall be completed within 45 calendar days of event identification. For sentinel events, the preliminary findings must be available to the Governing Body within 14 calendar days.

4.6 RCA findings and corrective actions shall be tracked to completion and monitored for effectiveness through the QAPI program.

4.7 RCA documents are quality improvement records and shall be maintained confidentially per applicable state peer review protections and agency policy.

4.8 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 RCA Trigger and Initiation

6.2 RCA Investigation Methodology

6.3 RCA Report

6.4 Corrective Action Development and Tracking

6.5 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

Surveyors will: (1) request documentation of RCAs conducted during the survey look-back period; (2) verify RCAs use structured methodology, not informal review; (3) verify RCAs identify systemic causes, not just individual blame; (4) verify RCAs lead to corrective action plans with measurable outcomes; (5) verify the Governing Body is informed of sentinel events and RCA findings; (6) assess whether corrective actions were effective in preventing recurrence.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 Cross-Referenced Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All individuals who may serve as RCA Leads or RCA Team members shall receive formal training in RCA methodology within 30 calendar days of their first assignment. Training must cover: (a) RCA purpose and principles; (b) 5 Whys technique; (c) Fishbone diagram construction; (d) interview techniques; (e) distinguishing root causes from contributing factors; (f) writing root causes in system terms; (g) developing measurable corrective recommendations.

10.2 The QAPI Coordinator shall maintain a roster of trained RCA facilitators and ensure at least 3 agency staff are trained at all times.

10.3 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form within 14 calendar days.

11. Version Control

Per standard enterprise version control (EN-LC-001).

QA-AE-003 — Corrective Action Plan Development & Tracking

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy defines the requirements for developing, implementing, tracking, verifying effectiveness, and closing Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A CAP is the structured, documented response to identified deficiencies — whether arising from adverse events, root cause analyses, quality indicator thresholds, CMS survey findings, compliance audits, or QAPI Committee directives. This policy ensures that identified problems are addressed with specific, measurable, accountable, and time-bound corrective actions, and that the agency can demonstrate to CMS surveyors and the Governing Body that quality improvement is sustained. This policy supports compliance with 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program improvement activities) and 42 CFR § 484.100 (compliance with federal, state, and local laws).

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

All individuals assigned as CAP Leads or responsible parties

All QAPI Committee members

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Administrator

The Compliance Officer

The Risk Manager

All department heads whose areas are subject to a CAP

4. Policy Statements

4.1 A Corrective Action Plan shall be developed for every: (a) Root Cause Analysis completed per QA-AE-002; (b) quality indicator below threshold for 2 consecutive periods with QAPI Committee directive; (c) CMS survey finding requiring a Plan of Correction; (d) compliance audit finding classified as high-risk; (e) Governing Body directive for corrective action; (f) any other deficiency the QAPI Committee determines warrants formal corrective action.

4.2 Each CAP must include: (a) a clear problem statement; (b) the identified root cause or contributing factors; (c) specific corrective actions; (d) responsible party for each action; (e) measurable outcome targets; (f) implementation timeline; (g) monitoring plan; (h) effectiveness verification criteria.

4.3 CAPs shall be tracked centrally by the QAPI Coordinator through the QAPI Corrective Action Tracker and reported to the QAPI Committee monthly and to the Governing Body quarterly.

4.4 No CAP shall be closed until effectiveness has been verified through documented evidence that the corrective action achieved the intended outcome and the deficiency has not recurred for a minimum of 3 consecutive monitoring periods.

4.5 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 CAP Initiation

6.2 CAP Development

6.3 CAP Implementation

6.4 Monitoring and Effectiveness Verification

6.5 CMS Survey Plan of Correction

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

Surveyors will: (1) request documentation of all corrective action plans during the survey look-back period; (2) verify each CAP has specific, measurable corrective actions with responsible parties and deadlines; (3) verify CAPs were actually implemented, not just documented; (4) verify effectiveness was measured; (5) verify the Governing Body was informed and involved when appropriate; (6) for repeat survey findings, determine whether prior CAPs were effective.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 Cross-Referenced Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All individuals assigned as CAP Leads shall receive training on CAP development methodology, measurable outcome writing, monitoring plan design, and effectiveness verification within 14 calendar days of first assignment.

10.2 All QAPI Committee members shall receive annual training on CAP review, approval criteria, and closure evaluation.

10.3 Policy acknowledgment within 14 calendar days per standard.

QA-AE-004 — Patient Safety Program

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes a formal, agency-wide Patient Safety Program at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., integrated with the QAPI framework, to proactively identify, assess, and mitigate risks to patient safety across all service delivery processes. A patient safety program moves beyond reactive adverse event management to include proactive hazard identification, safety culture promotion, and system-level risk mitigation. This policy ensures compliance with 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program including patient safety), 42 CFR § 484.60 (quality of care), and 42 CFR § 484.70 (infection prevention and control as a safety concern).

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

All agency staff — clinical, administrative, contracted, and per diem

All QAPI Committee members

The QAPI Coordinator (Patient Safety Program Lead)

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Administrator

The Risk Manager

The Compliance Officer

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a formal Patient Safety Program that is integrated within the QAPI program and led by the QAPI Coordinator (or a designated Patient Safety Officer).

4.2 The Patient Safety Program shall include both proactive and reactive components: (a) Proactive — hazard identification, safety risk assessments, safety culture monitoring, and preventive interventions; (b) Reactive — adverse event identification, investigation, corrective action, and trending per QA-AE-001 through QA-AE-003.

4.3 The Patient Safety Program shall maintain standing focus areas that include at minimum: (a) fall prevention; (b) medication safety; (c) infection prevention; (d) communication safety (transitions, handoffs, orders); (e) environmental safety in the patient home.

4.4 A culture of safety shall be promoted through non-punitive reporting, staff empowerment to report concerns, leadership engagement, and visible organizational commitment to patient safety.

4.5 Patient safety data shall be a standing item on the QAPI Committee agenda and included in the quarterly QAPI Performance Report to the Governing Body.

4.6 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Patient Safety Program Structure

6.2 Standing Patient Safety Focus Areas

6.3 Proactive Safety Assessments

6.4 Safety Culture Promotion

6.5 Integration with QAPI and Governing Body Reporting

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

Surveyors will: (1) ask the agency to describe its patient safety program; (2) look for evidence of proactive safety activities, not just reactive event management; (3) verify safety is integrated with QAPI; (4) assess whether a non-punitive reporting culture exists; (5) verify the Governing Body is informed of patient safety data; (6) look for evidence that safety concerns lead to measurable improvement.

8.3 Common Failure Points

QA-SM-001 — Utilization Review & Management

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes a structured, data-driven Utilization Review (UR) program at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. that monitors the appropriateness, efficiency, and clinical necessity of all home health services delivered to patients. The UR program ensures that services are ordered and delivered based on documented clinical need, that visit frequency and duration align with patient goals and physician orders, and that patterns of over-utilization or under-utilization are identified and corrected. This policy satisfies the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI — utilization data as a quality input), 42 CFR § 484.60 (care planning and quality of care), and 42 CFR § 484.55 (comprehensive assessment of patients), while also addressing the financial integrity requirements implicit in CMS payment integrity programs. Utilization review is treated as a quality of care program, not solely a cost-containment function.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Administrator

The CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

All QAPI Committee members

All clinical supervisors responsible for caseload oversight

All scheduling and intake staff

All clinical staff (RNs, LVNs, therapists, MSWs, HHAs) providing billable services

The Compliance Officer

Exclusion: Individual billing procedures for specific payers are governed by FN-BC-001. LUPA-specific monitoring procedures are governed by QA-PI-006 and FN-CM-005. This policy governs the overarching UR program framework.

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a formal, agency-wide Utilization Review program that monitors the appropriateness, frequency, duration, and clinical justification of all home health services at the episode, discipline, visit, and clinician level.

4.2 The UR program shall be integrated within the QAPI framework and shall serve as a standing data input to the QAPI Quality Indicator Dashboard per QA-PI-002.

4.3 All services delivered by the agency must be: (a) ordered by a licensed physician or allowed practitioner; (b) supported by documented clinical need in the patient's clinical record; (c) consistent with the patient's plan of care; (d) reasonable and necessary as defined by CMS coverage criteria.

4.4 The UR program shall identify and trigger review for both over-utilization (visits in excess of ordered or clinically justified frequency) and under-utilization (failure to deliver ordered visits), recognizing both as quality of care deficiencies.

4.5 A designated Utilization Review Committee (or function integrated within the QAPI Committee) shall conduct structured reviews at defined intervals and report findings to the QAPI Committee and Governing Body.

4.6 Utilization data shall be used to identify patterns by clinician, discipline, diagnosis group, referral source, and payer that may indicate quality concerns, training needs, or compliance risks.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 UR Program Structure

6.2 Prospective Utilization Review (Pre-Admission and Start of Care)

6.3 Concurrent Utilization Review (During Active Episodes)

6.4 Retrospective Utilization Review (Post-Episode Analysis)

6.5 Clinician-Level Utilization Profiling

6.6 QAPI Committee and Governing Body Reporting

6.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors evaluating care planning, quality, and payment integrity will verify: (1) the agency has a process for monitoring whether services are appropriate and medically necessary; (2) visit delivery matches physician orders; (3) over-utilization patterns are identified and addressed; (4) the UR process is integrated with QAPI; (5) the Governing Body is informed of utilization trends; (6) documentation supports all billed services.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

9.1 Federal Regulations

9.2 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All clinical supervisors and the DON shall receive training on utilization review methodology, case-level review standards, and documentation of medical necessity within 14 calendar days of assignment. Training must cover: (a) UR criteria and outlier thresholds; (b) how to conduct a case-level review; (c) medical necessity documentation standards; (d) escalation pathways.

10.2 All clinical staff (RNs, LVNs, therapists, MSWs) shall receive training during initial orientation and annually on: (a) medical necessity documentation requirements; (b) visit frequency compliance; (c) how utilization monitoring protects patients and the agency.

10.3 The QAPI Coordinator and CFO shall receive training on utilization data analysis and report generation within 30 calendar days of policy effective date.

10.4 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix F) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new assignment.

10.5 The QAPI Coordinator shall maintain a training tracking log documenting all UR-related training.

11. Version Control

11.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

11.2 Only the most current approved version, as reflected in the policy header, is valid. Superseded versions must be archived and marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

11.3 Substantive revisions require Governing Body approval, re-acknowledgment within 14 calendar days, and update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

11.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body.

QA-SM-002 — Infection Surveillance & Trending

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the agency's infection surveillance program at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. as a formal, data-driven component of the QAPI framework and the infection prevention and control program (CL-SD-016). Infection surveillance is the systematic collection, analysis, trending, and reporting of data on infectious diseases and infection-related events among patients receiving home health services and among agency staff, enabling the agency to identify patterns, investigate clusters, implement targeted interventions, and demonstrate continuous improvement in infection prevention outcomes. This policy satisfies the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.70 (Condition of Participation: Infection Prevention and Control), which requires an ongoing infection surveillance program, and 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program), which requires infection data as a standing QAPI input.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

The Infection Prevention and Control Designee (as designated per CL-SD-016)

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

All clinical staff (RNs, LVNs, therapists, MSWs, HHAs)

All QAPI Committee members

The Administrator

The Compliance Officer

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a formal, ongoing infection surveillance program that systematically collects, analyzes, and trends infection data for both patient infections and staff occupational exposures.

4.2 The infection surveillance program shall be integrated within the QAPI framework and shall serve as a standing data input to both the QAPI Quality Indicator Dashboard (QA-PI-002) and the monthly QAPI Committee agenda (QA-PG-003).

4.3 All clinical staff are responsible for identifying and reporting suspected or confirmed infections in patients and in themselves to the Infection Prevention and Control Designee and/or the Director of Nursing within 24 hours of identification.

4.4 Infection data shall be trended over time (minimum 12-month rolling trend) by infection type, patient population characteristics, geographic area, and clinician, to identify patterns and clusters requiring investigation.

4.5 When an infection cluster (defined in Section 5) is identified, the QAPI Committee shall conduct a documented investigation within 14 calendar days and implement a corrective action plan per QA-AE-003.

4.6 The infection surveillance program shall include monitoring of: (a) patient infections acquired during the episode of care; (b) staff occupational exposures and work-related infections; (c) process compliance indicators (hand hygiene, PPE use, wound care technique); (d) antibiotic use patterns (where data is available); (e) hospitalizations related to infection.

4.7 Infection surveillance findings and trends shall be reported to the Governing Body quarterly as part of the QAPI Performance Report.

4.8 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors evaluating 42 CFR § 484.70 compliance will verify: (1) an ongoing infection surveillance program exists with documented data collection; (2) infection data is trended over time with comparison to thresholds; (3) the agency acts when infection rates are elevated; (4) clusters are investigated with documented findings and corrective actions; (5) infection prevention process compliance is monitored; (6) the QAPI Committee reviews infection data; (7) the Governing Body is informed of infection trends.

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All clinical staff shall receive infection surveillance training during initial orientation per HR-TA-005, covering: (a) how to identify and report a patient infection; (b) the Patient Infection Report Form and submission process; (c) the 24-hour reporting requirement; (d) how to report an occupational exposure; (e) the non-punitive reporting culture for infection reporting.

10.2 Annual refresher training on infection surveillance shall be included in mandatory annual training per HR-TD-001.

10.3 The IPC Designee shall receive specific training on infection surveillance methodology, cluster identification, rate calculation, and CDPH reporting requirements within 30 days of designation and annually thereafter.

10.4 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix F) within 14 calendar days.

10.5 The QAPI Coordinator shall maintain a training tracking log for all infection surveillance training.

QA-SM-003 — Patient Satisfaction Survey & Analysis

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes the agency's patient satisfaction survey and analysis program at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., integrating the federally mandated Home Health Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (HHCAHPS) survey with any supplemental satisfaction monitoring the agency conducts. Patient experience data reflects the patient's perspective on care quality and is a critical, non-clinical dimension of quality that complements clinical outcome monitoring. This policy ensures that HHCAHPS and supplemental data are systematically collected, analyzed, trended, and used to drive improvements in patient experience, communication, care delivery, and agency reputation. This policy satisfies the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program — patient experience data as a quality input) and CMS HHCAHPS program requirements.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

The Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

All QAPI Committee members

All clinical staff whose conduct and communication affect patient experience

The CFO / Revenue Cycle Director (for Star Rating implications)

The Compliance Officer

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall comply with all CMS HHCAHPS program requirements including patient eligibility criteria, vendor contracting standards, and data submission timelines.

4.2 HHCAHPS results — including all reported measures, composite scores, and Star Ratings — shall be systematically monitored, trended, and reported through the QAPI program.

4.3 The agency shall supplement HHCAHPS data with agency-administered satisfaction monitoring (e.g., discharge satisfaction calls, post-discharge surveys) to obtain more timely, actionable feedback than the HHCAHPS quarterly release cycle provides.

4.4 Patient satisfaction data shall be a standing item on the monthly QAPI Committee agenda and shall be reported to the Governing Body quarterly.

4.5 When any HHCAHPS composite measure falls below the national average for 2 consecutive quarters, the QAPI Committee shall direct a documented root cause analysis and corrective action plan per QA-AE-003.

4.6 Patient satisfaction data shall be used to identify staff education needs, communication improvement opportunities, and service delivery changes.

4.7 All patient satisfaction data collection, storage, and analysis shall comply with HIPAA privacy and security requirements per CO-HP-001 and CO-HP-002.

4.8 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 HHCAHPS Program Compliance

6.2 HHCAHPS Data Analysis

6.3 Supplemental Patient Satisfaction Monitoring

6.4 Corrective Action for Below-Benchmark Performance

6.5 Governing Body Reporting

6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

Surveyors will: (1) ask whether the agency participates in HHCAHPS; (2) verify an approved vendor is contracted; (3) verify HHCAHPS data is analyzed and used to drive improvement; (4) assess whether below-average scores have documented corrective action; (5) verify the Governing Body is informed; (6) look for evidence that patient experience data is integrated with QAPI.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

References: CMS HHCAHPS program requirements; 42 CFR § 484.65; cross-references QA-PG-001, QA-PG-002, QA-PI-001, QA-PI-002, QA-PI-003, QA-AE-003, QA-SM-004, CO-HP-001, CO-HP-002, GV-GB-001, EN-TG-001.

10. Training Requirements

10.1 All clinical staff shall receive training on patient experience and communication skills during orientation and annually, including HHCAHPS survey domains most affected by clinician behavior (care of patients, communication, responsiveness).

10.2 Staff conducting post-discharge calls shall receive training on the standardized call script, active listening, complaint escalation, and documentation standards within 7 calendar days of assignment.

10.3 Policy acknowledgment within 14 calendar days per standard.
